cards.title: Describe a person you only met once recently and want to know more about
points: why you want to know more about him/her
and explain how you feel about him/her
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: người trong bài (tên Minh, giảng viên/diễn giả ở một buổi IT meetup tại Hà Nội) là nhân vật mình tự tạo để khớp hồ sơ IT Tester của bạn. Khi luyện, bạn thay bằng người thật mà bạn từng gặp một lần (đồng nghiệp công ty khác, người ngồi cạnh trên xe buýt, thầy/cô ở một buổi học...). Nếu không có ai, hãy "mượn" một người có thật mà bạn biết.

notes.v: Minh – senior test engineer – talk on automation testing
last month – IT meetup, Hanoi – 10 mins at coffee break
experienced in my field – how he built career – tips on tools
admire – inspired – hope to meet again

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a man I met last month at an IT meetup in Hanoi. His name is Minh, and he's a senior test engineer at a big software company.

I met him only once. He gave a talk about automation testing, and after the talk we chatted for about ten minutes during the coffee break. He was friendly, and he answered all my questions.

I want to know more about him for two reasons. First, he has a lot of experience in my field, and I'd like to learn how he built his career. Second, he gave me some useful tips about learning automation tools, but we didn't have enough time to talk more.

I feel respect and also a little inspired. He's a normal person, but he's very professional. I hope I can meet him again at the next meetup and ask him to share more advice with me.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a man called Minh, who I met just once, at an IT meetup in Hanoi last month. He's a senior test engineer at a large software company, and he gave a talk on automation testing.

We only spoke for about ten minutes during the coffee break, but he left a strong impression on me. He was approachable and patient, and he answered all my questions as if we'd known each other for years.

The reason I'd love to get to know him better is that he's exactly where I'd like to be in a few years' time. He mentioned a few tips on picking up automation tools, but the break ended before I could ask how he'd built his career. I've been wondering about that ever since.

As for how I feel about him, I genuinely admire him. He's clearly highly skilled, yet he was really down-to-earth. Meeting him gave me a push to take my own career more seriously, so I'm hoping to bump into him at the next meetup and ask for some advice.

p3.q: What can we do to leave a good impression on people we meet for the first time?
p3.vi: Chúng ta có thể làm gì để để lại ấn tượng tốt với người mới gặp lần đầu?
p3.a6: I think the most important thing is to be polite and smile. We should also dress neatly and listen carefully when the other person talks. For example, when I met Minh, I was a bit nervous, but I smiled and asked him some questions about his talk, and he seemed happy to talk to me.
p3.a7: First and foremost, a warm smile and a polite greeting go a long way. It also helps to show genuine interest by listening carefully and asking relevant questions, rather than just talking about yourself. Dressing neatly matters too, since appearance is the first thing people notice. In my case, I simply asked Minh a few questions about his talk, and that was enough to start a good conversation.

vocab.m: thể hiện sự quan tâm thật
điều đầu tiên người ta thấy

p3.grammar: *rather than + V-ing* → "listening **rather than just talking**." / *It helps to + V.*

p3.q: What should we not talk about when we meet a person for the first time?
p3.vi: Khi gặp ai lần đầu, chúng ta không nên nói về điều gì?
p3.a6: We shouldn't ask about personal things like salary, age or marriage, because these questions can make people uncomfortable. Also, we shouldn't talk about politics or religion because people have different opinions.
p3.a7: I'd steer clear of anything too personal, such as salary, age or relationship status, since it can make the other person feel uncomfortable. In Vietnam, people sometimes ask these questions quite casually, but they can come across as rude to others. Sensitive topics like politics and religion are also best avoided, as they can easily lead to an argument. With Minh, I kept to safe topics like work and technology.

vocab.m: chỉ nói chủ đề an toàn

p3.grammar: *best + V3 (bị động rút gọn)* → "are also **best avoided**."

p3.q: How do people make friends in your country?
p3.vi: Người ở nước bạn kết bạn bằng cách nào?
p3.a6: Most people make friends at school, at university or at work. Nowadays, many people also meet friends through social media like Facebook, or through hobby groups. Some people also make friends through their friends.
p3.a7: Traditionally, people make friends through school, university and work, because they spend so much time with the same group of people. Nowadays, though, social media and interest-based groups play a big part, such as running clubs or, in my case, IT meetups. Introductions through mutual friends are also very common.

vocab.u: Cấu trúc so sánh quá khứ – hiện tại

p3.grammar: *because + mệnh đề* → "...because they spend so much time together."

p3.q: On what occasions do people like to make friends?
p3.vi: Mọi người thích kết bạn vào những dịp nào?
p3.a6: People usually make friends at parties, at events like weddings, or when they join a club or a course. Also, when they start a new job or move to a new place, they want to make new friends.
p3.a7: Typically at social gatherings like birthday parties and weddings, or at events such as workshops and meetups, where everyone shares a common interest. People who have just started a new job or moved to a new area are also keen to widen their social circle.
p3.grammar: *Mệnh đề quan hệ "who" + present perfect* → "People **who have just started** a new job..."

p3.q: Is it important to have the same hobbies and interests when making friends?
p3.vi: Có cần có cùng sở thích khi kết bạn không?
p3.a6: I think it's helpful, but not necessary. Having the same hobbies gives you something to talk about, so it's easier to start a friendship. But a true friendship also depends on trust and respect. Some of my close friends have different hobbies from me.
p3.a7: It certainly helps, since shared interests give you plenty to talk about and make it easier to spend time together. That said, I wouldn't say it's essential. What keeps a friendship going in the long run is trust and mutual respect. Some of my closest friends are into totally different things, and we still get along really well.
p3.grammar: *"What + V + is + N"* (câu nhấn mạnh) → "**What keeps** a friendship going **is** trust."

p3.q: What qualities make true friends?
p3.vi: Những phẩm chất nào tạo nên người bạn thật sự?
p3.a6: I think a true friend should be honest, loyal and supportive. They should tell you the truth and help you when you have problems. They should also be trustworthy, so you can share your secrets with them.
p3.a7: For me, honesty and loyalty come first. A true friend tells you the truth even when it's uncomfortable, and sticks by you through hard times, not just the good ones. Being a good listener matters as well, because you need someone you can open up to. People like Minh, who are generous with their time, are the kind of people I'd love to have around.

vocab.m: cởi mở, tâm sự với ai

p3.grammar: *Mệnh đề quan hệ có dấu phẩy* → "People like Minh**, who** are generous with their time**,** are..."

cards.title: Describe a gift you would like to buy for your friend
points: how long you have known him/her
how you would choose a gift for him/her
and explain why you would choose that gift for him/her
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: người bạn tên Hùng (bạn đại học, nay là lập trình viên), món quà là bàn phím cơ. Bạn thay bằng bạn thật và món quà thật. Part 3 dùng lại ý của Part 2 (Hùng, bàn phím) làm ví dụ.

notes.v: Hung – university classmate – now developer
about 8 years
think what he needs – reviews – ask friend – budget
types all day – old keyboard broken – loves tech – thoughtful

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a gift I want to buy for my friend, Hung. I met him at university, so I've known him for about eight years. We were in the same class, and now he works as a software developer.

His birthday is coming next month, and I'd like to buy him a mechanical keyboard. To choose a good one, I'll first think about what he needs. Then I'll read some reviews online and ask a friend who knows a lot about keyboards. I'll also check the price, because I don't want it to be too expensive.

I would choose this gift for two reasons. First, Hung types all day at work, and his old keyboard is broken, so he really needs a new one. Second, he loves technology, so I think he will enjoy it. I hope he will be happy and know that I care about him.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a gift I'm planning to buy for my friend Hung. We met at university, so we've known each other for about eight years now. We were in the same class, and he's now working as a software developer.

His birthday is coming up next month, and I've got my eye on a mechanical keyboard for him. To pick the right one, I'll start by thinking about what he actually needs, then read a few reviews and ask a friend who's into keyboards for advice. I'll also keep an eye on the budget, since I don't want him to feel he has to buy me something equally expensive in return.

There are two reasons behind my choice. For one thing, he spends most of his day typing, and his current keyboard is falling apart. For another, he's a real tech enthusiast, so I'm sure he'd appreciate something he can use every day. I'd like the gift to be practical, but also to show that I put some thought into it.

vocab.u: *I've got my eye on a new watch.*

vocab.p: keep an eye on the budget

vocab.u: Dùng để liệt kê 2 lý do

grammar: **Present perfect + for/since** → "we**'ve known** each other **for** eight years." (✗ "I know him for 8 years")
**will + V (kế hoạch/dự định nói tại chỗ)** và **be going to / be planning to + V** → "I'm planning to buy..."
**To + V (mục đích)** → "**To pick** the right one, I'll start by..."
**so + mệnh đề (kết quả)** → "..., **so** I'm sure he'd appreciate it."

p3.q: When do people normally send gifts to others?
p3.vi: Mọi người thường tặng quà vào dịp nào?
p3.a6: People usually give gifts on special occasions like birthdays, weddings and Tet. In Vietnam, we also give gifts on Teachers' Day on 20 November and on Women's Day. People also give gifts when they visit someone's new house, or when they want to say thank you. For example, I'm planning to buy a gift for Hung's birthday.
p3.a7: Mainly on special occasions such as birthdays, weddings, housewarmings and Tet. In Vietnam, there are also dates like Women's Day and Teachers' Day on 20 November, when giving a small present is almost expected. Some people also send gifts simply to say thank you or to apologise. In my case, it's Hung's birthday that's coming up.
p3.grammar: *Câu nhấn mạnh (cleft)* → "**It's** Hung's birthday **that's** coming up."

p3.q: Is it easy to choose clothes as gifts?
p3.vi: Chọn quần áo làm quà có dễ không?
p3.a6: No, I think it's quite difficult. You need to know the person's size and their taste. Even if the size is right, they might not like the style or the colour. That's why I chose a keyboard for Hung instead of clothes.
p3.a7: Not really. Clothes are tricky because you have to get the size, the style and the colour right, and people's tastes differ a lot. I'm quite particular about what I wear myself, so I'd hesitate to buy clothes for someone else unless I knew them very well. That's why I settled on a keyboard for Hung. A gift voucher can be a safe alternative.
p3.grammar: *Câu điều kiện loại 2* → "I'd hesitate **unless I knew** them well."

p3.q: Will people feel happy when receiving an expensive gift?
p3.vi: Nhận quà đắt tiền, mọi người có vui không?
p3.a6: It depends. Some people feel happy because the gift shows that the giver cares about them. But others may feel uncomfortable, because they think they have to buy something expensive in return. I think a thoughtful gift is more important than an expensive one.
p3.a7: It depends on the person and the relationship. Some people are delighted, as it shows how much the giver values them. Others may feel awkward or under pressure to return the favour, especially in a culture where gift-giving goes both ways. Personally, I think a thoughtful gift beats an expensive one, which is why I'm keeping the budget for Hung reasonable.
p3.grammar: *"which is why..."* → nối kết quả.

cards.title: Describe a time when you changed an important decision of yours
points: and explain how you felt about the experience
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: quyết định ban đầu là chuyển từ tester sang developer, sau đó đổi ý ở lại QA và học automation testing sau khi nói chuyện với một đồng nghiệp lớn hơn. Đề này PDF chỉ có 1 câu Part 3, nên mình thêm 2 câu mở rộng giám khảo có thể hỏi tiếp.

notes.v: about a year ago – 2 years as a tester
switch to developer – more money, more exciting
senior colleague – demand for testers – automation – personality (careful, detail)
relieved – confident – right call

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a time when I changed an important decision. It was about a year ago, when I was thinking about my career.

At that time, I'd been a software tester for about two years, and I originally decided to change my job to become a developer. I thought developers earn more money and their job looks more exciting.

However, I changed my mind after I talked to a senior colleague. He told me that testing is also a good career, especially automation testing, and good testers are in demand. He also said that I should choose a job that fits my personality. I'm careful and I like finding problems, so testing suits me better.

So I decided to stay in QA and learn automation testing. I felt relieved and more confident, and I think it was the right decision.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a time, about a year ago, when I changed a major career decision. I'd been working as a software tester for about two years, and I'd more or less made up my mind to switch to development, because I assumed developers earned more and had more exciting work.

But before I'd taken any concrete steps, I had a long chat with a senior colleague. He pointed out that the demand for good testers, especially in automation, is growing, and that I should pick a path that suits my personality. That really made me think. I'm detail-oriented and I enjoy tracking down problems, so testing is actually a natural fit for me.

In the end, I decided to stay in QA and focus on learning automation. Looking back, I felt relieved and much more confident afterwards, and I'm convinced it was the right call.

vocab.u: *I changed my mind after the talk.*

vocab.m: cẩn thận, chú ý chi tiết

grammar: **Quá khứ hoàn thành tiếp diễn / hoàn thành** → "I'**d been working** as a tester for two years." (hành động trước mốc quá khứ)
**Quá khứ hoàn thành + before** → "before I'**d taken** any concrete steps."
**"that" sau point out/tell** → "He pointed out **that** the demand is growing."
**Looking back, S + V** → rút gọn mệnh đề thời gian.

p3.q: When do most children begin to make their own decisions?
p3.vi: Trẻ em thường bắt đầu tự đưa ra quyết định từ khi nào?
p3.a6: It's good if you have a good reason. Sometimes new information shows that your first plan was wrong, like in my case. But if you change your mind too often, you can't finish anything.
p3.a7: It can be, as long as it's based on good reasons. Changing course after getting new information is a sign of flexibility, as in my case. However, if someone keeps changing their mind, they never see anything through. So I'd say it's about finding a balance.
p3.grammar: *as long as + mệnh đề* (điều kiện) → "as long as it's based on good reasons."

cards.title: Describe a famous person in your local area
points: and explain how you feel about this person
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: người nổi tiếng là ông Tuấn, nghệ nhân ở một làng nghề truyền thống gần nhà bạn (khớp giả định ở topic Hometown đã làm). Bạn thay bằng người thật (nghệ nhân, thầy giáo nổi tiếng, cầu thủ, người làm từ thiện...).

notes.v: Mr. Tuan – master craftsman – craft village near home – 60s
40+ years – exhibitions – TV – teaches young people free
skillful – humble – generous – tourists visit
proud – respect – local hero

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a famous person in my local area. His name is Mr. Tuan, and he's a master craftsman in a traditional craft village near my home.

He's about sixty years old, and he has made handmade products for more than forty years. Some of his products have been shown at exhibitions and bought by foreign tourists. He also teaches the craft to young people for free, so the tradition of the village doesn't disappear.

He's popular because he's very skillful, and he's also kind and helpful. Many local people respect him, and he has appeared on TV a few times. Tourists often come to visit his workshop and take photos with him.

I feel proud of him. He's a good example of a person who works hard and loves his job. I think he's an important part of our community.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about Mr. Tuan, a well-known master craftsman in a traditional craft village not far from where I live. He's in his sixties and has been making handmade products for over forty years.

What he's done is quite impressive. Not only has he kept the village's traditional techniques alive, but he also teaches them to young people free of charge so the craft doesn't die out. Some of his work has been displayed at exhibitions, and he's appeared on local TV a few times.

He's popular mainly because of his exceptional skill, but also because he's incredibly humble and generous. Tourists often drop by his workshop, and he never minds spending time chatting with them.

Personally, I feel really proud of him. He's living proof that hard work and passion can earn you respect, and he's something of a local hero in our area.
grammar: **Present perfect + for** → "has been making handmade products **for** over forty years."
**Not only + đảo ngữ** → "**Not only has he kept** the traditions alive, **but he also teaches**..." (dùng 1 lần, tạo điểm nhấn)
**so + mệnh đề (mục đích/kết quả)** → "..., so the craft doesn't die out."
**Present perfect bị động** → "Some of his work **has been displayed**."

p3.q: Is it always good to be a popular student at school?
p3.vi: Trở thành học sinh nổi tiếng ở trường có luôn tốt không?
p3.a6: I don't think it's always good. Popular students often have many friends and more confidence, which is good. But they may feel pressure to keep their image, and some spend too much time on social activities instead of studying. Also, some people may only want to be friends because of their popularity. Mr. Tuan is popular because of real skill, which is different.
p3.a7: Not necessarily. On the plus side, popular students tend to be more confident and have a strong support network. On the downside, there's the pressure to keep up an image, and it can be hard to tell who's a genuine friend and who's just following the crowd. Some may even neglect their studies. It also depends on why they're popular. Someone like Mr. Tuan earned his reputation through real skill and kindness, which is a healthier kind of popularity.

vocab.p: on the plus side / on the downside

p3.grammar: *Not necessarily* (trả lời "không hẳn") + *It depends on why...*

p3.q: Why are some students popular?
p3.vi: Tại sao một số học sinh nổi tiếng?
p3.a6: There are several reasons. Some students are good at studying, sports or art, so others admire them. Some are friendly and funny, so people like being around them. Others are popular because they look good or have a nice style, or because they're active on social media.
p3.a7: A number of factors come into play. Some excel academically or in sports or the arts, which earns admiration. Others are simply outgoing and good with people, so everyone wants to be around them. Appearance and personal style can also play a part, especially in the age of social media, where a student with lots of followers can become a campus celebrity almost overnight.
p3.grammar: *Some..., Others..., ...* → cấu trúc liệt kê nhóm người, rất hợp với câu hỏi "Why?".

cards.title: Describe a time you made an important decision and were happy with the result
points: how easy it was for you to make the decision
and explain why you were happy with the result
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: quyết định là học tiếng Anh nghiêm túc để thi IELTS (khớp mục tiêu thật của bạn). Mình viết trung thực với trình độ hiện tại ("mới bắt đầu nhưng đã thấy kết quả"), nên bạn có thể dùng gần như nguyên văn, chỉ chỉnh số liệu.

notes.v: study English seriously for IELTS – few months ago
IT docs in English – better job – study/work abroad
not easy – work full-time – low level – friend + study plan
1 hour a day – understand work docs – more confident – habit

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about an important decision I made a few months ago: to study English seriously for IELTS.

I made this decision because English is very important for my career. In IT, many documents and tools are in English, and good English can help me get a better job in the future. I also want to study or work abroad someday.

It wasn't very easy to decide. I was worried that I wouldn't have enough time because I work full-time, and I wasn't sure about my level, which is quite low. But after I talked to a friend and made a study plan, I decided to start.

I'm happy with the result so far. It's still early, but I can understand more English at work, and I feel more confident. I study about an hour every day, and I think it was a good decision.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a decision I made a few months ago: to take my English learning seriously and aim for a decent IELTS score.

The main reason was my career. In IT, a lot of the documentation and tools are in English, and good English opens doors, whether it's a better job or the chance to study abroad one day.

To be honest, it wasn't an easy decision. I work full-time, so I was worried about finding the time, and my level was pretty low, which made me doubt myself. What tipped the balance was talking to a friend and drawing up a realistic study plan, one hour a day, built around my commute and evenings.

I'm genuinely happy with the outcome so far. It's early days, but I can follow work documents more easily and I'm a lot more confident. Most importantly, I've built a habit I can stick to.
grammar: **Quá khứ đơn + present perfect cho kết quả** → "I **made** a decision a few months ago... I**'ve built** a habit."
**Mệnh đề quan hệ "which"** → "my level was low, **which** made me doubt myself."
**What + V + was + V-ing** → "**What tipped** the balance **was talking** to a friend."
**whether it's A or B** → "whether it's a better job or the chance to study abroad."

p3.q: How can we tell the difference between an important and an easy decision?
p3.vi: Làm sao phân biệt quyết định quan trọng và quyết định dễ?
p3.a6: I think important decisions have a big effect on our future, like choosing a job or a university. Easy decisions are small and have little effect, like what to eat for lunch. Also, important decisions need more time and thinking, and we feel more stress.
p3.a7: A good rule of thumb is the consequences. Important decisions have a long-term impact on our lives, such as choosing a career or a place to live, and they're hard to undo. Easy ones, like what to have for lunch, have little effect and can be reversed quickly. Important ones also tend to make us anxious and require research. Deciding to study English was in the first category for me.
p3.grammar: *Easy ones* → "ones" thay danh từ đã nhắc.

p3.q: Do you think it is a good idea to make a small decision every day?
p3.vi: Mỗi ngày đưa ra một quyết định nhỏ có phải ý hay không?
p3.a6: Yes, I think so. Small decisions help us practise making choices, so we become more confident. For example, planning what to do each day helps us manage time. But too many decisions can make us tired, so people often make routines.
p3.a7: Yes, to a degree. Making small decisions, like what to wear or when to study, builds the habit of taking control of your day. On the other hand, too many choices can cause decision fatigue, which is why many people stick to routines for trivial things so they can save their energy for the important ones.

vocab.m: mệt mỏi vì quá nhiều lựa chọn

p3.grammar: *so (that) + mệnh đề* → "...so they can save their energy."

p3.q: What little decisions do people make every day?
p3.vi: Mỗi ngày người ta đưa ra những quyết định nhỏ nào?
p3.a6: People decide what to wear, what to eat and how to go to work. They also decide when to go to bed and how to spend their free time. For example, I decide whether to take the bus at seven or seven thirty.
p3.a7: Quite a lot, actually: what to wear, what to have for breakfast, which route to take to work, whether to reply to a message now or later. For me, even choosing which bus to catch, and whether to study English on the way, is a daily decision.
p3.grammar: *wh-word + to + V* → "what **to wear**, which route **to take**, whether **to reply**."

p3.q: What if people in a group have different opinions on a decision?
p3.vi: Nếu mọi người trong nhóm có ý kiến khác nhau thì sao?
p3.a6: I think they should discuss and listen to each other. If they can't agree, they can vote and follow the majority. It's also good to find a compromise, so everyone is happy.
p3.a7: Ideally, they'd discuss it openly and listen to one another's reasoning. If there's still no agreement, they could vote and go with the majority, or find a compromise that gives everyone something. At work, we often handle this by comparing the pros and cons and letting the person responsible make the final call.
p3.grammar: *Câu điều kiện* → "**If** there's still no agreement, they **could** vote."

p3.q: Do you think most people's decisions are made in their 20s?
p3.vi: Bạn có nghĩ hầu hết quyết định của con người được đưa ra ở tuổi 20 không?
p3.a6: I partly agree. In our 20s, we decide on many important things like career, partner and where to live. But decisions at other ages are also important, like having children or changing jobs in our 30s or 40s.
p3.a7: To a large extent, yes, since the twenties are when people choose a career, a partner and often where to settle. However, I wouldn't say most decisions are made then. Plenty of major ones, like buying a home, having children or changing careers, come later. And as the world changes, many people reinvent themselves in their 30s or 40s.
p3.grammar: *"when" làm mệnh đề quan hệ chỉ thời gian* → "the twenties **are when** people choose a career."

p3.q: Which is better, to make a decision quickly or slowly?
p3.vi: Quyết định nhanh hay chậm thì tốt hơn?
p3.a6: It depends on the situation. For small decisions, deciding quickly saves time. But for big decisions, we should take time to think carefully, because a bad decision can cause problems. In my case, I took a few weeks before deciding to study English.
p3.a7: I'd say it depends on what's at stake. For minor matters, deciding quickly saves time and energy. For major ones, it's wiser to take your time, gather information and sleep on it. That said, overthinking can lead to missed opportunities. I took a few weeks to decide on studying English, and I think that balance was about right.

vocab.m: điều đang bị đe dọa/đặt cược

p3.grammar: *it's + adj (wiser) + to + V* → "it's wiser **to take** your time."

cards.title: Describe a person you know who did something difficult and was successful
points: what difficult thing this person did
and explain how you feel about this person
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: người trong bài là chú của bạn, mất việc ở nhà máy rồi mở xưởng đồ gỗ nhỏ ở quê ngoại thành Hà Nội. Đề này ghép với Part 3 về kinh doanh, nên chọn người làm kinh doanh sẽ có sẵn ví dụ cho cả 3 câu. Bạn thay bằng người thật.

notes.v: my uncle – countryside near Hanoi – furniture workshop
lost factory job 10 years ago – no money/experience – started business
hard work – learned from mistakes – quality – word of mouth
proud – look up to – never give up

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about my uncle, who did something difficult and was successful. He lives in the countryside near Hanoi, and he runs a small furniture workshop.

About ten years ago, he lost his job at a factory. He had little money and no experience of running a business, but he decided to start his own workshop making wooden furniture. At first it was very hard. He had few customers, and sometimes he almost gave up.

He was successful because he worked very hard and he never stopped learning. He learned from his mistakes, and he cared about quality, so customers trusted him and recommended him to others. Now he has ten workers and sells his products online too.

I feel proud of him and I admire him. He shows me that if you don't give up, you can succeed.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about my uncle, who started a small furniture business from scratch and made it work. He lives in the countryside outside Hanoi.

About ten years ago, he was laid off from a factory. With very little money and no experience of running a business, he took the risk of opening his own workshop making wooden furniture. The first couple of years were tough. Orders were scarce, and more than once he was close to throwing in the towel.

What made him successful, I think, was his persistence and his attention to quality. He learned from every mistake, and word of mouth gradually brought in customers. Today he employs ten workers and also sells through online platforms.

I really look up to him. His story taught me that determination can take you a long way, even when the odds are against you.
grammar: **Mệnh đề quan hệ "who"** → "my uncle, **who** started a business from scratch."
**With + N, S + V** → "**With** very little money, he took the risk." (cụm "with" chỉ hoàn cảnh)
**What made him successful was + N** → câu nhấn mạnh (cleft sentence).
**even when + mệnh đề** → "even when the odds are against you."

p3.q: Is it difficult to do business in today's world?
p3.vi: Kinh doanh trong thế giới ngày nay có khó không?
p3.a6: Yes, I think so. There is a lot of competition, and customers can compare prices online easily. Costs for rent, materials and workers are also rising. But technology also helps, because businesses can sell online and reach more customers. My uncle had a hard time at the beginning, but selling online helped him a lot.
p3.a7: I'd say it's both harder and easier. Harder, because competition is fierce, margins are thin and customers can compare prices in seconds. Rising costs, such as rent and raw materials, add to the pressure. On the flip side, technology has lowered the barrier to entry, since anyone can sell through online platforms. My uncle's workshop is a good example: online orders now make up a big part of his income.
p3.grammar: *both harder and easier* + giải thích "Harder, because..." (rút gọn câu để tự nhiên).

p3.q: How can companies help protect the environment?
p3.vi: Các công ty có thể giúp bảo vệ môi trường như thế nào?
p3.a6: Companies can reduce plastic packaging and use recycled materials. They can also save energy by using solar power and LED lights. Another way is to reduce waste and treat it properly. For example, my uncle sells his wood scraps to people who use them as fuel instead of throwing them away.
p3.a7: There are several ways. They could cut down on single-use plastic packaging, switch to renewable energy, and design products that last longer or can be recycled. They can also manage waste responsibly and be open about their environmental impact. Even small businesses can contribute: my uncle sells his wood offcuts as fuel rather than dumping them, which reduces waste and brings in a little extra income.
p3.grammar: *rather than + V-ing* → "sells it as fuel **rather than dumping** it."

p3.q: Does money equal success?
p3.vi: Tiền có đồng nghĩa với thành công không?
p3.a6: No, I don't think so. Money is important, but success also includes health, family and happiness. Some rich people are not happy. For me, my uncle is successful not only because of his money, but because he built something by himself and people respect him.
p3.a7: Not necessarily. Money is certainly one measure, but I think true success is broader: being healthy, having good relationships and doing work you find meaningful. Some wealthy people are stressed and lonely, while others with modest incomes are content. What I admire about my uncle isn't his income; it's that he built something from nothing and earned people's respect.
p3.grammar: *What I admire about X isn't A; it's B* → mẫu nhấn mạnh rất đẹp cho câu hỏi quan điểm.

cards.title: Describe a course that impressed you a lot
points: what you did during the course
and explain why it impressed you a lot
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: khóa học là Automation Testing với Selenium ở một trung tâm đào tạo tại Hà Nội (khớp nghề của bạn). Part 3 của đề này xoay quanh trí nhớ, mình nối ý về khóa học và công việc test. Bạn thay bằng khóa học thật.

notes.v: automation testing – Selenium – test websites automatically
training centre in Hanoi – evenings – 3 months
theory → practice – weekly scripts – group project – real stories
practical – used at work – saved time – clear career direction

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about an automation testing course that impressed me a lot. I took it about two years ago at a training centre in Hanoi.

The course was about how to use tools like Selenium to test websites automatically. It lasted three months, and I studied in the evening, two or three times a week after work.

During the course, we learned the basic theory first, and then we did a lot of practice. Each week we wrote small test scripts, and at the end we did a group project to test a real website. The teacher was an experienced engineer, and he often shared real stories from his job.

It impressed me because it was very practical. I could use what I learned at work immediately, and my work became faster and easier. It also made me more confident about my career.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about an automation testing course that really left a mark on me. I took it about two years ago at a training centre in Hanoi. It ran for three months, with evening classes two or three times a week after work.

The course focused on using Selenium to test websites automatically. We spent the first few sessions on the basics, then moved on to hands-on practice. Every week we wrote small test scripts, and towards the end we worked in a group to test a real website from start to finish. The instructor was a seasoned engineer who often shared real-life stories from his job, which made the lessons far more engaging.

What impressed me most was how practical it was. I could apply what I'd learned at work almost immediately, and it cut down the time I spent on repetitive tasks. It also gave me a clear direction for my career, which is why I still look back on it so fondly.

vocab.m: công việc lặp đi lặp lại

vocab.p: apply X to Y / apply what I learned

grammar: **Quá khứ hoàn thành** → "what I'**d learned**" (điều học được trước lúc áp dụng).
**spend + time + V-ing** → "the time I spent **on** repetitive tasks" / "spent the first sessions **on** the basics."
**which + mệnh đề (bổ sung ý)** → "..., **which** made the lessons far more engaging."
**move on to + N** → "moved on to hands-on practice."

p3.q: What do people need to remember in their daily lives?
p3.vi: Trong cuộc sống hằng ngày, mọi người cần nhớ những gì?
p3.a6: People need to remember things like appointments, deadlines and passwords. They also need to remember to pay bills and take medicine. Because life is busy, many people forget small things. For me, I need to remember my class schedule and my tasks at work.
p3.a7: Quite a lot, from practical things like appointments, deadlines and passwords to personal ones like family birthdays. In a busy modern life, it's easy to let something slip, so most people rely on lists and reminders. I do the same. When I was taking the course, I had to keep track of assignments and class times.
p3.grammar: *It's easy to + V* → "It's easy to let something slip."

p3.q: What can we learn from history?
p3.vi: Chúng ta có thể học được gì từ lịch sử?
p3.a6: We can learn from the mistakes of the past, so we don't repeat them. History also helps us understand our culture and why society is the way it is today. We can also learn from great people who worked hard to solve problems.
p3.a7: Above all, we can learn from past mistakes so that we avoid repeating them. History also explains how our society and culture came to be what they are today, and it offers examples of people who overcame great difficulties. Even in my own field, the history of technology shows how quickly things can change.
p3.grammar: *so that + mệnh đề* → "so that we avoid repeating them."

p3.q: Why do some people have a better memory than others?
p3.vi: Vì sao một số người có trí nhớ tốt hơn người khác?
p3.a6: There are several reasons. Some people are born with a good memory. Others practise more, for example by repeating things or writing them down. Sleeping well and being healthy also help. And people remember better when they're interested in the topic. I remembered my course well because it was practical and I used it a lot.
p3.a7: It's probably a mix of factors. Genetics may play a part, but habits matter a great deal: getting enough sleep, staying healthy and using techniques like repetition and note-taking. Interest is also key, as people remember what they care about. In my course, learning by doing helped me remember far more than reading ever did.
p3.grammar: *far more than* → so sánh nhấn mạnh.

p3.q: Do people like things of memorial significance?
p3.vi: Mọi người có thích những thứ mang ý nghĩa kỷ niệm không?
p3.a6: Yes, I think many people do. They keep things like old photos, gifts or souvenirs because these remind them of special people and places. They have emotional value. But some people prefer to live in the present and don't keep many things.
p3.a7: Yes, by and large. Objects such as old photos, handwritten letters or souvenirs carry sentimental value, since they bring back memories of special people and moments. Having said that, some people prefer to travel light and keep their memories in their heads instead.
p3.grammar: *Having said that, ...* → nối ý đối lập.

p3.q: Which can help people remember things better, words or photos?
p3.vi: Từ ngữ hay hình ảnh giúp nhớ tốt hơn?
p3.a6: I think photos are better because they show details and feelings immediately. When I see an old photo, I remember the moment quickly. But words are better for explaining complex information, like ideas or steps. So the best way is to use both.
p3.a7: It depends on what you want to remember. Photos are powerful for places, faces and emotions, because they trigger memories instantly. Words, on the other hand, work better for ideas and instructions that need explaining. In my job, I always combine the two: a bug report with a screenshot and a clear description.
p3.grammar: *work better for* → "Words work better for ideas."

p3.q: Can technology help people remember things better? How?
p3.vi: Công nghệ có giúp con người nhớ tốt hơn không? Bằng cách nào?
p3.a6: Yes, it can. We can use phone reminders, calendar apps and notes to remember tasks. We can also save photos and documents in the cloud. But if we depend on technology too much, our own memory may become weaker.
p3.a7: Definitely. Calendar apps, reminders and note-taking tools take care of the small stuff, and cloud storage keeps photos and documents safe for years. The flip side is that over-reliance may weaken our natural memory, as many of us can't even recall a phone number any more. I use calendar alerts for almost everything at work.
p3.grammar: *can't ... any more* → "can't even recall a number any more."

p3vocab.m: quên mất; *keep track of* = theo dõi; *rely on* = dựa vào; *deadline* = hạn chót.
lặp lại sai lầm; *come to be* = hình thành; *overcome difficulties* = vượt qua khó khăn; *role model* = tấm gương.
góp phần; *matter a great deal* = rất quan trọng; *technique* = kỹ thuật; *learning by doing* = học qua làm.
giá trị tình cảm; *bring back memories* = gợi lại kỷ niệm; *travel light* = sống gọn nhẹ; *souvenir* = quà lưu niệm.
khơi gợi ký ức; *instantly* = ngay lập tức; *combine* = kết hợp; *screenshot* = ảnh chụp màn hình.
lo liệu; *cloud storage* = lưu trữ đám mây; *the flip side* = mặt trái; *over-reliance* = phụ thuộc quá mức; *alert* = thông báo nhắc.

cards.title: Describe a time when someone talked about something you were not interested in but you kept listening
points: and explain how you feel about the experience
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: người nói là trưởng nhóm nói về golf trong giờ ăn trưa. Bạn thay bằng người/chủ đề thật (bố mẹ nói về chứng khoán, đồng nghiệp nói về bóng đá...).

notes.v: team leader – lunch break – last year
golf – weekend – rules – equipment
boss – polite – excited and funny
learned something – closer – patient listening

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a time when someone talked about something I wasn't interested in, but I kept listening. It happened last year during a lunch break at my company.

The person was my team leader. He started to talk about golf. He's a big fan of it, and he told us about his weekend at a golf course, the rules and the equipment. I know almost nothing about golf, and honestly, I don't find it interesting.

But I kept listening for two reasons. First, he's my boss, so I wanted to be polite and show respect. Second, he was so excited and funny that I enjoyed his stories, even though I didn't understand everything.

I feel it was a good experience. I learned something new, and after that lunch we became closer. Now I understand that listening patiently is also a way to build good relationships.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a time last year when my team leader went on and on about golf during a lunch break. He's a huge fan, and he took us through his weekend on the course, the rules and even the equipment. I know next to nothing about golf, and to be honest, it isn't my cup of tea.

Still, I kept listening, for a couple of reasons. First, he's my boss, so I wanted to be polite and show respect. Second, he was so enthusiastic and funny that I couldn't help being drawn in, even though half of it went over my head.

Looking back, I feel it was a valuable experience. I picked up a few new things, and that lunch brought us closer together. It also taught me that listening patiently, even about something that doesn't interest you, is a simple way to build good relationships at work.
grammar: **so + adj + that + mệnh đề** → "so enthusiastic and funny **that** I couldn't help being drawn in."
**even though + mệnh đề** → "even though half of it went over my head."
**Gerund làm chủ ngữ** → "**Listening** patiently is a simple way to..."
**Looking back, ...** → mở đầu phần cảm nhận.

p3.q: What kind of topics do young people like to talk about today?
p3.vi: Giới trẻ ngày nay thích nói về những chủ đề gì?
p3.a6: Young people like to talk about social media, music, games and fashion. They also talk about their jobs, travel and relationships. Many of them like to share funny videos and news online. It's very different from my team leader's golf topic.
p3.a7: Mostly things they can relate to in daily life: social media trends, music, gaming, fashion, and increasingly careers and money. Travel and relationships are popular too. Since so much of their conversation happens online, memes and viral videos often become the topic. That's quite different from my team leader's golf stories, which probably appeals to an older crowd.
p3.grammar: *Since + mệnh đề (lý do)* → "Since so much happens online, ..."

p3.q: What would happen if the listener didn't listen carefully?
p3.vi: Điều gì xảy ra nếu người nghe không chú ý?
p3.a6: There could be misunderstandings. The listener may miss important information and make mistakes. For example, at work, if I don't listen carefully to the requirements, I may test the wrong thing. Also, the speaker may feel disrespected.
p3.a7: It would probably lead to misunderstandings and mistakes. In my job, for instance, if I missed a detail in the requirements, I could end up testing the wrong feature and letting a bug slip through. On a personal level, the speaker might feel ignored or disrespected, and that can damage the relationship.
p3.grammar: *Câu điều kiện loại 2* → "**If** I missed a detail, I **could end up** testing the wrong feature."

p3.q: How can we tell if a listener is listening carefully?
p3.vi: Làm sao biết người nghe đang chú ý lắng nghe?
p3.a6: We can see it from their eyes and body. A good listener looks at you, nods and doesn't look at their phone. They also ask questions about what you said, and sometimes repeat your main ideas in their own words.
p3.a7: There are a few giveaways. A careful listener keeps eye contact, nods at the right moments and puts their phone away. More importantly, they ask relevant follow-up questions and can paraphrase what you've said. When I listened to my team leader, I asked him about the rules of golf, and he looked quite pleased.
p3.grammar: *More importantly, ...* → thêm ý quan trọng hơn.

p3vocab.m: xu hướng mạng xã hội; *relate to* = đồng cảm/liên quan; *viral videos* = video lan truyền; *appeal to* = thu hút.
dẫn đến hiểu lầm; *let a bug slip through* = để lọt lỗi; *feel disrespected* = cảm thấy bị thiếu tôn trọng; *damage the relationship* = làm hại mối quan hệ.
giữ giao tiếp bằng mắt; *a giveaway* = dấu hiệu lộ ra; *follow-up question* = câu hỏi nối tiếp; *paraphrase* = diễn đạt lại.

cards.title: Describe a person you know who really likes taking photos
points: when and how you got to know him/her
and explain how you feel about him/her
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: người trong bài là Linh, đồng nghiệp (business analyst) rất mê chụp ảnh, hay chụp ở Hồ Tây và Phố Cổ. Bạn thay bằng người thật (bạn, người thân).

notes.v: Linh – colleague – business analyst
2 years ago – joined my team – lunch – photo of meal
West Lake – Old Quarter – trips – smartphone
admire – sees beauty in small things – inspired

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about my colleague, Linh, who really likes taking photos. I got to know her about two years ago, when she joined my team as a business analyst. We often had lunch together, and one day I saw her taking a picture of her meal very carefully, so I asked her about it. She told me that photography is her biggest hobby.

She takes photos in many places. On weekends, she often goes to West Lake or the Old Quarter to take pictures of the streets and sunsets. When she travels, she also takes many photos of nature and local people. She usually uses her smartphone, but sometimes she borrows a camera from her brother.

I feel admiration for her. She sees beauty in small things that most people ignore. She also shares her photos with me, and they have inspired me to notice my surroundings more.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about my colleague Linh, who's passionate about photography. I got to know her about two years ago, when she joined our team as a business analyst. One lunchtime I noticed her carefully framing a shot of her meal, so I asked her about it, and she told me photography was her biggest hobby.

She takes photos pretty much everywhere. At weekends she often heads to West Lake or the Old Quarter to capture street scenes and sunsets, and when she travels, she photographs the scenery and local people. She mostly uses her smartphone, though she sometimes borrows her brother's camera.

I really admire her. She has a knack for noticing beauty in small things that most of us walk right past. She sometimes shares her photos with me, and they've inspired me to pay more attention to my surroundings.

vocab.m: đi ngang qua mà không để ý

grammar: **Mệnh đề quan hệ "who"** → "my colleague Linh, **who**'s passionate about photography."
**Quá khứ đơn + quá khứ tiếp diễn / noticing + V-ing** → "I noticed her **framing** a shot."
**Present perfect** → "they**'ve inspired** me to pay more attention." (kết quả đến hiện tại)
**though + mệnh đề** → "though she sometimes borrows..."

p3.q: Why are some people keen on taking photos?
p3.vi: Vì sao một số người mê chụp ảnh?
p3.a6: There are several reasons. Some people want to keep memories of special moments. Others enjoy being creative and showing their own view of the world. Many people also like sharing photos on social media to get likes and comments. For Linh, it's a hobby that helps her relax.
p3.a7: For a variety of reasons. Some want to preserve precious moments, others see photography as a creative outlet, and many enjoy sharing their lives on social media and getting a good response. For someone like Linh, it's also a way to slow down and appreciate the little things.
p3.grammar: *Some..., others..., many...* → liệt kê nhóm lý do.

p3.q: What kind of photos do people often take?
p3.vi: Mọi người thường chụp loại ảnh nào?
p3.a6: People often take selfies, photos of food, and photos with family and friends. They also take pictures of beautiful places when they travel. Some people take photos of pets or documents. Most of these photos are taken with smartphones.
p3.a7: Mostly everyday snapshots: selfies, group photos with friends and family, food and scenery. Pets are popular subjects too. Smartphones have also made it normal to photograph practical things, like receipts, documents or a parking spot. In my work, I take screenshots of bugs all the time, so that's one kind of photo I take a lot.
p3.grammar: *make it + adj + to V* → "have made it normal **to photograph** receipts."

p3.q: Do you think it's OK to take photos everywhere?
p3.vi: Bạn có nghĩ chụp ảnh ở mọi nơi là ổn không?
p3.a6: No, I don't think so. In some places, like museums, temples or private areas, taking photos may be not allowed or not polite. We should also ask for permission before taking photos of people. Linh always asks people before she takes their picture.
p3.a7: Not really. Some places, such as museums, religious sites and private areas, restrict photography, and it's simply a matter of respect. We should also ask permission before photographing strangers, since not everyone wants to end up on social media. Linh is good about this: she always checks with people first.
p3.grammar: *since + lý do* → "since not everyone wants to end up online."

p3.q: Why do tourists like taking photos while they are travelling?
p3.vi: Vì sao du khách thích chụp ảnh khi đi du lịch?
p3.a6: They want to keep memories of the places they visit, because they may not go back there again. They also want to show their friends and family where they have been, and many post photos online. Beautiful places also make people want to take pictures.
p3.a7: Mainly to capture memories of places they may never revisit. Photos also let them share the experience with friends and family, and posting them online has almost become part of the trip. And of course, picturesque scenery is hard to resist.
p3.grammar: *may never + V* → "places they **may never revisit**."

p3.q: Some people don't mind others walking into their shot when they're taking photos. What do you think?
p3.vi: Một số người không phiền khi người khác đi vào khung hình. Bạn nghĩ sao?
p3.a6: I think it depends. In crowded places, it's very hard to avoid, so I don't mind. People walking by can even make the photo look more natural. But if someone stands in front of the camera on purpose, that's annoying. In that case, I'd ask them politely to move.
p3.a7: I'm fairly relaxed about it. In busy tourist spots, it's almost impossible to get a shot without strangers in it, and they can even add some life to the picture. What I wouldn't tolerate is someone deliberately blocking the view. In that case, I'd politely ask them to move. For a really important shot, though, I'd wait for the right moment.
p3.grammar: *What I wouldn't tolerate is + N/V-ing* → câu nhấn mạnh.

p3vocab.m: lưu giữ kỷ niệm; *creative outlet* = lối thoát sáng tạo; *get likes* = nhận lượt thích; *slow down* = sống chậm lại.
ảnh chụp nhanh; *selfie* = ảnh tự sướng; *scenery* = phong cảnh; *screenshot* = ảnh chụp màn hình.
hạn chế; *a matter of respect* = vấn đề tôn trọng; *ask permission* = xin phép; *end up on social media* = rốt cuộc xuất hiện trên mạng.
lưu giữ kỷ niệm; *revisit* = thăm lại; *picturesque* = đẹp như tranh; *hard to resist* = khó cưỡng.
đi vào khung hình; *on purpose / deliberately* = cố ý; *add life to* = làm sinh động; *tolerate* = chịu đựng.

cards.title: Describe a new skill you learned when you were a child
points: and explain how you feel about learning the skill
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: kỹ năng là đi xe đạp, bố dạy lúc 8 tuổi ở sân trường gần nhà. Bạn thay bằng kỹ năng thật (bơi, thắt dây giày, nấu cơm, gấp quần áo...).

notes.v: riding a bicycle – about 8 years old
my father – small bike for birthday
school yard at weekends – held the seat – fell – 2 weeks
proud – independent – father's patience

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about riding a bicycle, which was a new skill I learned when I was a child. I learned it when I was about eight years old.

My father taught me. He bought me a small bicycle for my birthday, and on weekends he took me to the yard of a nearby school to practise. At first, he held the back of the seat and ran behind me. After a few days, he let go, and I rode alone. I fell several times and hurt my knees, but I didn't give up. After about two weeks, I could ride quite well.

I feel happy and proud when I remember it. It made me feel independent, because I could ride to school and to my friends' houses by myself. It also reminds me of my father's patience.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about learning to ride a bicycle, which was an important skill for me as a child. I was about eight at the time, and it was my father who taught me.

He bought me a small bike for my birthday, and at weekends he took me to the yard of a nearby school to practise. At first he held the back of the seat and jogged behind me. After a few days he let go without telling me, and suddenly I was riding on my own. I took quite a few tumbles and scraped my knees, but I was determined not to give up, and within about two weeks I could ride quite confidently.

Looking back, I feel proud and grateful. It gave me a sense of independence, since I could cycle to school and to my friends' houses by myself. It also reminds me of how patient my father was.
grammar: **Câu nhấn mạnh (cleft)** → "It was my father **who** taught me."
**at first... after a few days...** → trình tự thời gian.
**Quá khứ đơn kể chuyện + within + khoảng thời gian** → "within about two weeks I could ride."
**how + adj + S + was** → "how patient my father **was**." (câu gián tiếp, không đảo)

p3.q: What skills should children learn before they go to school?
p3.vi: Trẻ nên học những kỹ năng gì trước khi đi học?
p3.a6: I think children should learn basic self-care skills, like eating, dressing and going to the toilet by themselves. They should also learn good manners, like greeting people and saying thank you. Social skills like sharing and listening are important too, because they will need them at school.
p3.a7: First, basic self-care, such as dressing and eating independently. Second, good manners, like greeting people and saying please and thank you. And finally, social skills like sharing and taking turns, which make the transition to school a lot smoother. I'd also add simple safety habits, such as looking both ways before crossing the road.
p3.grammar: *First, / Second, / And finally,* → liệt kê rõ ràng (Coherence).

p3.q: What are the differences between learning in a group and learning by yourself?
p3.vi: Học nhóm và học một mình khác nhau thế nào?
p3.a6: In a group, you can share ideas, ask others for help and stay motivated. But sometimes you can be distracted. When you learn by yourself, you can study at your own pace and focus better, but you may feel lonely or get stuck.
p3.a7: Group learning is good for sharing ideas, getting instant help and staying motivated, although it can be distracting and you're tied to the group's pace. Studying alone lets you move at your own speed and concentrate fully, but there's no one to turn to when you get stuck. I tend to prefer studying alone, then checking my understanding with others.
p3.grammar: *although + mệnh đề* → đối lập trong cùng câu.

p3.q: What are the differences between the way adults learn and the way children learn?
p3.vi: Người lớn và trẻ em học khác nhau thế nào?
p3.a6: Children learn by playing, copying and trying things. They are curious and don't worry about mistakes. Adults learn more by reasoning and usually have a clear goal, but they have less time and often fear making mistakes.
p3.a7: Children tend to learn through play, imitation and trial and error, and they're not afraid of failing. Adults, on the other hand, learn by reasoning and usually have a clear goal in mind, but they're short of time and often worry about looking foolish. Learning to ride a bike was a good example for me: as a child, I simply kept falling and trying again.
p3.grammar: *tend to + V* → nói xu hướng chung.

p3.q: Do you think it is easier for children to learn new skills than for adults?
p3.vi: Trẻ em học kỹ năng mới dễ hơn người lớn không?
p3.a6: I think so, for most skills. Children's brains develop fast, and they have more free time. They also don't feel shy about making mistakes. But adults can learn faster in some areas because they understand the reasons and can plan their study.
p3.a7: Generally, yes, especially for things like languages and physical skills. Children's brains are very adaptable, they have fewer commitments and they're not embarrassed by mistakes. That said, adults have advantages too, such as discipline and the ability to plan, so with enough effort they can catch up.
p3.grammar: *with + N, S + V* → "with enough effort, they can catch up."

p3.q: Can a child learn skills from another child?
p3.vi: Trẻ có thể học kỹ năng từ trẻ khác không?
p3.a6: Yes, definitely. Children often copy each other when they play together. For example, they can learn games, sports or even how to ride a bike from friends. They also feel more relaxed with other children, so they learn fast.
p3.a7: Absolutely. Children pick up a lot from their peers by watching and copying them, whether it's a new game, a sport or how to ride a bike. They're often more relaxed around other children than around adults, so the learning feels natural and fun.
p3.grammar: *more relaxed around X than around Y* → so sánh hơn với giới từ.

p3.q: Is it important for everyone to have a specialised skill?
p3.vi: Mỗi người có cần một kỹ năng chuyên môn không?
p3.a6: Yes, I think it's important. A special skill helps people get a good job and earn money. It also gives people confidence. But general skills like communication and problem-solving are important too. My skill in software testing helps me in my career.
p3.a7: I'd say so. A specialised skill sets you apart in the job market and gives you a source of income and confidence. That said, it shouldn't come at the expense of general skills like communication and problem-solving, which are useful in any field. In my own case, software testing is my specialism, but teamwork and English matter just as much.
p3.grammar: *just as much* → "matter just as much."

p3vocab.m: kỹ năng tự chăm sóc; *manners* = phép lịch sự; *take turns* = lần lượt; *transition* = sự chuyển tiếp.
theo nhịp của mình; *distracting* = gây xao nhãng; *get stuck* = bị kẹt; *turn to someone* = nhờ cậy ai.
thử và sai; *imitation* = bắt chước; *be short of time* = thiếu thời gian; *look foolish* = trông ngớ ngẩn.
dễ thích nghi; *commitments* = trách nhiệm/bận rộn; *discipline* = kỷ luật; *catch up* = bắt kịp.
bạn đồng trang lứa; *pick up (skills)* = học được; *whether it's A or B* = dù là A hay B; *feel natural* = tự nhiên.
làm bạn nổi bật; *at the expense of* = đánh đổi bằng; *specialism* = chuyên môn; *job market* = thị trường việc làm.

cards.title: Describe a time when you saved money to buy something you wanted
points: why you wanted to buy it
how you saved money for it
and explain how you feel after buying it
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: món đồ là laptop, tiết kiệm 8 tháng, bằng cách để dành khoảng 1/4 lương và bớt trà sữa, ăn ngoài, mua quần áo (khớp tính cách chăm chút ngoại hình của bạn). Bạn thay bằng món đồ và số liệu thật.

notes.v: laptop – 2 years ago
old one slow, crashing – practise automation + study English
8 months – 1/4 salary – savings account – cut back bubble tea, eating out, clothes
sense of achievement – own money – take good care of it

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a time when I saved money to buy something I wanted. It was a laptop, and I bought it about two years ago.

I wanted it for two reasons. My old laptop was very slow and often broke down, which was a problem for my work. Also, I wanted a good machine to practise automation testing and study English at home.

It took me about eight months to save enough money. Every month, I put aside about a quarter of my salary in a savings account. I also cut down on things I didn't really need, like bubble tea, eating out and new clothes. That was a bit hard for me, because I like looking good.

When I finally bought it, I felt very happy and proud, because I paid for it with my own money. I also take better care of it than if someone had given it to me.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a time, about two years ago, when I saved up for a new laptop.

There were two reasons behind it. My old one had become painfully slow and kept crashing, which was getting in the way of my work. I also wanted a decent machine to practise automation testing and study English at home.

It took me around eight months to save enough. I set aside roughly a quarter of my salary every month and moved it into a savings account so I wouldn't be tempted to touch it. I also cut back on non-essentials, like bubble tea, eating out and new clothes, which wasn't easy for someone who cares about their appearance.

The day I finally bought it, I felt a real sense of achievement, because it was paid for entirely with my own money. I think I also look after it better than I would have if someone had given it to me.

vocab.p: cut back on / cut down on

grammar: **It took me + thời gian + to + V** → "It took me eight months **to save** enough."
**Quá khứ hoàn thành** → "My old one **had become** slow."
**so + S + wouldn't + V (mục đích)** → "so I wouldn't be tempted to touch it."
**Câu điều kiện loại 3 (so sánh)** → "better than I would have **if someone had given** it to me."

p3.q: Should schools teach children how to manage money from a young age?
p3.vi: Trường học có nên dạy trẻ quản lý tiền từ nhỏ không?
p3.a6: Yes, I think so. Money management is an important life skill, but many people don't learn it at school. If children learn how to budget and save from a young age, they can avoid money problems later. Schools can teach it with simple games and real examples.
p3.a7: Definitely. Managing money is a basic life skill, yet most of us learn it the hard way, through mistakes. If schools introduced budgeting and saving early, perhaps through games and real-life examples, students would be better prepared for adult life and less likely to fall into debt.
p3.grammar: *Câu điều kiện loại 2* → "**If** schools introduced..., students **would be**..."

p3.q: Should parents teach their children to spend money freely or to save money?
p3.vi: Cha mẹ nên dạy con tiêu tiền thoải mái hay tiết kiệm?
p3.a6: I think parents should teach them to save, but not too strictly. Children should learn that money is hard to earn. At the same time, it's good to let them spend a little on things they enjoy, so they learn from their choices. A balance is best.
p3.a7: Ideally, a bit of both. Teaching children to save instils discipline and shows them that money has to be earned. But letting them spend small amounts freely is also valuable, because that's how they learn from their own choices. I'd say a balance is best.
p3.grammar: *that's how + mệnh đề* → "that's how they learn."

p3.q: Do you think it is easier to teach teenagers how to manage money when they are around 16 or 17 years old?
p3.vi: Dạy thiếu niên 16–17 tuổi quản lý tiền có dễ hơn không?
p3.a6: I think it can be easier, because teenagers can understand more complex ideas, like budgets and interest. They also start to have their own money, for example from part-time jobs. But if they start learning earlier, it will become a habit, so it's better to start early.
p3.a7: In some ways, yes. At 16 or 17, teenagers can grasp more abstract ideas such as budgeting, interest and debt, and they often have real money from gifts or part-time jobs, which makes the lessons relevant. However, habits formed in childhood tend to stick, so starting earlier would still be better.
p3.grammar: *habits formed in childhood* → quá khứ phân từ rút gọn mệnh đề quan hệ.

p3.q: Is it easier to spend money or save money?
p3.vi: Tiêu tiền hay tiết kiệm tiền dễ hơn?
p3.a6: I think it's easier to spend money. Shopping is fun and there are so many things to buy, especially online. Saving needs discipline and patience. My own experience shows it: it took eight months to save for my laptop, but spending is very quick.
p3.a7: Spending, without a doubt. With online shopping and constant advertising, temptation is everywhere, and the reward is instant. Saving, by contrast, takes discipline and patience, because the payoff comes much later. Saving up for my laptop took eight months, but I could have spent that money in a single afternoon.
p3.grammar: *could have + V3* → "I **could have spent** that money in an afternoon."

p3.q: What kind of things do people usually save money for?
p3.vi: Mọi người thường tiết kiệm tiền để làm gì?
p3.a6: People save money for many things, like a house, a car or a wedding. They also save for their children's education, for travel, and for emergencies. Some people save for retirement. I saved for a laptop.
p3.a7: The big ones are usually a home, a wedding, children's education and retirement. Many people also keep an emergency fund for unexpected costs such as medical bills, while others save for travel or a particular gadget, as I did with my laptop.
p3.grammar: *as I did* → so sánh ngắn gọn với trợ động từ.

p3vocab.m: lập ngân sách; *learn it the hard way* = học qua sai lầm; *fall into debt* = rơi vào nợ nần; *life skill* = kỹ năng sống.
hình thành kỷ luật; *strike a balance* = tìm sự cân bằng; *learn from one's choices* = học từ lựa chọn của mình.
nắm bắt ý niệm trừu tượng; *relevant* = thiết thực; *stick* = bám lâu; *form a habit* = hình thành thói quen.
sự cám dỗ; *instant reward* = phần thưởng tức thì; *payoff* = kết quả/lợi ích; *by contrast* = ngược lại.
quỹ khẩn cấp; *retirement* = nghỉ hưu; *medical bills* = viện phí; *gadget* = thiết bị công nghệ.

cards.title: Describe a person you know who is very organised
points: what this person usually does to stay organised
in what situations you have noticed this quality
and explain why you think being organised is important to him/her
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: người trong bài là chị Hoa, project manager của bạn (đang quản lý 3 dự án). Bạn thay bằng người thật (sếp, đồng nghiệp, mẹ...).

notes.v: Ms. Hoa – project manager – late 30s – 3 projects
to-do list – calendar – task board – colour-coded – neat desk
meetings – agenda – release weeks – deadlines
many tasks and people – avoid mistakes – less stress

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about my project manager, Ms. Hoa, who is a very organised person. She's in her late thirties, and she manages three projects at the same time.

To stay organised, she does several things. Every morning she writes a to-do list and checks her calendar. She uses a task board to follow the progress of every task, and she colour-codes her notes. Her desk is always neat, and all her files are in the right folders.

I've noticed this quality in many situations, especially in meetings and in busy release weeks. She always prepares an agenda before a meeting, and she never forgets a deadline.

I think being organised is important to her because she handles many tasks and many people. If she isn't organised, things will go wrong, and she'll feel stressed. I really admire her, and I try to learn from her.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about my project manager, Ms. Hoa, who's one of the most organised people I know. She's in her late thirties and juggles three projects at the same time.

To stay on top of everything, she has a few habits. Every morning she writes a to-do list and goes through her calendar. She tracks every task on a project board, colour-codes her notes, and keeps her desk spotless, with every file in its proper folder.

I've noticed this most in meetings and during busy release weeks. She always sends out an agenda beforehand, and as far as I can remember, she's never missed a deadline.

I think being organised matters to her because she's responsible for so many tasks and people. Without a system, things would slip through the cracks, and she'd be constantly stressed. I really admire her, and I've picked up a few of her habits myself.
grammar: **Present perfect** → "I**'ve noticed** this quality." / "she's **never missed** a deadline."
**as far as I can remember** → cụm hạn định chắc chắn.
**Without + N, S + would + V** → "**Without a system**, things **would slip** through the cracks."
**one of the most + adj + N số nhiều** → "one of the most organised people I know."

p3.q: Why is it important for people to be organised?
p3.vi: Vì sao việc có tổ chức quan trọng?
p3.a6: Being organised helps people save time and avoid mistakes. They can finish their work on time and don't forget important things. It also reduces stress, because everything is under control. For Ms. Hoa, it's necessary because she manages many projects.
p3.a7: It saves time, prevents mistakes and reduces stress, because you always know what needs doing and when. Organised people also come across as more reliable, which builds trust with colleagues. For someone like Ms. Hoa, who's juggling several projects, it's simply essential.
p3.grammar: *because you always know what needs doing* → mệnh đề danh từ "what needs doing".

p3.q: Do you think children should learn to be organised from a young age?
p3.vi: Trẻ có nên học cách sống có tổ chức từ nhỏ không?
p3.a6: Yes, I think so. If children learn good habits when they're young, like keeping their rooms tidy and doing homework on time, they'll keep these habits as adults. It also helps them study better at school.
p3.a7: Yes. Habits formed in childhood tend to last a lifetime, so learning simple routines early, like tidying up and planning homework, pays off in the long run. It also makes school life much smoother and less stressful for them.
p3.grammar: *Habits formed in childhood* → quá khứ phân từ rút gọn.

p3.q: Are organised people more likely to be successful at work or in their studies?
p3.vi: Người có tổ chức có dễ thành công trong công việc/học tập hơn không?
p3.a6: Generally yes, because they use time well and finish tasks on time. People trust them more as well. But being organised is not enough. They also need skills, knowledge and good relationships with others.
p3.a7: Generally, yes. They manage their time well, meet deadlines and make a dependable impression, all of which count for a lot. But organisation alone isn't enough. You also need skills, creativity and good people skills. Ms. Hoa is successful not only because she's organised but also because she communicates well.
p3.grammar: *not only... but also...* → "not only because she's organised **but also** because..."

p3.q: What can people do to become more organised?
p3.vi: Người ta có thể làm gì để có tổ chức hơn?
p3.a6: People can write to-do lists and use a calendar or a phone app. They should also decide which tasks are most important and do them first. Keeping the desk and room tidy helps too. It's better to start with small habits.
p3.a7: Start small. Write a daily to-do list, use a calendar or app with reminders, and prioritise the tasks that matter most. Decluttering your desk and room helps clear your mind too. The key is to build these into a routine, so that being organised becomes automatic.
p3.grammar: *Mệnh lệnh để đưa lời khuyên* → "Start small. Write..., use..."

p3.q: Should parents teach their children to be organised?
p3.vi: Cha mẹ có nên dạy con có tổ chức không?
p3.a6: Yes, parents are the first teachers. They can give children small tasks, like cleaning their own room. Parents should also set a good example, because children copy what they see. But they shouldn't be too strict.
p3.a7: Yes, parents are a child's first role models. They can assign small chores, like tidying their own room, and set a good example, as children copy what they see at home. The trick is not to be overly strict, or it can backfire.
p3.grammar: *or + mệnh đề (nếu không thì)* → "not to be strict, **or** it can backfire."

p3.q: Do you think it is important for managers to be organised?
p3.vi: Quản lý có cần phải có tổ chức không?
p3.a6: Yes, very important. Managers handle many tasks and many people. If a manager is not organised, the team will be confused and may miss deadlines. A good manager also gives a good example, like Ms. Hoa does for us.
p3.a7: Absolutely, perhaps more than anyone. Managers coordinate people, deadlines and resources, so disorganisation at the top quickly spreads confusion through the whole team. Besides, a manager's habits set the tone for everyone, which is exactly what Ms. Hoa does for our team.
p3.grammar: *perhaps more than anyone* → câu rút gọn nhấn mạnh.

p3vocab.m: trong tầm kiểm soát; *come across as* = tạo cảm giác là; *reliable* = đáng tin cậy; *build trust* = xây dựng niềm tin.
giữ phòng gọn gàng; *last a lifetime* = bền suốt đời; *pay off* = đem lại kết quả; *in the long run* = về lâu dài.
kịp hạn chót; *dependable* = đáng tin; *count for a lot* = có giá trị lớn; *people skills* = kỹ năng giao tiếp.
ưu tiên; *declutter* = dọn dẹp bớt đồ; *a routine* = thói quen; *automatic* = tự động.
hình mẫu; *assign chores* = giao việc nhà; *set a good example* = làm gương; *backfire* = phản tác dụng.
điều phối; *resources* = nguồn lực; *spread confusion* = lan truyền sự rối loạn; *set the tone* = định hướng không khí.

cards.title: Describe a time when you interviewed a famous person
points: when and where you interviewed this person
what you talked about during the interview
and explain how you feel about the experience
cards.note: Lưu ý quan trọng: hầu hết người học chưa từng phỏng vấn người nổi tiếng. Trong IELTS Speaking, giám khảo không kiểm tra sự thật, bạn được phép bịa câu chuyện miễn là nói tự nhiên và mạch lạc. Bài mẫu dưới đây là câu chuyện giả định: bạn là thành viên CLB IT thời đại học, phỏng vấn một doanh nhân phần mềm (tên giả Mr. Long) cho bản tin của CLB. Bạn có thể đổi thành "phỏng vấn thầy giáo nổi tiếng, cựu sinh viên thành đạt, diễn giả..." tùy ý.

notes.v: Mr. Long – Vietnamese software entrepreneur
university – IT club event – meeting room after talk
how he started company – difficulties – advice for young IT people – English
nervous → excited – inspired – preparation = confidence

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a time when I interviewed a famous person. It happened when I was a university student, and the person was a well-known Vietnamese software entrepreneur. I'll call him Mr. Long.

I interviewed him in a meeting room at my university, after he gave a talk at an event organised by our IT club. I was in charge of the club's newsletter, so my job was to write an article about him.

We talked about how he started his company, the difficulties he faced, and his advice for young people in IT. He also said that English is very important for a career in technology, which I still remember well.

I felt very nervous before the interview, but it went well. Afterwards I felt excited and inspired. I also learned that good preparation makes you more confident.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a time I interviewed a well-known software entrepreneur, whom I'll call Mr. Long. It happened back when I was a university student.

I was in charge of our IT club's newsletter, and after he gave a talk at one of our events, I got the chance to interview him in a meeting room on campus for an article.

We talked about how he'd started his company from nothing, the setbacks he'd faced along the way, and his advice for young people in IT. One thing he stressed was the importance of English for a career in technology, which has stuck with me ever since.

I was extremely nervous beforehand, so I'd prepared a list of questions and practised them several times. Thankfully it went smoothly, and I came away feeling excited and inspired. More than anything, it taught me that thorough preparation is the best cure for nerves.
grammar: **Mệnh đề quan hệ "whom/who"** → "an entrepreneur, **whom** I'll call Mr. Long." (nói "who" cũng được)
**Quá khứ hoàn thành** → "how he**'d started** his company", "I**'d prepared** a list."
**which + present perfect** → "..., **which has stuck** with me ever since."
**More than anything, ...** → nhấn mạnh điều quan trọng nhất.

p3.q: What kinds of people are usually interviewed?
p3.vi: Những loại người nào thường được phỏng vấn?
p3.a6: Famous people like actors, singers and sports stars are often interviewed. Business leaders and experts are also interviewed because people want to learn from them. In the news, ordinary people who were involved in an event can also be interviewed. Job candidates are interviewed too.
p3.a7: Mainly public figures such as actors, athletes and politicians, but also experts and business leaders, since people want to learn from their experience, like Mr. Long. Ordinary people can be interviewed too, for example witnesses to an event or people in a survey. And, of course, job candidates are interviewed all the time.
p3.grammar: *Bị động* → "Ordinary people **can be interviewed** too."

p3.q: Why do some people dislike being interviewed?
p3.vi: Vì sao một số người không thích bị phỏng vấn?
p3.a6: Some people feel nervous when they have to speak in front of others. Others worry about their privacy, because they don't want to share personal information. They may also be afraid that their words will be changed or misunderstood in the news.
p3.a7: For a few reasons. Some people simply get nervous under pressure, particularly when they're being recorded. Others value their privacy and don't want to share personal details. There's also the worry of being misquoted or having their words taken out of context, which can damage their reputation.
p3.grammar: *the worry of + being + V3* → "the worry of **being misquoted**."

p3.q: Why do some people think interviews are a waste of time?
p3.vi: Vì sao một số người cho rằng phỏng vấn là lãng phí thời gian?
p3.a6: Some people think the questions are always the same, and the answers are not honest, so nothing new is learned. For job interviews, some people feel that a short talk cannot show a person's real ability. Also, preparing for an interview takes a lot of time.
