p3.a7: Some feel the questions are repetitive and the answers are rehearsed, so nothing genuinely new comes out of it. In the case of job interviews, a short conversation can't always reveal someone's true ability, and the preparation can eat up a lot of time. They'd rather judge people on their actual work.
p3.grammar: *They'd rather + V* → "They'd rather judge people on their work."

p3.q: What should people do to prepare for a job interview?
p3.vi: Cần chuẩn bị gì cho một buổi phỏng vấn xin việc?
p3.a6: They should research the company and the job first. Then they should practise answering common questions, and prepare examples of their experience. They should also dress neatly and arrive early. It's also a good idea to prepare a few questions to ask the interviewer.
p3.a7: First, research the company and the role so you know what they're looking for. Then rehearse answers to common questions, backed up with concrete examples from your experience. On the day, dress smartly, arrive early and bring a couple of questions of your own, as that shows genuine interest. A neat appearance helps create a good first impression, too.
p3.grammar: *Lời khuyên bằng mệnh lệnh / should* → "First, research... Then rehearse..."

p3vocab.m: nhân vật của công chúng; *witness* = nhân chứng; *survey* = khảo sát; *job candidate* = ứng viên.
chịu áp lực; *privacy* = quyền riêng tư; *be misquoted* = bị trích dẫn sai; *out of context* = bị tách khỏi ngữ cảnh.
lặp lại; *rehearsed* = đã chuẩn bị sẵn; *eat up time* = ngốn thời gian; *true ability* = năng lực thật.
tập dượt; *concrete examples* = ví dụ cụ thể; *dress smartly* = ăn mặc chỉnh tề; *first impression* = ấn tượng đầu tiên.

cards.title: Describe a happy person you know
points: and explain why you think he/she is a happy person
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: người trong bài là mẹ bạn (khớp với chi tiết "mẹ nấu ăn cho cả nhà" ở các file trước). Bạn thay bằng người thật (bạn thân, ông bà, đồng nghiệp vui tính...).

notes.v: my mother – fifties
kind – easygoing – optimistic – bright side
smiles – laughs – hums while cooking – chats with neighbours
content with simple life – grateful – doesn't compare – contagious

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about my mother, who is one of the happiest people I know. She's in her fifties, and she takes care of our family.

She's kind, easygoing and optimistic. She doesn't worry too much about small problems, and she always looks at the bright side.

She shows her happiness in many ways. She smiles a lot, she laughs loudly at funny things, and she hums old songs while she's cooking. She also loves chatting with our neighbours.

I think she's happy because she's content with a simple life. She doesn't compare herself with other people, and she's grateful for what she has, like her health and her family. Her happiness is also contagious. When she's at home, the whole house feels warmer. I really appreciate her.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about my mother, who's one of the happiest people I know. She's in her fifties and runs our household.

She's kind, easygoing and incredibly upbeat. Small problems hardly ever bother her, and she has a talent for looking on the bright side.

She shows her happiness in lots of little ways. She smiles easily, bursts out laughing at funny things, and hums old songs while she's cooking. She also loves a good chat with the neighbours over the fence.

The reason I think she's genuinely happy is that she's content with a simple life. She never compares herself with others, and she's grateful for what she has, especially her health and her family. What's more, her happiness is contagious: when she's around, the whole house feels warmer. I'm really grateful to have her as my mother.
grammar: **Mệnh đề quan hệ "who"** → "my mother, **who**'s one of the happiest people I know."
**have a talent for + V-ing** → "a talent for looking on the bright side."
**The reason I think... is that...** → cấu trúc giải thích.
**What's more, ...** → thêm ý mạnh hơn.

p3.q: Should teachers know what children are doing all the time?
p3.vi: Giáo viên có nên biết trẻ đang làm gì mọi lúc không?
p3.a6: I don't think so. Teachers should know what children do at school, for safety and for study. But if they watch children all the time, children may feel under pressure and have no privacy. Children also need some freedom to learn to be independent.
p3.a7: Not all the time, no. Teachers do need to keep an eye on children's safety and progress at school. But constant monitoring can make children feel under pressure and take away their independence. A good balance would be to stay aware without hovering over them, and to build trust.
p3.grammar: *without + V-ing* → "stay aware **without hovering** over them."

p3.q: Do you think teachers are able to spot the unhappy children?
p3.vi: Giáo viên có thể nhận ra những đứa trẻ không vui không?
p3.a6: Often yes, if they pay attention. Unhappy children may become quiet, lose interest in their studies or not play with friends. But in big classes, it's hard for teachers to notice everyone. Also, some children hide their feelings.
p3.a7: Often, yes, provided they pay attention. Warning signs include a child becoming withdrawn, losing interest in lessons or their grades dropping. But in large classes it's hard to notice everyone, and some children are good at hiding their feelings. That's why teachers and parents need to communicate regularly.
p3.grammar: *provided + mệnh đề* → điều kiện nhẹ.

p3.q: How can the arts spread positive emotions in society?
p3.vi: Nghệ thuật lan tỏa cảm xúc tích cực trong xã hội như thế nào?
p3.a6: Music, films and paintings can make people feel happy and relaxed. Public art, like murals and street music, can make a city more beautiful. Festivals and concerts also bring people together. My mother's singing at home is a small example: it makes our family happy.
p3.a7: The arts can lift people's moods and bring them together. A good song or comedy can make a whole audience laugh at the same time, and public art like murals and street music brightens up shared spaces. Festivals and concerts create a sense of community. Even in small ways, like my mother humming at home, music can spread a good mood.
p3.grammar: *like + N/V-ing* (ví dụ) → "like my mother humming at home."

p3.q: When do you think people are happiest?
p3.vi: Bạn nghĩ khi nào con người hạnh phúc nhất?
p3.a6: I think people are happiest when they spend time with family and friends. They are also happy when they achieve a goal, or when they do something they love. Many times, happiness comes from simple things, like having a good meal together.
p3.a7: I'd say when they're surrounded by people they love, or when they're absorbed in something they enjoy. Achieving a long-held goal can bring intense joy too. But, as my mother shows, happiness often comes from simple moments, like a home-cooked meal shared with family.
p3.grammar: *as + S + shows* → "as my mother shows."

p3vocab.m: để mắt đến; *constant monitoring* = giám sát liên tục; *hover over* = bám sát; *build trust* = xây dựng niềm tin.
dấu hiệu cảnh báo; *withdrawn* = thu mình; *provided (that)* = miễn là; *hide one's feelings* = giấu cảm xúc.
cải thiện tâm trạng; *mural* = tranh tường; *brighten up* = làm tươi sáng; *a sense of community* = tinh thần cộng đồng.
được vây quanh bởi; *be absorbed in* = mải mê; *long-held goal* = mục tiêu ấp ủ lâu; *simple moments* = khoảnh khắc giản dị.

cards.title: Describe your least favourite movie
points: and explain why it's your least favourite movie
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: bộ phim là phần tiếp theo của một series khoa học viễn tưởng (không nêu tên phim thật). Phù hợp với việc bạn thích phim hành động/sci-fi ở topic Films. Bạn thay bằng phim thật bạn không thích.

notes.v: last year – sequel of sci-fi series
cinema – shopping mall in Hanoi – 2 friends
heroes save Earth from aliens
boring – predictable plot – flat characters – 3 hours – special effects only

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about my least favourite movie. It was a sequel to a famous science fiction series, and I watched it last year.

I watched it at a cinema in a shopping mall in Hanoi with two friends. I'd been looking forward to it because I loved the first film, and the tickets were quite expensive.

The story was about a group of heroes who tried to save the Earth from an alien attack.

It's my least favourite because it was boring and disappointing. The plot was predictable, the characters were flat, and the film was almost three hours long. There were many special effects, but they couldn't cover the weak story. I even felt sleepy in the middle of the film. It was a waste of time and money, so I probably won't watch the next part.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about my least favourite movie, a sequel to a well-known sci-fi series that I watched last year.

I saw it at a cinema in a shopping mall in Hanoi with two friends. I'd been really looking forward to it, since I loved the first film, and the tickets weren't cheap either.

The story followed a group of heroes trying to save the Earth from an alien invasion.

The reason it tops my list of least favourite films is that it was a huge letdown. The plot was predictable, the characters were flat, and it dragged on for almost three hours. The special effects were impressive, but they couldn't make up for the weak storyline. I actually nodded off halfway through. It felt like a waste of both time and money, so I'll think twice before watching the next instalment.
grammar: **Quá khứ hoàn thành tiếp diễn** → "I'**d been looking forward** to it."
**a group of heroes + V-ing (rút gọn)** → "followed a group of heroes **trying** to save the Earth."
**The reason it tops my list is that...** → giải thích nguyên nhân.
**both A and B** → "a waste of **both** time **and** money."

p3.q: What kinds of movies are the most popular in Vietnam?
p3.vi: Thể loại phim nào phổ biến nhất ở Việt Nam?
p3.a6: I think action and superhero films from Hollywood are very popular, especially among young people. Vietnamese comedies and family films are also popular, especially during Tet. Horror movies and Korean romantic films have many fans too.
p3.a7: Hollywood blockbusters, particularly action and superhero films, draw big crowds, especially among younger audiences. Locally made comedies and family dramas also do well, notably around Tet. Horror films and Korean romances have loyal followings as well. Given my own taste, I mostly go for action and sci-fi, even if not every one lives up to expectations.
p3.grammar: *do well* = đạt thành công; *notably + mốc thời gian*.

p3.q: What are the differences between watching movies at home and in a cinema?
p3.vi: Xem phim ở nhà và ở rạp khác nhau thế nào?
p3.a6: At a cinema, the screen is big and the sound is great, so the experience is more exciting. But tickets are expensive and we must follow the time schedule. At home, it's cheaper and more comfortable. We can pause the film and eat anything we like.
p3.a7: The cinema offers a big screen, powerful sound and no distractions, which makes it a more immersive experience. On the downside, it costs more and you have to stick to the schedule. At home, it's cheaper and more convenient, and you can pause whenever you like. For a long film like the one I mentioned, I'd probably have preferred the comfort of my sofa.
p3.grammar: *would have preferred* → giả định về quá khứ.

p3.q: Are movies more likely to help people become more creative than books?
p3.vi: Phim có giúp con người sáng tạo hơn sách không?
p3.a6: I think books are better for creativity. When we read, we have to imagine the characters and places by ourselves. Movies show everything already, so we don't need to imagine. But movies can also give us new ideas, especially with their special effects and visuals.
p3.a7: If anything, books have the edge. When you read, you have to build the characters and settings in your own mind, which exercises your imagination. Movies serve everything up on a plate, so there's less left to the imagination. That said, films can still spark ideas through their visuals and storytelling, so both have a role to play.
p3.grammar: *there's less left to + N* → "less left to the imagination."

p3.q: Can movies help people better understand the cultural background of a country?
p3.vi: Phim có giúp hiểu rõ hơn bối cảnh văn hóa của một quốc gia không?
p3.a6: Yes, I think so. Movies show how people live, what they wear and eat, and what traditions they have. For example, Korean films helped many people learn about Korean food and family values. But movies are sometimes not realistic, so they may give a wrong idea.
p3.a7: To a certain extent, yes. Films give a window into everyday life, food, clothing, traditions and values. Korean dramas, for example, have introduced many people to Korean cuisine and family culture. The caveat is that movies often exaggerate or stereotype, so they should be a starting point rather than the full picture.
p3.grammar: *rather than + N* → "a starting point rather than the full picture."

p3vocab.m: phim bom tấn; *draw big crowds* = thu hút đông khán giả; *loyal following* = lượng fan trung thành; *live up to expectations* = đáp ứng kỳ vọng.
đắm chìm; *stick to the schedule* = theo lịch chiếu; *pause* = tạm dừng; *the comfort of my sofa* = sự thoải mái của ghế sofa.
nhỉnh hơn; *exercise one's imagination* = rèn trí tưởng tượng; *serve up on a plate* = dọn sẵn; *spark ideas* = khơi gợi ý tưởng.
cánh cửa nhìn vào; *caveat* = lưu ý; *stereotype* = rập khuôn; *the full picture* = bức tranh toàn cảnh.

cards.title: Describe a person who learns history and loves history
points: and explain how you feel about him/her
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: người trong bài là bố bạn, thích đọc sách sử, xem phim tài liệu và đi bảo tàng. Khớp với phần History (topic 39) bạn đã học: hồi nhỏ không mê lịch sử, nay đã thấy thú vị hơn. Bạn thay bằng người thật.

notes.v: my father – late fifties
history books – old newspapers – documentaries – museums – historical sites – chats
understand past → present – stories of great people – value peace
respect – I enjoy history more because of him

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about my father, who learns history and loves history. He's in his late fifties.

He learns history in several ways. He reads history books and old newspapers, and he watches documentaries on TV in the evening. On holidays, he likes to visit museums and historical sites, and he sometimes takes me with him. He also talks about history with his old friends.

He loves history because he thinks that understanding the past helps us understand the present. He also says that history is full of interesting stories about great people, and that it teaches us to value peace.

I feel respect for him. At first I wasn't interested in history, but because of him, I've started to enjoy it a little more.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about my father, who's a real history buff. He's in his late fifties and has been fascinated by history for as long as I can remember.

He learns about it in all sorts of ways. He reads history books and old newspapers, watches documentaries most evenings, and on holidays he likes to visit museums and historical sites, often dragging me along. He also enjoys swapping stories with his old friends.

He loves history because he believes that understanding the past is the key to understanding the present. He also finds it full of fascinating stories about great people, and he says it teaches us to value peace.

I have a lot of respect for him. I wasn't into history at school, but his enthusiasm is rubbing off on me, and I'm starting to see why he finds it so absorbing.

vocab.p: for as long as I can remember

grammar: **Present perfect continuous** → "has been fascinated" / "I've started to enjoy..."
**believes that + mệnh đề** → "he believes **that** understanding the past is the key."
**Gerund làm chủ ngữ** → "**Understanding** the past helps us..."
**Hiện tại tiếp diễn cho thay đổi** → "his enthusiasm **is rubbing off** on me."

p3.q: Do you think children should begin learning history from an early age?
p3.vi: Trẻ có nên bắt đầu học lịch sử từ nhỏ không?
p3.a6: Yes, I think so, but in a simple and fun way. Young children can learn through stories and cartoons about heroes and events. If they start early, they will have more interest and understand their country better. But it shouldn't be too difficult or boring.
p3.a7: Yes, provided it's done in an engaging way. Young children respond well to stories, cartoons and field trips, which can plant an early interest in the past and a sense of national identity. What would be counterproductive is forcing them to memorise dates and names, which is what put me off history at school.
p3.grammar: *What would be counterproductive is + V-ing* → câu nhấn mạnh.

p3.q: At what age do you think people should begin to learn history?
p3.vi: Bạn nghĩ nên bắt đầu học lịch sử từ độ tuổi nào?
p3.a6: I think from about six or seven, when children start primary school. They can start with simple stories, and later at around twelve they can learn more about dates and causes. It's best to increase the difficulty step by step.
p3.a7: I'd say from around six or seven, with simple stories and famous figures. From about twelve, when they can think more critically, they can move on to causes and consequences, and in the teenage years to analysing different sources. The key is to raise the level gradually.
p3.grammar: *from + tuổi, ...* → chia giai đoạn.

p3.q: How do children learn history before they attend school?
p3.vi: Trẻ em học lịch sử thế nào trước khi đến trường?
p3.a6: They learn from stories told by grandparents and parents. They also learn from cartoons, children's books and visits to museums or historical places. In Vietnam, many children hear folk tales and legends about heroes from their families.
p3.a7: Mostly through storytelling. Grandparents and parents pass on family tales, folk stories and legends about national heroes, and children also pick things up from picture books, cartoons and occasional visits to museums or historic sites. In Vietnam, many kids grow up hearing legends of heroes long before they study them in class.
p3.grammar: *long before + mệnh đề* → "long before they study them in class."

p3.q: Is it important to learn how people in the past lived their lives?
p3.vi: Học cách người xưa sống có quan trọng không?
p3.a6: Yes, I think it's important. It helps us understand why society is the way it is today. We can also learn good values and traditions from the past. And we feel more grateful for the better life we have now.
p3.a7: Yes, I think so. It explains how we got to where we are today, and it passes on values and traditions worth preserving. It also puts our own lives into perspective, as we realise how much easier things are now. My father often reminds us of that.
p3.grammar: *how much easier things are* → câu gián tiếp, không đảo.

p3.q: Do you think people should learn ancient history before learning modern history?
p3.vi: Có nên học lịch sử cổ đại trước lịch sử hiện đại không?
p3.a6: I think it's better to learn in order of time, because ancient history explains the beginning of things. It helps us understand later events. But for young children, modern history is closer to their life, so it might be easier and more interesting.
p3.a7: Learning chronologically makes sense, since earlier events help explain later ones. However, for young learners, modern history can be more relatable and therefore more engaging. So I'd suggest a flexible approach: spark interest with recent, familiar events, then go back to the roots.
p3.grammar: *since + lý do; therefore + kết quả* → nối ý logic.

p3.q: Besides historical events, what else is important when learning history?
p3.vi: Ngoài sự kiện lịch sử, học lịch sử còn cần chú ý điều gì?
p3.a6: I think the causes and results of events are important. We should also learn about culture, daily life and famous people. And it's important to think critically, so we don't believe everything we read.
p3.a7: Understanding the causes and consequences behind events matters more than the events themselves. It's also worth learning about everyday life, culture and the people involved, as that makes history feel real. Above all, learners should develop critical thinking, checking sources instead of accepting every account at face value.
p3.grammar: *instead of + V-ing* → "checking sources instead of accepting..."

p3vocab.m: phản ứng tốt với; *plant an interest* = gieo hứng thú; *national identity* = bản sắc dân tộc; *counterproductive* = phản tác dụng; *put someone off* = làm ai chán.
nhân vật nổi tiếng; *causes and consequences* = nguyên nhân và hệ quả; *analyse sources* = phân tích nguồn; *gradually* = dần dần.
truyền lại câu chuyện; *folk tale* = truyện dân gian; *legend* = truyền thuyết; *pick things up* = học lỏm.
đặt vào góc nhìn đúng; *worth preserving* = đáng bảo tồn; *pass on values* = truyền lại giá trị; *how we got to where we are* = chúng ta đã đi đến hôm nay thế nào.
theo trình tự thời gian; *relatable* = dễ đồng cảm; *go back to the roots* = quay về cội nguồn; *flexible approach* = cách tiếp cận linh hoạt.
tin theo bề ngoài; *critical thinking* = tư duy phản biện; *sources* = nguồn tài liệu; *daily life* = đời sống thường ngày.

cards.title: Describe an enjoyable evening you had with your friends
points: who you spent the evening with
and explain why it was enjoyable
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: buổi tối là sinh nhật anh Hùng (bạn đại học, người trong đề 2): ăn lẩu rồi hát karaoke. Khớp với việc bạn "chỉ hát karaoke với bạn bè". Đề này PDF chỉ có 1 câu Part 3, nên mình thêm 2 câu mở rộng giám khảo có thể hỏi tiếp.

notes.v: last month – Hung's birthday – hotpot restaurant – karaoke
ate – old school days – joked – sang 2 hours
6 university friends – rarely meet
laughed a lot – no work talk – relaxed – good mood

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about an enjoyable evening I had with my friends last month. It was my friend Hung's birthday, and we celebrated it at a hotpot restaurant in the city centre, and then we went to a karaoke place nearby.

There were six of us, all from my university class. We don't meet very often because everybody is busy with work, so it was a good chance to catch up.

At the restaurant, we ate a lot, talked about our old school days and joked about each other. After that, we sang karaoke for two hours. I'm not a good singer, but with friends I felt free to sing loudly.

It was enjoyable because we laughed a lot, and nobody talked about work. I felt relaxed and happy, and I went home late but in a very good mood.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a really enjoyable evening I spent with my friends last month. It was my friend Hung's birthday, so we had dinner at a hotpot restaurant in the city centre and then headed to a karaoke place nearby.

There were six of us, all former classmates from university. Since we're all tied up with work, we rarely get together, so it was a great chance to catch up.

Over dinner, we reminisced about our old school days and teased each other about silly things we'd done. Afterwards, we spent two hours at karaoke. I'm no singer, but among friends, I had no qualms about belting out a few songs.

What made it so enjoyable was that we laughed non-stop, and nobody mentioned work once. I felt completely relaxed, and I went home late, but on a real high.
grammar: **Since + lý do** → "**Since** we're all tied up with work, we rarely get together."
**There were six of us** → mẫu giới thiệu số người.
**What made it so enjoyable was that + mệnh đề** → câu nhấn mạnh.
**Quá khứ hoàn thành** → "silly things we'**d done**."

p3.q: How do people get along in a big family?
p3.vi: Mọi người sống hòa thuận thế nào trong một đại gia đình?
p3.a6: Now many people chat online instead of meeting face to face. They use social media and video calls. It's more convenient, but I think meeting in person is better for real friendship.
p3.a7: Technology has changed a lot. People chat through messaging apps and video calls, so it's easier than ever to stay in touch. The downside is that it can replace face-to-face contact, which is still the best way to build real bonds, as that evening with my friends reminded me.
p3.grammar: *easier than ever* → so sánh nhấn mạnh.

p3vocab.m: nhường nhịn qua lại; *look out for* = quan tâm, che chở; *defer to* = nghe theo; *talk things through* = nói chuyện cho rõ; *inevitable* = không thể tránh khỏi.
nghiêng về; *a lively night out* = buổi tối đi chơi sôi động; *a mix of* = sự kết hợp; *vary with* = thay đổi theo.
trực tiếp; *stay in touch* = giữ liên lạc; *build bonds* = xây dựng gắn kết; *the downside* = mặt trái.

cards.title: Describe a person who is good at making things by hand
points: what materials or technologies he/she uses
and why you think this person is good at making things by hand
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: người trong bài là bà của bạn, đan len (áo, khăn, mũ). Ở mục "technologies", bà dùng điện thoại xem video YouTube để học mẫu mới. Bạn thay bằng người thật (mẹ may vá, dì làm đồ thủ công...).

notes.v: my grandmother – seventies – countryside
woollen sweaters, scarves, hats – every winter – baby socks
wool – bamboo needles – YouTube tutorials on phone
50+ years – neat, strong – unique – made with love

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about my grandmother, who is very good at making things by hand. She's in her seventies, and she lives in the countryside.

She mostly makes woollen clothes, like sweaters, scarves and hats. Every winter she knits something for each member of the family. She also makes small things like baby socks for the neighbours' children.

She uses wool and bamboo needles. She doesn't use any machines, but she uses her smartphone to watch videos on YouTube and learn new patterns, which surprised me a lot.

I think she's good at it because she has done it for more than fifty years. Her work is neat and strong, and every piece is unique. I wear her sweaters every winter, and they're warmer than the ones from shops, because they're made with love.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about my grandmother, who has a real talent for making things by hand. She's in her seventies and lives in the countryside.

Her speciality is knitting. Every winter she makes a woollen sweater, scarf or hat for each member of the family, and she often knits little baby socks for the neighbours' children as well.

As for materials, she works with wool and bamboo needles, and no machines are involved. What surprised me, though, is that she uses her smartphone to watch tutorials on YouTube and pick up new patterns.

I think she's so good at it because she's been knitting for over fifty years. Her stitches are neat and sturdy, and every piece is one of a kind. I wear her sweaters every winter, and they feel much warmer than shop-bought ones, perhaps because they're made with love.
grammar: **Mệnh đề quan hệ "who"** → "my grandmother, **who** has a real talent."
**As for + N** → "**As for** materials, she works with wool."
**What surprised me is that + mệnh đề** → câu nhấn mạnh.
**Present perfect continuous** → "she's **been knitting** for over fifty years."

p3.q: Do you think handmade is a good thing?
p3.vi: Bạn có nghĩ đồ làm thủ công là điều tốt không?
p3.a6: Yes, I think so. Handmade things are usually unique and made with more care. They are also often made with natural materials. But they take time and cost more money, so not everyone can buy them.
p3.a7: By and large, yes. Handmade items are one of a kind, crafted with care and often made from natural materials. The trade-off is that they take longer and cost more, which puts them out of reach for some people. Still, I'd rather own one well-made piece, like my grandmother's sweaters, than several mass-produced ones.
p3.grammar: *I'd rather + V than + V* → "I'd rather own one... than several..."

p3.q: Do you think children like making things by hand?
p3.vi: Trẻ em có thích làm đồ thủ công không?
p3.a6: Yes, most children do. They like drawing, making paper toys and playing with clay. It's fun, and they can be creative. But nowadays, many children prefer phones and games, so they make fewer things by hand.
p3.a7: Generally, yes. Young children love getting their hands dirty with paper, clay and paint, because it's playful and lets them be creative. These days, though, screens compete for their attention, so parents and schools need to encourage hands-on activities.
p3.grammar: *fewer + N đếm được* → "fewer things."

p3.q: Is traditional craftsmanship important to the country's industry?
p3.vi: Nghề thủ công truyền thống có quan trọng với nền công nghiệp quốc gia không?
p3.a6: Yes, I think so. Traditional crafts keep cultural identity and provide jobs for local people, especially in villages. Many products are also exported, so they bring money to the country. We should protect them.
p3.a7: Yes, definitely. Traditional crafts preserve cultural heritage, provide livelihoods in rural areas and generate export income, such as ceramics, silk and lacquerware. They also give a country a distinctive brand in the global market, which is why they deserve government support.
p3.grammar: *which is why + mệnh đề* → nối kết quả.

p3.q: What kinds of handmade things did you make as a child?
p3.vi: Hồi nhỏ bạn đã làm đồ thủ công nào?
p3.a6: I made paper boats and paper planes, and cards for my teachers on Teachers' Day. During the Mid-Autumn Festival, I also made a star lantern from paper and bamboo with my father. I enjoyed these activities a lot.
p3.a7: Quite a few things: paper boats and planes, handmade cards for my teachers on Teachers' Day and, around the Mid-Autumn Festival, a star-shaped lantern from bamboo and coloured paper, which I made with my father. They weren't perfect, but I was very proud of them.
p3.grammar: *Quá khứ đơn kể kỷ niệm* → "I made..., I enjoyed..."

p3.q: What can handmade products bring to tourist attractions?
p3.vi: Sản phẩm thủ công mang lại điều gì cho điểm du lịch?
p3.a6: They can bring money and more visitors. Tourists like to buy unique local souvenirs. They can also watch how the products are made, which is an interesting experience. It also helps local craftspeople.
p3.a7: Handmade products add authenticity and give visitors something unique to take home, which boosts local income. Demonstrations and workshops, where tourists try making things themselves, turn a simple visit into a memorable experience. It also creates jobs for local craftspeople and helps keep traditions alive.
p3.grammar: *turn A into B* → "turn a visit into an experience."

p3vocab.m: sự đánh đổi; *out of reach* = ngoài tầm với; *mass-produced* = sản xuất hàng loạt; *crafted with care* = làm tỉ mỉ.
tự tay làm; *compete for attention* = tranh sự chú ý; *hands-on activities* = hoạt động thực hành; *creative* = sáng tạo.
di sản văn hóa; *livelihood* = kế sinh nhai; *export income* = thu nhập xuất khẩu; *deserve support* = xứng đáng được hỗ trợ.
thuyền giấy; *star lantern* = đèn ông sao; *Mid-Autumn Festival* = Tết Trung thu; *be proud of* = tự hào về.
tính chân thực; *demonstration* = buổi trình diễn; *memorable experience* = trải nghiệm đáng nhớ; *keep traditions alive* = giữ truyền thống.

cards.title: Describe a natural place in your city that you enjoy visiting
points: who you often go there with
and explain why you enjoy visiting there
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: nơi trong bài là Hồ Tây (West Lake), Hà Nội, bạn đi khoảng 2 lần/tháng vào cuối tuần. Bạn thay bằng nơi thật (công viên Yên Sở, Ecopark, hồ Gươm...).

notes.v: West Lake – north-west Hanoi – biggest lake
peaceful – trees – cool air – joggers – sunset – temples, cafés
twice a month – weekends – late afternoon – friends/family/alone
escape from traffic – relax after stressful week – fresh air

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about West Lake, a natural place in Hanoi that I enjoy visiting. It's in the north-west of the city, and it's the biggest lake in Hanoi.

It's large and peaceful. There are many trees along the road around it, and the air is fresh and cool. You can see people jogging, cycling or walking, and the sunset on the water is very beautiful. There are also some old temples and cafés near the lake.

I go there about twice a month, usually at weekends in the late afternoon. I usually go with my friends, but sometimes I go with my family or alone.

I enjoy it because it's a good escape from the noisy traffic and busy work life. After a stressful week, walking by the lake makes me feel relaxed, and the fresh air makes me feel better.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about West Lake, a natural spot in Hanoi that I really enjoy visiting. It's in the north-west of the city and it's the largest lake in Hanoi.

It's wonderfully peaceful, with tree-lined roads running around it and a cool breeze coming off the water. You'll see people jogging, cycling or just strolling, and the sunset over the lake is stunning. There are also a few old temples and cafés dotted along the shore.

I go about twice a month, usually at the weekend in the late afternoon. Most of the time I'm with friends, although occasionally I go with my family or on my own.

What I love most about it is that it's a welcome escape from the traffic and the pressure of work. After a stressful week, a walk by the lake helps me unwind, and the fresh air gives me a real lift.
grammar: **Mệnh đề quan hệ rút gọn** → "a natural spot **that** I enjoy visiting" (có thể bỏ "that").
**with + N + V-ing** → "with tree-lined roads **running** around it."
**What I love most about it is that...** → câu nhấn mạnh.
**although + mệnh đề** → "although occasionally I go with family."

p3.q: Do you think there should be many natural places in cities?
p3.vi: Thành phố có nên có nhiều không gian thiên nhiên không?
p3.a6: Yes, definitely. Cities are crowded and polluted, so people need places with trees and water to relax. Parks and lakes also make the air cleaner and the city cooler. In Hanoi, I think we need more of them, because many areas are full of buildings.
p3.a7: Absolutely. Cities tend to be crowded and polluted, so green spaces serve as the lungs of the city, cleaning the air and keeping temperatures down. They also give residents somewhere to exercise and unwind. In Hanoi, where new buildings are going up everywhere, I think more such places are badly needed.
p3.grammar: *so + kết quả* → "Cities are polluted, so green spaces..."

p3.q: Do you think staying in a natural place would help change people's mood?
p3.vi: Ở trong không gian thiên nhiên có giúp thay đổi tâm trạng không?
p3.a6: Yes, I think so. When I walk by West Lake, I feel more relaxed and less stressed. Nature is quiet and beautiful, and the fresh air helps us think more clearly. Many studies also say that nature is good for mental health.
p3.a7: Definitely. I speak from experience: a walk by the lake lifts my mood and clears my head after a stressful week. Peace and quiet, greenery and fresh air all help the mind to reset. There's plenty of research linking time in nature to lower stress and better mental health.
p3.grammar: *I speak from experience* → mở đầu bằng trải nghiệm cá nhân.

p3.q: Which is more important, protecting the environment or developing the economy?
p3.vi: Bảo vệ môi trường hay phát triển kinh tế quan trọng hơn?
p3.a6: I think both are important, but protecting the environment is more important in the long term. If we damage the environment, we will have health problems and lose natural resources. A strong economy is useful, but we can't enjoy money in a polluted place. The best way is to develop the economy in a green way.
p3.a7: It's a tough call, but in the long run I'd say protecting the environment, because a damaged environment ends up harming health and the economy itself. That said, the two don't have to be at odds. With renewable energy and cleaner technology, countries can grow and stay green at the same time.
p3.grammar: *don't have to be at odds* → "don't have to + V."

p3vocab.m: không gian xanh; *the lungs of the city* = lá phổi của thành phố; *keep temperatures down* = giữ nhiệt độ thấp; *badly needed* = rất cần.
nâng tâm trạng; *clear one's head* = đầu óc thông thoáng; *greenery* = cây xanh; *mental health* = sức khỏe tinh thần.
quyết định khó; *in the long run* = về lâu dài; *at odds* = mâu thuẫn; *renewable energy* = năng lượng tái tạo.

cards.title: Describe a noisy place you have been to
points: and explain why you feel it's a noisy place
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: nơi ồn ào là nhà hàng tiệc cưới trong đám cưới của anh/chị họ vào mùa xuân năm nay. Rất hợp văn hóa Việt Nam (nhạc to, MC hô, mọi người cùng hô "dô"). Đề này PDF không liệt kê câu Part 3, nên mình thêm 3 câu Part 3 có thể gặp (tác động của tiếng ồn, giảm ồn, vì sao có người thích nơi ồn).

notes.v: wedding hall – Hanoi
this spring – cousin's wedding – ~300 guests
dinner – photos with couple – speeches – singing show
loud speakers – MC shouting – everyone shouting "cheers" – headache

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a noisy place I've been to, which is a wedding hall in Hanoi. I went there in the spring of this year for my cousin's wedding.

The hall was big, and there were about three hundred guests. I went there with my family. We had dinner, took photos with the bride and groom, and listened to the speeches. We also watched a short singing performance.

I think it was very noisy for several reasons. The music from the speakers was extremely loud, and the MC kept shouting into the microphone. Also, when people raised their glasses, everyone shouted "cheers" together, and many people were talking at the same time. I had to shout to talk to the person next to me, and I had a headache after the party.

Even though it was noisy, I understand that it's part of the happy atmosphere of a Vietnamese wedding.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a noisy place I went to earlier this year: a wedding hall in Hanoi, where my cousin held her wedding in the spring.

The hall was huge, with around three hundred guests, and I went with my family. We had dinner, took photos with the bride and groom, listened to the speeches and watched a short singing performance.

It was incredibly noisy, for a few reasons. The music blasting from the speakers was deafening, and the MC kept shouting into the microphone. On top of that, every time the guests raised their glasses, the whole room shouted "cheers" at the top of their voices, while dozens of conversations were going on at once. I had to shout just to talk to the person next to me, and I left with a splitting headache.

Still, I understand that the racket is part of the festive atmosphere at a Vietnamese wedding, so I didn't mind too much.

vocab.p: at the top of one's voice

grammar: **Mệnh đề quan hệ "where"** → "a wedding hall, **where** my cousin held her wedding."
**keep + V-ing** → "the MC **kept shouting**."
**every time + mệnh đề** → "**every time** the guests raised their glasses."
**while + mệnh đề** → "while dozens of conversations were going on."

p3.q: What are the bad effects of noise on people?
p3.vi: Tiếng ồn ảnh hưởng xấu gì đến con người?
p3.a6: Noise can make people feel stressed and angry. It can also cause headaches, and in the long term it can damage our hearing. If it's noisy at night, people can't sleep well, so they feel tired the next day. It also makes it hard to focus on studying or working.
p3.a7: Quite a few. Noise raises stress levels, causes headaches and, with long-term exposure, can even damage hearing. It also disrupts sleep, leaving people exhausted the next day, and makes it hard to concentrate at work or school. After the wedding, I had a headache for hours, which is a small example of what constant noise can do.
p3.grammar: *which is a small example of what...* → mệnh đề quan hệ + câu gián tiếp.

p3.q: How can we reduce noise in cities?
p3.vi: Làm thế nào để giảm tiếng ồn trong thành phố?
p3.a6: The government can make rules about noise, for example limiting loud music at night and horn use. Cities can plant more trees and build sound barriers near busy roads. People can also use quieter vehicles, like electric motorbikes. And everyone should be more considerate to others.
p3.a7: It takes both rules and awareness. Authorities can enforce noise limits, especially at night, and restrict unnecessary honking. Planting trees and building sound barriers along busy roads help too, as does switching to quieter electric vehicles. Above all, people need to be considerate, for example by keeping the volume down at parties.
p3.grammar: *as does + N* (đảo ngữ "cũng vậy") → "..., as does switching to electric vehicles."

p3.q: Why do some people like noisy places?
p3.vi: Vì sao một số người thích nơi ồn ào?
p3.a6: Some people enjoy noisy places because they feel excited and full of energy, like at concerts or festivals. They also like being around many people. For some people, noise can also help them forget their worries or feel less lonely.
p3.a7: For many people, noise means energy and excitement, as at concerts, festivals or lively markets. It gives them a sense of being part of something, and for those who live alone, a buzzing place can ease loneliness. Others find that background noise helps them stop overthinking. Personally, I prefer the quiet, but I understand the appeal.
p3.grammar: *as at concerts...* → so sánh ví dụ ngắn gọn.

p3vocab.m: tiếp xúc lâu dài; *damage hearing* = hại thính giác; *disrupt sleep* = làm gián đoạn giấc ngủ; *concentrate* = tập trung.
thực thi giới hạn; *sound barrier* = rào chắn âm; *honk* = bấm còi; *considerate* = biết nghĩ cho người khác.
nhộn nhịp; *ease loneliness* = xoa dịu cô đơn; *overthink* = nghĩ quá nhiều; *the appeal* = sức hấp dẫn.

cards.title: Describe an older person you admire
points: and explain why you admire this person
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: người trong bài là bác Lan, hàng xóm, 62 tuổi, từng là cô giáo tiểu học đã nghỉ hưu, làm tình nguyện dạy chữ miễn phí cho trẻ trong xóm. Bạn thay bằng người thật (ông bà, cô giáo cũ...). Đề này PDF liệt kê ít câu Part 3 nên mình thêm 2 câu mở rộng.

notes.v: Mrs Lan – 62 – retired primary teacher
neighbour – since childhood – taught me to read
free lessons – kids in neighbourhood – gardening
hard-working – patient – kind – never complains – active

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about Mrs Lan, an older person I really admire. She's sixty-two years old and used to be a primary school teacher.

She's my neighbour, and I have known her since I was a child. When I was little, she taught me how to read and write before I started school, so I'm very grateful to her.

Although she retired a few years ago, she's still very active. Every evening she gives free lessons to the children in our neighbourhood, and in her free time she grows vegetables in her small garden.

I admire her because she's hard-working, patient and kind. She never complains about anything, even when she is tired. She shows me that people can still do useful things when they get older. I hope I can be like her in the future.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about Mrs Lan, an older neighbour of mine whom I really look up to. She's sixty-two and used to be a primary school teacher.

I've known her since I was a child. In fact, she taught me to read and write before I even started school, so I owe her a lot.

Even though she retired a few years ago, she hasn't slowed down at all. Every evening she gives free lessons to the children in our neighbourhood, and in her spare time she tends a small vegetable garden.

What I admire most is her patience and kindness. She never complains, even when she's exhausted. She's living proof that you can stay useful and contribute to the community well into old age. If I'm half as energetic and generous as she is at her age, I'll be very happy.
grammar: **used to + V** → "used to be a primary school teacher."
**whom/who** → "a neighbour **whom** I look up to."
**Present perfect** → "I've known her since I was a child."
**If + hiện tại, will** → "If I'm half as energetic..., I'll be happy."

p3.q: Do old people in your country usually live with their children?
p3.vi: Người già ở nước bạn thường sống chung với con cái không?
p3.a6: Yes, many of them do. In Vietnam, it's traditional for three generations to live in the same house. Children take care of their parents, and grandparents help look after the grandchildren. But now, some young people move to the city for work, so more old people live alone.
p3.a7: Traditionally, yes. It's quite common in Vietnam for three generations to share a roof, with children looking after their elderly parents and grandparents helping with the grandchildren. That said, as more young people move to cities for work, the number of older people living alone is on the rise.
p3.grammar: *with + N + V-ing* → "with children looking after..."

p3.q: What can young people learn from older people?
p3.vi: Người trẻ có thể học gì từ người lớn tuổi?
p3.a6: I think it's good if they want to and are healthy. Working keeps them active and gives them a purpose. They can also earn some extra money. But they shouldn't be forced to work if they are tired.
p3.a7: It can be, provided it's their choice. Staying active gives them a sense of purpose, keeps their minds sharp and supplements their pension. However, nobody should feel pressured to work if their health no longer allows it.
p3.grammar: *provided (that) + mệnh đề* → điều kiện.

p3vocab.m: sống chung nhà; *three generations* = ba thế hệ; *on the rise* = đang tăng; *look after* = chăm sóc.
sức bền bỉ; *setback* = trở ngại; *by example* = bằng hành động; *a link to* = cầu nối với.
ăn sâu; *give up one's seat* = nhường ghế; *elders* = người lớn tuổi; *exception* = ngoại lệ.
cảm giác có mục đích; *keep one's mind sharp* = giữ đầu óc minh mẫn; *supplement* = bổ sung; *pension* = lương hưu.

cards.title: Describe an activity that you think is a waste of time
points: and explain why you think it is a waste of time
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: hoạt động là lướt mạng xã hội (TikTok/Facebook) vô định trước khi ngủ. Rất đời thường với người đi làm. Đề này PDF liệt kê ít câu Part 3 nên mình thêm 2 câu mở rộng.

notes.v: scrolling social media – TikTok, Facebook
before bed – on the bus – 1–2 hours
alone – phone
no value – forget time – sleep late – tired – eyes hurt

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about scrolling through social media, which I think is a waste of time. I mean watching short videos on TikTok and Facebook without any clear purpose.

I usually do it at night before I go to bed, and sometimes on the bus on my way home. I often spend one or two hours on it, which is a lot more than I plan to.

I do it alone, with just my phone. Sometimes I share funny videos with my friends, but mostly I'm on my own.

I think it's a waste of time because I don't learn anything useful from it. I start with "just ten minutes", but then I forget about the time. As a result, I go to bed late, feel tired the next day, and my eyes hurt. I'm trying to cut down, and now I read a book before bed instead.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about mindlessly scrolling through social media, which I honestly consider a waste of time. I'm talking about watching short videos on TikTok and Facebook with no real purpose.

I tend to do it at night before bed, and sometimes on the bus ride home. I often end up spending an hour or two on it, which is far more than I intend.

I do it on my own, just me and my phone, although occasionally I send funny clips to friends.

The reason I see it as a waste of time is that I gain nothing of value from it. I start with "just ten minutes", but I lose track of time completely. The result is that I go to bed late, feel drained the next day and get tired eyes. I'm trying to cut down, and these days I read a book before bed instead, which works much better.
grammar: **Mệnh đề quan hệ chỉ cả câu** → "...an hour or two, **which** is far more than I intend."
**tend to + V** → "I **tend to** do it at night."
**The reason I see it as... is that...** → cấu trúc giải thích.
**spend + thời gian + V-ing** → "spending an hour on it."

p3.q: Do you think it's a waste of time for kids to play computer games?
p3.vi: Trẻ em chơi game có phải lãng phí thời gian không?
p3.a6: It depends. If children play too much, it's a waste of time because it hurts their eyes and their studies. But some games can help them think faster and work in a team. So I think parents should limit the time, not ban games completely.
p3.a7: It depends on how much and what they play. Excessive gaming harms eyesight and schoolwork, but some games build problem-solving skills and teamwork. So rather than banning games outright, parents should set time limits and keep an eye on the content.
p3.grammar: *rather than + V-ing* → "rather than banning games."

p3.q: What do you think people can do to avoid wasting time?
p3.vi: Mọi người có thể làm gì để tránh lãng phí thời gian?
p3.a6: I think yes. We can earn money again, but we can't get lost time back. For example, time with family is very important and we can't buy it. But money is also necessary for life.
p3.a7: In my opinion, yes. Money lost can be earned back, but time can never be recovered. Time with family and friends is something no amount of money can buy. Of course, money is necessary too, so it's about striking a balance.
p3.grammar: *no amount of + N + can + V* → nhấn mạnh.

p3vocab.m: quá mức; *problem-solving skills* = kỹ năng giải quyết vấn đề; *set limits* = đặt giới hạn; *keep an eye on* = để mắt tới.
ưu tiên; *distraction* = sự xao nhãng; *cap* = giới hạn; *rewarding* = đáng giá.
chiếm bớt; *commute* = đi lại đi làm; *default to* = mặc định chọn; *passive entertainment* = giải trí thụ động.
lấy lại; *no amount of money* = bao nhiêu tiền cũng không; *strike a balance* = cân bằng.

cards.title: Describe a crowded place you have been to
points: and explain why it was crowded
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: nơi đông đúc là Phố đi bộ hồ Gươm / khu Phố cổ Hà Nội vào dịp Tết Trung thu. Bạn thay bằng nơi thật (siêu thị dịp Tết, lễ hội...). Đề này PDF không liệt kê Part 3, nên mình thêm 3 câu Part 3 có thể gặp.

notes.v: Old Quarter – Hoan Kiem Lake pedestrian area
Mid-Autumn Festival – weekend evening – with friends
walked – lanterns – street food – photos
festival – tourists – pedestrian zone – narrow streets

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a very crowded place I have been to, which is the Old Quarter around Hoan Kiem Lake in Hanoi. I went there with my friends on a weekend evening during the Mid-Autumn Festival.

We walked around the pedestrian streets, looked at the colourful lanterns, and tried some street food, like grilled sausages and ice cream. We also took many photos.

It was extremely crowded for several reasons. First, it was the festival, so many families and children came to see the lanterns. Second, there were also many foreign tourists. And the streets in the Old Quarter are narrow, so there was not much space to move.

We could only walk very slowly, and sometimes I couldn't see my friends in the crowd. It was tiring, but the atmosphere was lively and fun, so I enjoyed it.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a seriously crowded place I visited: the Old Quarter around Hoan Kiem Lake in Hanoi. I went there with a few friends on a weekend evening during the Mid-Autumn Festival.

We strolled around the pedestrian streets, admired the colourful lanterns and sampled some street food, like grilled sausages and ice cream. Naturally, we took plenty of photos too.

It was packed for several reasons. For one thing, it was the festival, so families with children had come out in force to see the lanterns. On top of that, the area is a magnet for foreign tourists, and the streets are narrow, so there was barely any room to move.

We could only shuffle along, and at one point I lost sight of my friends in the crowd. It was exhausting, but the atmosphere was so lively that I wouldn't have missed it.
grammar: **For one thing... On top of that...** → liệt kê lý do.
**so + kết quả** → "narrow, so there was barely any room."
**Quá khứ hoàn thành** → "families **had come** out in force."
**wouldn't have missed it** → điều kiện loại 3 rút gọn.

p3.q: Why do people like going to crowded places?
p3.vi: Vì sao mọi người thích đến nơi đông đúc?
p3.a6: Many people enjoy the lively atmosphere. They feel excited and part of the event, like at festivals or concerts. Crowded places also have more activities, shops and food. And going with friends makes it more fun.
p3.a7: For many, the buzz is the whole point. Crowds create an energetic atmosphere and a feeling of being part of something bigger, as at festivals and concerts. Busy places also tend to offer more food, shops and entertainment, and sharing the experience with friends makes it even more memorable.
p3.grammar: *as at festivals* → ví dụ rút gọn.

p3.q: What problems can crowded places cause?
p3.vi: Nơi đông đúc gây ra vấn đề gì?
p3.a6: They can be unsafe because it's easy to have accidents or for thieves to steal things. It's also easy to get lost, especially for children. People also feel tired and stressed, and sometimes there is a lot of rubbish.
p3.a7: Safety is the biggest concern: overcrowding can lead to accidents or stampedes, and pickpockets thrive in crowds. It's also easy for children to get separated from their parents. On top of that, crowds generate a lot of litter and noise, which stresses both visitors and local residents.
p3.grammar: *lead to + N* → "overcrowding can lead to accidents."

p3.q: How can the government deal with overcrowding in public places?
p3.vi: Chính phủ xử lý tình trạng quá tải ở nơi công cộng thế nào?
p3.a6: They can limit the number of visitors, for example by selling tickets online. They can also organise events in more places so that people don't gather in one area. More police and clear signs would also help keep people safe.
p3.a7: Authorities can cap visitor numbers through online ticketing and spread events across several venues to avoid concentrating everyone in one spot. Better public transport and clearer signage would help manage the flow, and a visible police presence at big events would keep people safe.
p3.grammar: *so that + mệnh đề* → mục đích.

p3vocab.m: sự náo nhiệt; *the whole point* = mục đích chính; *a sense of belonging* = cảm giác thuộc về; *memorable* = đáng nhớ.
giẫm đạp; *pickpocket* = móc túi; *get separated* = bị lạc nhau; *litter* = rác thải.
giới hạn số lượng; *venue* = địa điểm; *signage* = biển chỉ dẫn; *manage the flow* = điều tiết dòng người.

cards.title: Describe a time when you received good service in a shop/store
points: and explain why you think it was good service
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: cửa hàng là cửa hàng điện thoại/laptop nơi bạn mua tai nghe, nhân viên tư vấn rất tận tình. Bạn thay bằng trải nghiệm thật (cửa hàng mỹ phẩm, quán cà phê...). Đề này PDF liệt kê ít câu Part 3 nên mình thêm 2 câu mở rộng.

notes.v: two months ago – electronics shop – Cau Giay
wireless headphones – budget ~1 million VND
staff friendly – asked needs – let me try – no pressure – discount
patient – honest – recommended cheaper one – I'll go back

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a time I received really good service in an electronics shop in Cau Giay, Hanoi, about two months ago.

I went there to buy a pair of wireless headphones, because my old ones were broken. I only had about one million dong, so I was worried I couldn't find a good pair.

The salesperson was very friendly and patient. First, she asked me how I would use the headphones. Then she showed me three models and let me try each of them. She didn't pressure me to buy anything. In the end, she recommended a cheaper pair that was perfect for me, and she even gave me a small discount.

I think it was good service because she was honest and helpful. She cared about what I needed, not only about selling. Now I'm very happy with the headphones, and I plan to go back to that shop.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a time I received excellent service at an electronics shop in Cau Giay, Hanoi, about two months ago.

I'd gone there to buy a pair of wireless headphones because my old ones had given up the ghost. My budget was only around a million dong, so I was worried I wouldn't find anything decent.

The salesperson couldn't have been more helpful. She began by asking how I'd be using the headphones, then showed me three models and let me test each one. There was no pressure to buy whatsoever. In the end, she steered me towards a cheaper pair that suited me perfectly, and even knocked a little off the price.

What made it good service was her honesty: she was clearly more interested in meeting my needs than in making a quick sale. I'm delighted with the headphones, and I'll definitely go back to that shop.
grammar: **Quá khứ hoàn thành** → "I'd gone there to buy..." (đi trước câu chuyện).
**couldn't have been more + adj** → cấu trúc nhấn mạnh.
**more interested in A than in B** → so sánh.
**Mệnh đề "that"** → "a cheaper pair **that** suited me."

p3.q: How can shops provide good service to customers?
p3.vi: Cửa hàng có thể cung cấp dịch vụ tốt cho khách bằng cách nào?
p3.a6: They should train their staff to be polite and patient. Staff should listen to customers and give honest advice. Shops can also offer free delivery, easy returns and discounts for regular customers. A clean and tidy shop is also important.
p3.a7: It starts with well-trained staff who are polite, attentive and honest in their advice, as the salesperson was in my case. Beyond that, shops can offer easy returns, free delivery and loyalty discounts, and keep the store clean and well laid out so that customers can browse comfortably.
p3.grammar: *as + S + was* → so sánh với ví dụ.

p3.q: Why do some shop assistants not provide good service?
p3.vi: Vì sao một số nhân viên không phục vụ tốt?
p3.a6: I like both. Online shopping is convenient and often cheaper, so I use it for clothes and small things. But for electronics, I prefer shops because I can try the products and get advice from staff.
p3.a7: It depends on what I'm buying. For everyday items, online shopping is quicker and often cheaper, but for things like electronics I prefer a physical shop, where I can test the product and get advice from staff, as I did with my headphones.
p3.grammar: *where + mệnh đề* → "a physical shop, where I can test..."

p3vocab.m: chu đáo; *loyalty discount* = ưu đãi khách thân thiết; *browse* = xem lướt; *well laid out* = bố trí hợp lý.
mất động lực; *lack of training* = thiếu đào tạo; *prioritise* = ưu tiên; *incentive* = động lực.
quan hệ hai chiều; *go the extra mile* = làm nhiều hơn yêu cầu; *rudeness* = sự thô lỗ; *miserable* = khổ sở.
cửa hàng thực tế; *test the product* = dùng thử sản phẩm; *convenient* = tiện lợi; *everyday items* = đồ dùng hằng ngày.

cards.title: Describe a city you have visited and would like to visit again
points: and explain why you would like to visit it again
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: thành phố là Đà Nẵng, bạn đi cùng công ty (team building) hoặc bạn bè năm ngoái. Bạn thay bằng nơi thật (Đà Lạt, Huế, Hội An...). Đề này PDF liệt kê ít câu Part 3 nên mình thêm 2 câu mở rộng.

notes.v: Da Nang – central Vietnam
last summer – 4 days – with colleagues
My Khe beach – Ba Na Hills – Golden Bridge – seafood – Hoi An
clean – friendly – too short – want to see Son Tra, Marble Mountains

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about Da Nang, a city in central Vietnam that I visited and would like to go to again. I went there last summer with my colleagues for a four-day trip.

We spent a lot of time on My Khe beach, and we visited Ba Na Hills, where we took photos on the Golden Bridge. We also ate delicious seafood and visited the old town of Hoi An, which is not far from Da Nang.

I would like to visit it again for several reasons. First, the city is very clean and beautiful, and the people are friendly. Second, the trip was too short, so we didn't have time to see everything. I still want to visit Son Tra Peninsula and the Marble Mountains. I hope to go back next year with my family.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about Da Nang, a coastal city in central Vietnam that I'd love to revisit. I went there last summer with my colleagues for a four-day trip.

We spent a lot of time on My Khe beach and visited Ba Na Hills, where we took photos on the famous Golden Bridge. We also tucked into plenty of fresh seafood and took a day trip to the ancient town of Hoi An, which isn't far away.

There are a couple of reasons I'd like to go back. For one thing, the city is spotless and scenic, and the locals are warm and welcoming. For another, four days wasn't nearly enough, so we missed out on places like Son Tra Peninsula and the Marble Mountains. I'm hoping to return next year with my family, so I can take my time and see it all properly.
grammar: **Mệnh đề "where"** → "Ba Na Hills, **where** we took photos."
**For one thing... For another...** → liệt kê lý do.
**wasn't nearly enough** → nhấn mạnh "chưa đủ".
**I'm hoping to + V** → dự định gần.

p3.q: Why do people like to visit cities?
p3.vi: Vì sao mọi người thích đến các thành phố?
p3.a6: Cities have many things to see and do, like museums, shopping malls and restaurants. They also have modern buildings and convenient transport. For many people, visiting a city is a chance to try new food and learn about the local culture.
p3.a7: Cities offer a wide range of attractions in one place: museums, shopping, nightlife and a diverse food scene. They're also well connected, so they're easy to get around. For many people, a city break is a chance to experience local culture and take a break from their routine.
p3.grammar: *easy to + V* → "easy to get around."

p3.q: Do you think it's better to travel alone or with others?
p3.vi: Đi du lịch một mình hay đi cùng người khác tốt hơn?
p3.a6: I prefer travelling with others. It's more fun and safer, and we can share the cost. Also, we can help each other if there is a problem. But travelling alone gives more freedom, so some people like it.
p3.a7: Personally, I prefer travelling in company. It's more fun, safer and cheaper, as you can split costs, like on my Da Nang trip. Solo travel offers more freedom and flexibility, though, so it suits people who like to do things at their own pace.
p3.grammar: *though* ở cuối câu → nhượng bộ nhẹ.

p3.q: What are the advantages of tourism for a city?
p3.vi: Du lịch mang lại lợi ích gì cho một thành phố?
p3.a6: I'd like to live in a big city because there are more jobs and more entertainment. But big cities are also noisy and expensive. My home is in the suburbs now, and it's a good balance.
p3.a7: I'd choose a big city for the job opportunities and the amenities, though I'd miss the quiet of a small town. Living on the outskirts, as I do now, is a good compromise: I get the calm at home and the city's convenience when I need it.
p3.grammar: *as I do now* → so sánh mệnh đề rút gọn.

p3vocab.m: đa dạng; *food scene* = ẩm thực; *well connected* = giao thông thuận tiện; *city break* = kỳ nghỉ ngắn ở thành phố.
chia chi phí; *in company* = có bạn đồng hành; *flexibility* = sự linh hoạt; *at one's own pace* = theo nhịp độ riêng.
thúc đẩy kinh tế; *tax revenue* = nguồn thu thuế; *infrastructure* = hạ tầng; *raise the profile* = nâng tầm.
du lịch quá tải; *congestion* = ùn tắc; *push up prices* = đẩy giá lên; *commercialised* = thương mại hóa.
tiện ích; *on the outskirts* = ngoại ô; *compromise* = thỏa hiệp; *job opportunities* = cơ hội việc làm.

cards.title: Describe a place where you listened to music that you did not like
points: what kind of music you listened to
and explain why you did not like it
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: nơi trong bài là quán cà phê gần công ty, nơi bật nhạc EDM/nhạc remix quá to. Bạn thay bằng nơi thật (nhà hàng, xe bus, siêu thị...). Đề này PDF liệt kê ít câu Part 3 nên mình thêm 2 câu mở rộng.

notes.v: café near my company – Cau Giay
last month – lunch break – with colleagues
loud EDM / remix – fast – heavy bass
too loud – couldn't talk – headache – prefer soft pop/ballad

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a café near my company in Hanoi, where I listened to music I really didn't like.

I went there last month during my lunch break with some colleagues. We wanted a quiet place to relax and talk before going back to work.

Unfortunately, the café was playing very loud electronic dance music, with fast rhythms and heavy bass. It sounded like a nightclub, not a café.

I didn't like it for two reasons. First, the music was too loud, so we had to shout to talk to each other. Second, I prefer soft music, like pop songs or ballads, which makes me feel relaxed. After half an hour, I had a headache, so we left early and had our drinks somewhere else. I won't go back to that café.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a café near my company in Hanoi, where I once had to put up with music I really couldn't stand.

It was last month, during my lunch break. A few colleagues and I were hoping for somewhere quiet to unwind before heading back to work.

Unfortunately, the café was blasting electronic dance music, with a fast tempo and heavy bass. It felt more like a nightclub than a café.

There were two reasons I disliked it. For a start, the volume was so high that we had to raise our voices just to hold a conversation. Secondly, it's simply not my taste: I prefer gentle pop songs and ballads, which help me relax. After half an hour, I had a pounding headache, so we cut our visit short and finished our drinks elsewhere. Needless to say, I won't be going back.
grammar: **Mệnh đề "where"** → "a café..., **where** I once had to put up with music."
**more like A than B** → "more like a nightclub than a café."
**so + adj + that + mệnh đề** → "so high that we had to raise our voices."
**Needless to say,...** → cụm kết luận.

p3.q: Do you think music is important in people's lives?
p3.vi: Âm nhạc có quan trọng trong cuộc sống không?
p3.a6: Yes, I think it is. Music helps people relax and feel better when they are stressed. It can also bring people together, for example at concerts or parties. Many people listen to music every day, on the bus or while working.
p3.a7: Definitely. Music is a great stress-reliever and a powerful mood booster, and it brings people together at concerts, festivals and parties. For many, it's part of the daily routine, whether they're commuting or working. I often listen to ballads on the bus, which makes the long ride much more bearable.
p3.grammar: *whether + S + V or V* → "whether they're commuting or working."

p3.q: What kind of music do young people like today?
p3.vi: Giới trẻ ngày nay thích loại nhạc nào?
p3.a6: Many young people like pop, rap and electronic music because they are modern and energetic. K-pop is also very popular in Vietnam. They often find new songs on TikTok and YouTube, so trends change very fast.
p3.a7: Mostly pop, rap and electronic dance music, because they're upbeat and catchy. K-pop is hugely popular in Vietnam, too. Social media like TikTok plays a big role in spreading new songs, so musical trends come and go very quickly.
p3.grammar: *so + mệnh đề* → kết quả.

p3.q: Is it good to play music in public places?
p3.vi: Phát nhạc ở nơi công cộng có tốt không?
p3.a6: Yes, a lot. In the past, people bought CDs or listened to the radio. Now most people use their phones and apps like Spotify or YouTube. It's cheaper and more convenient, because they can listen anywhere.
p3.a7: Hugely. People used to buy CDs or tune in to the radio, but now streaming apps like Spotify and YouTube put millions of songs in our pockets. It's cheaper and more convenient, though it means we rarely listen to a whole album any more.
p3.grammar: *used to + V... but now...* → so sánh quá khứ - hiện tại.

p3vocab.m: thứ giải tỏa căng thẳng; *mood booster* = thứ nâng tâm trạng; *bearable* = chịu được; *bring people together* = gắn kết mọi người.
sôi động; *catchy* = dễ nhớ; *come and go* = đến rồi đi; *play a big role in* = đóng vai trò lớn.
không khí; *nuisance* = sự phiền toái; *background music* = nhạc nền; *reasonable* = vừa phải.
ở mức độ nào đó; *gravitate towards* = nghiêng về; *hard-and-fast rule* = quy tắc cứng nhắc; *outgoing* = hướng ngoại.
bật nghe; *streaming* = phát trực tuyến; *a whole album* = nguyên album; *used to + V* = từng.

cards.title: Describe an experience that you were proud of
points: and explain why you were proud of it
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: trải nghiệm là thi đậu chứng chỉ ISTQB Foundation (kiểm thử phần mềm) sau 3 tháng ôn cùng 2 đồng nghiệp. Hợp nghề IT Tester của bạn. Bạn thay bằng chuyện thật.

notes.v: passed ISTQB exam – software testing certificate
last year – exam centre in Hanoi – studied 3 months
2 colleagues – study group – exam alone
hard – studied after work – almost gave up – parents happy – confidence

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about the time I passed an international exam for software testers, called ISTQB. I'm very proud of it.

It happened last year. I studied for three months, and then I took the exam at a test centre in Hanoi. I studied with two colleagues from my company. We met after work twice a week and helped each other with difficult parts. On the exam day, of course, I had to work alone.

I was proud of it for several reasons. First, the exam was difficult, and I had to study after a long day at work. Sometimes I was so tired that I wanted to give up. Second, when I saw my result, I felt really happy, and my parents were also proud of me. After that, I felt more confident about my career.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about the day I passed an international certification for software testers, known as ISTQB, which I'm still very proud of.

It happened last year. I spent three months preparing, and then took the exam at a test centre in Hanoi. I prepared alongside two colleagues from my company: we met twice a week after work and helped one another with the trickier topics. On the day itself, of course, I was on my own.

There are a couple of reasons I'm proud of it. For one thing, it was tough: I had to study after exhausting days at work, and there were times I was on the verge of giving up. For another, when I saw the word "Passed" on the screen, I was over the moon, and my parents were delighted too. It also gave me a real confidence boost, because it proved that I could stick with a goal until the end.
grammar: **Quá khứ đơn kể chuyện** → "I spent..., I took..."
**for one thing... for another...** → liệt kê lý do.
**so + adj + that** → "so tired that I wanted to give up."
**Mệnh đề quan hệ "which"** → "..., which I'm still very proud of."

p3.q: What kinds of achievements make people feel proud?
p3.a6: Many things can, such as passing an exam, getting a good job or finishing a hard project. People also feel proud when they help others or reach a personal goal.
p3.a7: Anything that took real effort: academic or career milestones, overcoming a personal challenge, or helping others. Often it's not the size of the achievement but the struggle behind it.

p3.q: Do young people feel proud of the same things as older people?
p3.a6: Not always. Young people often feel proud of study results, new skills or online success. Older people are more proud of their family, their children and a stable life.
p3.a7: Not entirely. Younger people tend to take pride in personal achievements such as grades, skills or career progress, whereas older people often take more pride in their family and in providing a stable home.

p3.q: Is it important for parents to praise their children?
p3.a6: Yes, it is. Praise makes children feel confident and want to try more. But parents should praise effort, not only good marks, and not too much.
p3.a7: Yes, within reason. Praise builds self-esteem and motivation, but it should recognise effort rather than just results, otherwise children may become afraid of failure.

p3.q: Why do some people find it difficult to accept praise?
p3.a6: Some people are shy or modest, so they feel uncomfortable. In Vietnamese culture, people are taught to be humble, so they often say "no, it's nothing". Others don't believe they deserve it.
p3.a7: Partly because of modesty: in Vietnamese culture we're taught to stay humble, so we tend to brush compliments off. Others suffer from low self-confidence and feel they don't deserve the praise.

p3.q: Do you think people should be proud of their achievements?
p3.a6: Yes, they should. Being proud gives motivation to continue. But they shouldn't show off, because it can annoy others.
p3.a7: Yes, a healthy sense of pride motivates us to keep going. The key is to stay modest and not boast.

p3.q: Is it better to be proud of yourself or to receive recognition from others?
p3.a6: I think being proud of yourself is better, because it's real and lasts longer. Recognition from others is nice, but you can't always get it.
p3.a7: Self-pride is more meaningful and lasting, since it doesn't depend on others. Recognition is a pleasant bonus, but relying on it can leave you disappointed.

p3.q: Can being too proud of yourself have negative effects?
p3.a6: Yes. People who are too proud may become arrogant and stop learning. They may also lose friends because they look down on others.
p3.a7: Certainly. Excessive pride can turn into arrogance, making people stop learning and look down on others, which damages relationships.

p3.q: What can people learn from experiences that make them proud?
p3.a6: They learn that hard work pays off. They also learn about their strengths and become more confident. It also makes them want to set new goals, like me after the ISTQB exam.
p3.a7: That perseverance pays off, and what their strengths are. Such experiences build confidence and encourage people to set higher goals, as passing the ISTQB exam did for me.

p3vocab.m: cột mốc; *overcome a challenge* = vượt qua thử thách.
tự hào về; *a stable life* = cuộc sống ổn định.
lòng tự trọng; *within reason* = vừa phải.
gạt đi; *humble* = khiêm tốn.
khoe khoang; *show off* = khoe.
sự công nhận; *a pleasant bonus* = phần thưởng thêm.
kiêu ngạo; *look down on* = coi thường.
sự kiên trì; *pay off* = được đền đáp.
