p3.q: How easy is it to find a place to live in your country?
p3.a6: It depends on the city. In small towns, it's easy. But in big cities like Hanoi, it's difficult to find a good place with a reasonable price, because there are many people and the price is high.
p3.a7: It varies. In small towns it's straightforward, but in big cities like Hanoi, finding a decent place at a reasonable price is tough, as demand far outstrips supply.

p3.q: Do you think it's better to rent or to buy a place to live in?
p3.a6: I think buying is better in the long term, because the house is yours and you feel safe. But renting is more flexible and cheaper at first, so it is good for young people.
p3.a7: In the long run, buying is a sound investment and gives you security. However, renting offers flexibility and lower upfront costs, which suits young people who may change jobs or cities.

p3.q: What are some of the pleasures involved in making a home for ourselves?
p3.a6: We can decorate it in our own style and feel comfortable. It's also a place for family and for relaxing. We feel proud of what we have made.
p3.a7: Personalising your space to suit your taste, creating a cosy refuge for the family and the pride of having built it yourself.

p3.q: Why are there more and more tall buildings in big cities?
p3.a6: Land is expensive and there are many people, so cities build upwards to save space. Tall buildings also give more offices and homes in a small area.
p3.a7: Because land is scarce and expensive and populations are growing, cities build upwards to accommodate more homes and offices in a limited area.

p3.q: What are the disadvantages of living in tall apartment buildings?
p3.a6: There can be problems with lifts, noise and fire safety. People also have less contact with neighbours and no garden for children to play.
p3.a7: Lift breakdowns, noise, fire-safety concerns and a weaker sense of community, plus a lack of outdoor space for children.

p3vocab.m: cầu vượt cung; *straightforward* = dễ dàng.
chi phí ban đầu; *a sound investment* = khoản đầu tư an toàn.
cá nhân hóa; *refuge* = nơi nương náu.
khan hiếm; *accommodate* = chứa được.
an toàn cháy nổ; *sense of community* = tinh thần cộng đồng.

cards.title: Describe a boring place
points: and explain why you think it is a boring place
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: nơi chán là trung tâm thương mại, bạn đi cùng em họ vì em ấy mua sắm hàng giờ liền. Rất đời thường và không chê một nơi cụ thể. Bạn thay bằng nơi thật.

notes.v: big shopping mall – Hanoi – weekend
my female cousin
walked – waited outside fitting rooms – held bags – cafe
not a shopper – same shops – crowded, noisy – waited 3 hours

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a boring place, which is a big shopping mall in Hanoi. I went there last month at the weekend with my cousin.

She wanted to buy some clothes, so we visited many shops. I walked behind her, carried her bags, and waited outside the fitting rooms. We also had a drink at a café, but then she continued shopping. In total, we stayed there for about three hours.

I think it's a boring place for me for several reasons. First, I'm not a shopping person, so I'm not interested in clothes. Second, all the shops look similar, and the mall is crowded and noisy. I felt tired, and I kept looking at my phone. I'd prefer to go to a quiet café or a park. I'll never go shopping with my cousin again!
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a place I find terribly boring: a big shopping mall in Hanoi. I went there last month at the weekend with my cousin.

She wanted to buy some clothes, so we trailed from one shop to the next. I followed her around, carrying her bags and waiting outside the fitting rooms. We stopped for a drink at a café, but then she carried on shopping, and we ended up staying for about three hours.

I find it dull for a few reasons. For one thing, I'm not really into shopping, and clothes don't interest me much. For another, every shop looks the same, and the mall was packed and noisy. I felt drained, and I kept checking my phone. I'd much rather spend my weekend at a quiet café or in a park, so I think I'll politely decline next time!

vocab.p: trail from one shop to the next
vocab.m: lẽo đẽo hết cửa hàng này đến cửa hàng khác

grammar: **end up + V-ing** → "we ended up staying."
**keep + V-ing** → "I kept checking my phone."
**would much rather + V** → "I'd much rather spend..."
**find + O + adj** → "I find it dull."

p3.q: Why do some people get bored easily?
p3.a6: Some people are very active and need new things all the time. Others have too many entertainment choices, like phones, so they lose interest quickly.
p3.a7: Some have restless personalities and crave constant stimulation, and others have grown used to instant entertainment on their phones, so they lose interest quickly.

p3.q: What kinds of places do young people enjoy visiting?
p3.a6: They like shopping malls, cafés, cinemas, parks and places for taking photos. They also like places with music and many friends.
p3.a7: Trendy cafés, shopping malls, cinemas, amusement parks and photogenic spots, essentially anywhere they can hang out with friends and post on social media.

p3.q: Do people have different ideas of what is interesting?
p3.a6: Yes, of course. It depends on interests and age. For example, my cousin loves shopping but I find it boring, and I like quiet places.
p3.a7: Certainly. It depends on personality, age and interests: my cousin loves shopping malls, whereas I'd rather be somewhere quiet.

p3.q: How can tourist attractions become more appealing?
p3.a6: They can add activities and good services, such as guides and clean toilets. They can also use technology, like apps and videos, and hold festivals.
p3.a7: By offering interactive experiences, better facilities and knowledgeable guides, using technology such as apps and virtual tours, and hosting events throughout the year.

p3.q: Is it important to try new experiences?
p3.a6: Yes, it is. New experiences help us learn and become more confident. We also discover new interests. But we should be careful and safe.
p3.a7: Yes, they broaden our horizons, build confidence and help us discover hidden interests, provided we stay safe.

p3.q: Do people today have less patience than in the past?
p3.a6: I think so. We are used to fast internet and fast delivery, so we don't want to wait. People get angry quickly in traffic or when they wait in a line.
p3.a7: I believe so. With instant messaging, fast delivery and quick answers online, many of us have lost the habit of waiting, which shows in traffic or queues.

p3vocab.m: không yên; *stimulation* = sự kích thích.
ăn ảnh; *hang out* = đi chơi.
tính cách; *whereas* = trong khi.
tương tác; *facilities* = tiện nghi.
mở rộng tầm mắt; *hidden interest* = sở thích tiềm ẩn.
thỏa mãn tức thì; *queue* = hàng chờ.

cards.title: Describe a plan that you had to change recently
points: what made you change the plan
and how you felt about the change
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: kế hoạch là chuyến đi Sa Pa cuối tuần cùng bạn bè bị hủy vì dự báo bão và mưa lớn; thay bằng ở Hà Nội ăn lẩu và xem phim. Bạn thay bằng chuyện thật.

notes.v: last month – long weekend – planned trip to Sa Pa
storm warning – heavy rain – landslides – unsafe
stay in Hanoi – hotpot – movie – café
disappointed – but safe – surprisingly fun – relaxed

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a plan that I had to change recently. It happened last month, during a long weekend.

My friends and I planned a trip to Sa Pa. We had booked the hotel and bought the bus tickets. But two days before the trip, there was a storm warning, and the weather forecast said there would be heavy rain and landslides in the mountains. It was not safe, so we decided to cancel the trip.

Our new plan was to stay in Hanoi. On Saturday, we had hotpot at a restaurant and then watched a movie. On Sunday, we went to a café and talked all afternoon.

At first, I felt very disappointed because I had looked forward to the trip. But then I felt happy that we were safe, and the weekend was surprisingly fun and relaxing.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a plan I had to change recently. It happened last month, over a long weekend.

A few friends and I had planned a trip to Sa Pa, and we'd already booked the hotel and bought the bus tickets. But two days before we were due to leave, a storm warning was issued, and the forecast predicted heavy rain and landslides in the mountains. It simply wasn't safe, so we reluctantly called the trip off.

Instead, we stayed in Hanoi. On Saturday, we had hotpot and then watched a film, and on Sunday we spent the afternoon chatting in a café.

I was bitterly disappointed at first, as I'd been looking forward to the trip for weeks. But I soon felt relieved that we'd stayed safe, and the weekend turned out to be surprisingly fun and relaxing. It was a blessing in disguise.

p3.q: Why do people sometimes change their plans?
p3.a6: Because of bad weather, illness, work or money problems. Sometimes they also get a better idea or a better chance.
p3.a7: Owing to unforeseen circumstances such as bad weather, illness or work emergencies, or because a better opportunity comes along.

p3.q: Is it important to be flexible in life?
p3.a6: Yes, it is. Life is not always the same as our plan. If we are flexible, we can solve problems easily and feel less stressed.
p3.a7: Very. Life rarely goes to plan, so flexibility helps us adapt, solve problems and stay calm.

p3.q: Do young people change plans more often than older people?
p3.a6: I think yes. Young people are more spontaneous and have fewer responsibilities. Older people have families and work, so they plan more carefully.
p3.a7: Probably. Young people tend to be more spontaneous and less tied down, whereas older people have family and work commitments that make them plan carefully.

p3.q: How do people feel when their plans suddenly change?
p3.a6: Most feel disappointed, stressed or angry at first. But some people can accept it quickly and find a new plan, like me.
p3.a7: Typically frustrated or anxious at first, though those who are adaptable soon move on and make the best of it.

p3.q: Can changing plans sometimes lead to better results?
p3.a6: Yes, it can. When we change the plan, we may find something better. For example, my trip was cancelled, but I had a very relaxing weekend.
p3.a7: Definitely. Sometimes the new plan beats the original, as my cancelled trip showed: the quiet weekend at home was exactly what I needed.

p3.q: How can people deal with unexpected changes?
p3.a6: They should stay calm and think about the reasons. It's good to have a backup plan, and to ask friends or family for help.
p3.a7: Stay calm, assess the situation, keep a backup plan ready and talk to others for support.

thích nghi; *go to plan* = đúng kế hoạch.
tùy hứng; *commitment* = trách nhiệm.
bực bội; *make the best of it* = tận dụng tối đa.

cards.title: A new law you would like to introduce in your country
points: whether the new law will be popular
how you came up with the new law
and explain how you feel about this new law
cards.note: Lưu ý quan trọng: Part 3 của đề này trong PDF là 3 câu y hệt đề 38 (chụp ảnh khi du lịch, travel journals, yếu tố ảnh hưởng cảm nhận về chuyến đi), rõ ràng bị chép nhầm. Những câu đó mình đã trả lời ở file đề 38, nên ở đây mình viết 5 câu Part 3 bám sát chủ đề luật pháp (giám khảo thật sự sẽ hỏi kiểu này).

notes.v: limit overtime – fair pay – punish companies
less overtime – healthier – more time for family – better productivity
employees yes – some employers no – small companies difficult
friends in IT work late – tired – my own experience
hopeful – fair – but needs strict checking

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a law that I would like to introduce. It's a law that limits overtime and makes sure employees are paid fairly if they work extra hours.

If this law existed, companies could not force people to work too many extra hours. People would have more time for their family and health, and they would be happier and more productive at work.

I think most employees would like this law. Some employers might not, because they have to pay more or hire more staff. Small companies may find it difficult.

I came up with this idea from my own experience. Many of my friends in IT often work late at night and at weekends before deadlines, and they feel very tired. I feel hopeful about this law, but I think the government has to check carefully, otherwise companies will not follow it.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a law I'd love to see introduced: one that sets stricter limits on overtime and guarantees fair pay for any extra hours worked.

If it existed, companies couldn't pressure employees into working excessive extra hours. People would have more time for family and health, and they'd be happier and more productive at work.

I think most employees would welcome it. Some employers might object, since they'd have to pay more or recruit extra staff, and small companies might struggle.

The idea came from personal experience. Many of my friends in IT regularly work late at night and at weekends before deadlines, and they end up exhausted. I feel optimistic about such a law, but only if it's strictly enforced. Otherwise, companies will simply find ways around it.

vocab.m: cân bằng công việc - cuộc sống

grammar: **Điều kiện loại 2** → "If it existed, companies **couldn't**..., people **would** have..."
**only if** → "only if it's strictly enforced."
**Otherwise + mệnh đề** → "Otherwise, companies will find ways around it."
**end up + adj** → "they end up exhausted."

p3.q: Why do governments make new laws?
p3.a6: To protect people and keep society in order. When society changes, for example with new technology, old laws are not enough, so new laws are needed.
p3.a7: To protect citizens, maintain order and respond to social change. As technology and society evolve, existing laws can become outdated.

p3.q: Do people always obey the law?
p3.a6: No, not always. Some people think they won't be caught, or the punishment is too light. Some people also don't understand the law.
p3.a7: Unfortunately not. Some break rules because they expect to get away with it, the penalties are weak or they simply don't know the rules.

p3.q: What can the government do to make people follow new laws?
p3.a6: They should explain the laws clearly through TV and social media. They should also check regularly and punish people who break them, but fairly.
p3.a7: Run public awareness campaigns, apply penalties consistently and make the rules easy to comply with.

p3.q: Are there any laws in your country that you think are not necessary?
p3.a6: I can't think of a law that is unnecessary, but I think some laws are not enforced well, for example about traffic. I think the problem is not the law but how it is applied.
p3.a7: I wouldn't say any are unnecessary, but some, such as traffic regulations, are poorly enforced. The problem lies less in the law than in how it's applied.

p3.q: Should the public be involved in making laws?
p3.a6: Yes, I think so. Ordinary people understand the real problems, so they can give good ideas. The government can ask for opinions online before it makes a law.
p3.a7: Yes. Ordinary citizens understand real-life problems, so public consultation produces more practical laws and boosts public support.

p3vocab.m: lỗi thời; *evolve* = phát triển.
thoát tội; *penalty* = hình phạt.
chiến dịch nâng cao nhận thức; *consistently* = nhất quán.
thực thi kém; *regulation* = quy định.
lấy ý kiến cộng đồng; *practical* = thiết thực.

cards.title: An important decision that you made
points: what the results of the decision were
and explain why it was important
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: quyết định là nghỉ công ty đầu tiên để chuyển sang công ty hiện tại (môi trường chuyên nghiệp hơn, có khách nước ngoài, học được nhiều hơn). Chủ đề này khác đề 5 (quyết định học IELTS) nên bạn có hai câu chuyện để lựa. Bạn thay bằng quyết định thật.

notes.v: leave first company – join current company
2 months thinking – list pros and cons – asked parents, senior friend
better salary – foreign clients – learn automation – more stressful at first
turning point – career direction – English need

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about an important decision that I made about three years ago. I decided to leave my first company and join my current company.

It was not an easy decision. My first company was small, and I felt comfortable there because my colleagues were friendly. But I was not learning much. I thought about it for two months. I wrote a list of good and bad points, and I asked my parents and a senior friend for advice. In the end, I decided to change.

The results were mostly positive. I have a better salary, and I work with foreign clients. I also learn new tools, like automation testing. At the beginning, it was stressful because everything was new.

It's important because it was a turning point in my career. It also made me realise that I need to improve my English.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about an important decision I made about three years ago: leaving my first company to join my current one.

It wasn't an easy choice. My first company was small, and I felt comfortable there because my colleagues were friendly, but I wasn't learning much. I thought it over for two months, weighed up the pros and cons on paper and asked my parents and a senior friend for advice. In the end, I took the plunge.

The results have been largely positive. My salary is better, I work with foreign clients and I'm picking up new skills such as automation testing. It was stressful at first, as everything was unfamiliar.

It was important because it was a real turning point in my career. It also made me realise how much I need to improve my English, which eventually led me to take up IELTS.

vocab.p: weigh up the pros and cons

grammar: **Quá khứ đơn** → "I made", "I took."
**Present perfect** → "The results have been positive."
**how much + S + V** → "how much I need to improve."
**Mệnh đề quan hệ chỉ cả câu** → "..., which eventually led me to IELTS."

p3.q: What decisions do people usually make in their daily lives?
p3.a6: Small decisions such as what to eat, what to wear and how to travel to work. They also make bigger decisions about money, studying and their jobs.
p3.a7: Mostly minor ones, such as what to eat or wear and which route to take, along with major ones about money, education and careers.

p3.q: Which is easier, making a decision by yourself or making a decision after group discussion?
p3.a6: Deciding by yourself is faster, but it is risky because you may miss something. A group discussion gives more ideas but takes more time, and people may disagree.
p3.a7: Deciding alone is quicker but riskier, as you may overlook something. Group discussion yields more perspectives, though it's slower and can lead to disagreement.

p3.q: Why are many young people unwilling to follow their parents' advice?
p3.a6: Young people want to be independent and make their own choices. They also think their parents are old-fashioned and don't understand modern life.
p3.a7: They crave independence and want to learn from their own mistakes, and some feel their parents' views are old-fashioned and out of touch with modern life.

p3.q: Why would middle-aged people tend to second-guess their own decisions?
p3.a6: Because they have many responsibilities, like family, money and children. A wrong decision can have a big effect, so they worry a lot. They also look back and think about what they could have done differently.
p3.a7: Because the stakes are higher: they have families, mortgages and careers at risk, and they often look back wondering whether they could have chosen differently.

p3vocab.m: nhỏ; *major* = lớn.
bỏ sót; *perspective* = góc nhìn.
lạc hậu; *crave independence* = khao khát độc lập.
nghi ngờ lại quyết định; *the stakes are high* = rủi ro cao.

cards.title: A friend from your childhood
points: where and how you met each other
and explain what made you like him/her
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: người bạn là Quân, hàng xóm cùng ngõ hồi nhỏ, cùng đá bóng và thả diều; hiện vẫn liên lạc qua Zalo. Bạn thay bằng người thật. Part 3 PDF có 4 câu.

notes.v: Quan – same age – neighbour
same lane – primary school – walked to school together
played football – flew kites – caught fish in pond – shared snacks
funny – loyal – generous – shared secrets

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a friend from my childhood, called Quan. He's the same age as me, and he was my neighbour.

We met in the lane near our houses when we were about six years old. After that, we went to the same primary school, and we walked to school together every day.

We often played together after school. We played football in the lane, flew kites in the field and caught small fish in the pond. Sometimes we shared snacks, and we studied together too.

I liked him because he was very funny and always made me laugh. He was also loyal and generous. When I had a problem, he listened and helped me. We told each other many secrets. Now we live in different places, but I still keep in touch with him.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a friend from my childhood, Quan. We're the same age, and he used to live next door.

We met in the lane near our houses when we were about six, and we ended up at the same primary school, walking there together every day.

We spent most afternoons playing together: football in the lane, flying kites in the field and catching tiny fish in the pond. We shared snacks and did our homework side by side.

What I liked about him was his sense of humour. He always had me in stitches. He was also loyal and generous, and whenever I had a problem, he was the first to lend a hand. We told each other all our secrets. These days we live in different places, but we still keep in touch.
grammar: **used to + V** → "he used to live next door."
**whenever + S + V** → "whenever I had a problem."
**the first to + V** → "the first to lend a hand."
**Quá khứ đơn miêu tả thói quen** → "we spent most afternoons playing."

p3.q: Do you still keep in touch with your friends from childhood? Why or why not?
p3.a6: Yes, with some of them, like Quan. We message each other on Zalo and meet at Tet. But with others, I lost contact because we moved to different cities and we are busy.
p3.a7: With a few, yes, like Quan: we chat on Zalo and meet up at Tet. With the rest, I've drifted apart, as we moved to different cities and got caught up in work.

p3.q: What do you think of online social media?
p3.a6: It's useful because we can keep in touch easily and share information. But it takes a lot of time, and sometimes we spend too much time online and talk less to people in real life.
p3.a7: It's a double-edged sword: great for staying in touch and sharing information, but it can eat up our time and weaken real-life interaction.

p3.q: Do you think online social media will replace face-to-face communication?
p3.a6: No, I don't think so. Online chat is convenient, but we can't feel emotions in the same way. For important talks, people still want to meet in person.
p3.a7: I doubt it. Online chat is convenient, but it can't fully convey tone and emotion, so people will still want to meet in person for what matters.

p3.q: How important is childhood friendship to children?
p3.a6: Very important. Friends teach children how to share, cooperate and solve problems. Children also feel happy and safe with friends, so they develop better.
p3.a7: Very. It teaches sharing, cooperation and empathy, and gives children emotional security that supports their development.

p3vocab.m: xa cách dần; *get caught up in* = bận cuốn vào.
con dao hai lưỡi; *eat up time* = ngốn thời gian.
truyền tải cảm xúc; *in person* = trực tiếp.
sự thấu cảm; *emotional security* = cảm giác an toàn tinh thần.

cards.title: A time when you were stuck in a traffic jam for a very long time
points: and explain how you felt in the traffic jam
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: tình huống là chiều thứ Sáu mưa lớn, xe bus của bạn kẹt hơn 2 tiếng trên đường về nhà ở ngoại thành Hà Nội. Rất khớp thực tế của bạn. Part 3 PDF chỉ có 1 câu, mình thêm 5 câu bonus. Bạn thay bằng chuyện thật.

notes.v: Friday evening – last winter – heavy rain
on the bus – main road to suburbs – accident ahead
watched videos – listened to music – chatted with mother – looked out of window
tired, hungry, bored – then calm – late 2 hours

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a time when I was stuck in a traffic jam for a very long time. It happened on a Friday evening last winter, when it was raining heavily.

I was on the bus going home from work, on the main road to my area in the suburbs. There was an accident in front of us, and many people were driving slowly because of the rain, so the bus stopped for a long time.

While waiting, I watched videos on my phone, listened to music and looked out of the window at the rain. I also called my mother to tell her that I would be late.

I felt tired, hungry and bored. At first I was angry, but later I was calm because I knew I couldn't do anything. Finally, I got home two hours later than usual, and my mother had kept some hot food for me.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a time when I got stuck in a really long traffic jam. It was one Friday evening last winter, in heavy rain.

I was on the bus heading home from work along the main road to my area in the suburbs. There had been an accident up ahead, and with the rain, traffic was crawling, so we ended up at a near standstill for ages.

To pass the time, I watched videos, listened to music and gazed out of the window at the rain. I also called my mother to let her know I'd be late.

I felt exhausted, hungry and bored. I was irritated at first, but eventually I resigned myself to it, since there was nothing I could do. In the end, I got home two hours later than usual, and my mother had kept some hot food for me, which made it all feel a little better.

vocab.p: be stuck in a traffic jam

grammar: **Quá khứ hoàn thành** → "There **had been** an accident."
**with + N + mệnh đề** → "with the rain, traffic was crawling."
**I'd be late** → tương lai trong quá khứ.
**since + lý do** → "since there was nothing I could do."

p3.q: Which vehicles are more likely to be in a traffic jam, cars or buses?
p3.a6: I think cars are more likely, because there are many more cars on the road, and they take a lot of space. Buses carry many people, so they are better for reducing traffic. But in Hanoi, buses also get stuck because they have no special lane.
p3.a7: Cars, I'd say, since there are so many of them and each carries only one or two people. Buses are more space-efficient, but in Hanoi they get stuck too, as they often share lanes with everything else.

p3.q: What causes traffic jams in big cities?
p3.a6: Too many vehicles, narrow roads, accidents and bad weather. Rush hour is the worst time. Some people also park in the wrong place.
p3.a7: Too many vehicles for the road capacity, accidents, flooding, roadworks and poor discipline, all peaking at rush hour.

p3.q: How can traffic jams be reduced?
p3.a6: The government can build more metro lines and bus lanes and make public transport better. It can also limit private cars and use smart traffic lights.
p3.a7: By investing in metro lines and dedicated bus lanes, discouraging private vehicles through parking fees, and using smart traffic lights.

p3.q: Do you think public transport in your city is good enough?
p3.a6: It's improving, but not good enough yet. Buses are often late and crowded, and the metro only has a few lines. In my suburb, there are few buses at night.
p3.a7: It's improving, but it still has gaps. Buses are often late and crowded, the metro network is limited and services to the suburbs thin out in the evening.

p3.q: How does traffic affect people's daily lives?
p3.a6: It wastes time and makes people tired and stressed. It also causes air pollution, and people have less time for their family.
p3.a7: It eats into people's time, raises stress levels, worsens air quality and leaves less time for family and rest.

p3.q: Would you like to work from home to avoid traffic?
p3.a6: Yes, sometimes. I'd save travel time and feel less tired. But I also want to go to the office to meet my colleagues, so I'd like a mix of both.
p3.a7: Partly. I'd love to skip the commute a couple of days a week, but I value face-to-face time with colleagues, so a hybrid arrangement would suit me best.

p3vocab.m: tiết kiệm không gian; *share lanes* = chung làn đường.
sức chứa đường; *rush hour* = giờ cao điểm.
làn riêng; *discourage* = hạn chế.
thưa dần; *network* = mạng lưới.
chiếm bớt; *air quality* = chất lượng không khí.
làm việc kết hợp; *skip the commute* = bỏ việc đi lại.

cards.title: A special day out that cost you little money / didn't cost you much
points: and explain how you feel about the day
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: ngày đi chơi là một ngày dạo Hà Nội cùng bạn bè: đạp xe quanh hồ, ăn vặt ở phố cổ, tổng chi khoảng 250.000 đồng. Part 3 PDF chỉ có 1 câu, mình thêm 4 câu bonus. Bạn thay bằng chuyện thật.

notes.v: Sunday last autumn – nice weather – with 3 friends
West Lake – bike – Old Quarter – street food
~250,000 VND – bike rental, street food, iced tea
happy – cheap but memorable – realised fun isn't expensive

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a special day out that didn't cost me much money. It was a Sunday last autumn, and the weather was lovely.

I went out with three friends. In the morning, we rented bikes and cycled around West Lake. Then we went to the Old Quarter, where we walked around the streets and tried many kinds of street food, like grilled rice paper, fried spring rolls and iced tea.

I spent only about two hundred and fifty thousand dong. Most of the money was for renting the bike and for the food. We didn't buy anything else.

I feel very happy about that day. It was cheap but very memorable. I realised that we don't need to spend a lot of money to have a good time, if we go with good friends.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a special day out that cost me very little. It was a Sunday last autumn, and the weather was beautiful.

I went out with three friends. In the morning, we hired bikes and cycled around West Lake. After that, we headed to the Old Quarter, where we wandered the streets and sampled lots of street food: grilled rice paper, fried spring rolls and iced tea.

I spent only about two hundred and fifty thousand dong, mostly on the bike rental and food. We didn't buy anything else.

I look back on that day very fondly. It was cheap, but it was one of the most memorable days I've had. It taught me that you don't need to spend a lot to enjoy yourself, as long as you're in good company.
grammar: **Mệnh đề quan hệ "where"** → "the Old Quarter, **where** we wandered."
**spend + tiền + on + N** → "spent 250,000 on bike rental."
**as long as + mệnh đề** → "as long as you're in good company."
**one of the most + adj + N** → so sánh nhất.

p3.q: How do people spend their leisure time in Vietnam?
p3.a6: Many people meet friends in cafés, eat out, watch films or play sports like football and badminton. Others spend time with their family at home or use social media.
p3.a7: Many meet friends at cafés or eat out, others watch films or play football or badminton, and a lot of people spend their downtime with family or on social media.

p3.q: Do you think people spend too much money on entertainment?
p3.a6: Some people do, especially young people who go to expensive cafés and concerts. I think we should save money for the future and look for cheap activities.
p3.a7: Some do, especially young people who splurge on concerts and trendy cafés. A little moderation and a savings habit would serve them better.

p3.q: What are some free or cheap activities in your city?
p3.a6: You can walk around West Lake, visit parks, go to the walking street near Hoan Kiem Lake or join free festivals. Street food is also cheap.
p3.a7: Strolling around West Lake, visiting parks, the pedestrian streets near Hoan Kiem Lake, festivals and, of course, cheap and delicious street food.

p3.q: Is it more fun to spend leisure time with friends or alone?
p3.a6: I think with friends is more fun because we can share and talk. But sometimes I need time alone to relax, so I like both.
p3.a7: With friends, generally: the shared experience makes it more fun. But I also need some solitude to recharge, so I like a mix.

p3.q: Do people have enough leisure time nowadays?
p3.a6: I don't think so. People work long hours and have to commute, so they are often tired at weekends. Some people also work overtime.
p3.a7: Not really. Long hours and commutes leave many people too tired to enjoy their weekends, which is why a cheap, easy day out is so valuable.

p3vocab.m: thời gian nghỉ; *eat out* = ăn ngoài.
tiêu xài hoang phí; *moderation* = sự điều độ.
phố đi bộ; *free festival* = lễ hội miễn phí.
sự ở một mình; *recharge* = nạp lại năng lượng.
đi lại đi làm; *valuable* = quý giá.

cards.title: A time when you organised a happy event successfully
points: who helped you to organise it
and explain why you think it was a successful event
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: sự kiện là tiệc sinh nhật bất ngờ cho mẹ (mẹ ở đề 14, 46) cùng em trai và bố. Bạn thay bằng sự kiện thật.

notes.v: surprise birthday party for my mother – 50th
list guests – ordered cake – decorated – cooked her favourite dishes – a week
younger brother, father, aunt (invited, hid, cooked)
mother surprised and cried – everyone happy – photos – on budget

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a happy event that I organised successfully. It was a surprise birthday party for my mother, for her fiftieth birthday.

I prepared for it for about a week. First, I made a list of guests, mostly our relatives and her close friends. Then I ordered a cake, bought some balloons and decorated the living room. On the day, we cooked her favourite dishes.

My younger brother and my father helped me a lot. My brother took my mother out for a walk while we decorated the house, and my aunt helped me to cook.

I think it was successful because my mother was very surprised and she cried with happiness. Everybody enjoyed the food, and we took many photos. Also, we didn't spend too much money. I felt very happy and proud.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a happy event I organised that went really well: a surprise party for my mother's fiftieth birthday.

I spent about a week preparing. I began by drawing up a guest list, mostly relatives and her close friends. Then I ordered a cake, bought balloons and decorated the living room. On the day itself, we cooked all her favourite dishes.

I had plenty of help. My younger brother took my mother out for a walk while we decorated, my father kept the secret, and my aunt lent a hand with the cooking.

I'd call it a success because my mother was completely taken by surprise and burst into tears of joy. Everybody loved the food, we took lots of photos, and we stayed within our budget. I felt happy and proud, and it taught me how rewarding it is to plan something for someone you love.
grammar: **Trình tự** → "I began by... Then... On the day itself..."
**while + mệnh đề** → "while we decorated."
**I'd call it + N** → cách đánh giá.
**how + adj + it is to + V** → "how rewarding it is to plan something."

p3.q: How would you feel when you were not well prepared for something?
p3.a6: I would feel nervous and worried, and I'd be afraid of making mistakes. But it can also teach me a lesson to prepare better next time.
p3.a7: Anxious and a bit panicky, as I'd be afraid of making mistakes. Still, it's a good lesson to plan more carefully next time.

p3.q: Do you prefer to prepare and organise an activity or just take part in an activity?
p3.a6: I prefer just taking part, because organising takes a lot of time and responsibility. But I'm happy to organise special events for my family.
p3.a7: Honestly, I'd rather take part, as organising demands a lot of time and responsibility. For something special, like my mother's party, though, I'm happy to take charge.

p3.q: How can parents help children to be organised?
p3.a6: Parents can teach children to make a daily plan and keep their things tidy. They should be a good example and praise children when they do it well.
p3.a7: By teaching them to plan their day, keep their belongings tidy and set routines, while leading by example and praising progress.

p3.q: On what occasions do people need to be organised?
p3.a6: When they have an exam, a job interview, a big meeting or a trip. They also need it for weddings and other big events.
p3.a7: For exams, job interviews, important meetings, trips and large events such as weddings, where many details could go wrong.

p3.q: Does everything need to be well prepared?
p3.a6: No, not everything. Important things need good preparation, but for small things we can be flexible. Sometimes unplanned things are more fun.
p3.a7: Not necessarily. High-stakes tasks need thorough preparation, but small everyday things can be spontaneous, and some of the best moments are unplanned.

p3.q: Do people need others' help when organising things?
p3.a6: Yes, I think so. One person can't do everything, so they should share the tasks. It also makes the event more fun, like my brother and aunt helped me.
p3.a7: Generally, yes. No one can handle everything alone, so delegating tasks saves time and reduces stress, as my family's help showed at my mother's party.

p3vocab.m: hoảng; *plan carefully* = lên kế hoạch kỹ.
đảm nhận; *demand* = đòi hỏi.
đồ đạc; *routine* = thói quen.
phỏng vấn xin việc; *go wrong* = hỏng.
quan trọng; *thorough* = kỹ lưỡng.
giao việc; *reduce stress* = giảm căng thẳng.

cards.title: A special cake you received from others
points: who you got the cake from
and explain why it's a special cake
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: chiếc bánh là bánh sinh nhật đồng nghiệp tặng bất ngờ ở công ty, có trang trí hình một con "bug" nhỏ (đùa nghề tester). Part 3 PDF có 3 câu, mình thêm 2 câu bonus. Bạn thay bằng chuyện thật.

notes.v: my birthday – last March – afternoon
meeting room at the office
my team – 10 colleagues – manager
surprise – little "bug" on cake – funny – first time at work – felt valued

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a special cake that I received from my colleagues on my birthday last March.

It happened at my office. In the afternoon, my manager asked me to come to the meeting room to discuss something about work. When I opened the door, all my team were inside, about ten people, and they were singing "Happy Birthday" with a cake in front of them.

The cake was a small chocolate cake. It was decorated with a tiny "bug" on top, because I'm a software tester. Everyone laughed when they saw it.

It's special to me for several reasons. First, it was a complete surprise. Second, the decoration was funny and it showed that they knew my job. Also, it was my first birthday cake at work. I felt valued and happy, and I got closer to my team.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a special cake I received from my colleagues on my birthday last March.

It happened at my office. That afternoon, my manager asked me to pop into the meeting room to discuss something work-related. When I opened the door, my whole team, about ten people, were standing there singing "Happy Birthday" around a cake.

It was a small chocolate cake, decorated with a tiny "bug" on top, a nod to the fact that I'm a software tester. Everybody burst out laughing when they saw my face.

It's special to me for a few reasons. For one thing, it was a total surprise. For another, the decoration was so thoughtful and funny, which showed that they knew me and my job well. And it was my first-ever birthday cake at work. I felt genuinely valued, and it brought me closer to my team.
