**decorated with + N** → cụm quá khứ phân từ.
**For one thing... For another...** → liệt kê.
**and it was my first-ever + N** → nhấn mạnh.

p3.q: What are the differences between the special food in Vietnam and foreign countries?
p3.a6: Vietnamese special food often uses rice, fresh herbs and fish sauce, and it's usually shared by the whole family. In western countries, special food is often turkey, cake or meat, and it's more about baking and roasting.
p3.a7: Vietnamese festive food tends to be rice-based, flavoured with fresh herbs and fish sauce and shared communally, whereas western special occasion dishes, such as roast turkey or baked cakes, rely more on roasting and baking.

p3.q: Do people usually cook special food in Vietnam?
p3.a6: Yes, many families cook special food at home for Tet and anniversaries because it has meaning. But now some people buy it because they are busy.
p3.a7: Many families still do for Tet and death anniversaries, because the cooking carries meaning. Busy city dwellers, though, increasingly buy ready-made dishes.

p3.q: Should special food be easily available?
p3.a6: I don't think so. If it is available every day, it won't feel special. But some food can be sold before festivals for people who don't have time to cook.
p3.a7: Not necessarily. If it's available all year round, it loses its special quality. Making it available around festivals, though, helps people who lack time to cook.

p3.q: Why do people give cakes or gifts on special occasions?
p3.a6: It's a way to show love and care. A gift also makes the person happy and makes the relationship stronger.
p3.a7: It's a gesture of affection that shows you care, makes the recipient feel valued and strengthens relationships.

p3.q: Do you think birthdays are important?
p3.a6: Yes, I think so, because it's a chance to be with family and friends. But I don't think we need an expensive party. A small, warm celebration is enough.
p3.a7: Yes, they're a chance to gather loved ones and feel appreciated, though a modest, heartfelt celebration is plenty. Expensive parties aren't necessary.

p3vocab.m: chung, cùng nhau; *rely on* = dựa vào.
mang ý nghĩa; *ready-made* = làm sẵn.
quanh năm; *lose its special quality* = mất tính đặc biệt.
cử chỉ yêu thương; *recipient* = người nhận.
chân thành; *modest* = giản dị.

cards.title: A thing you did to learn another language
points: how it helped you learn the language
and how you feel about it
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: bạn học tiếng Anh bằng cách nghe podcast và xem YouTube có phụ đề tiếng Anh trên xe bus mỗi ngày (hợp với hoàn cảnh đi bus 1 tiếng). Part 3 PDF có 2 câu, mình thêm 3 câu bonus. Bạn thay bằng cách học thật của mình.

notes.v: English
listened to podcasts and YouTube with English subtitles – on the bus – 1 hour a day – 6 months
listening better – new words – used time on the bus – get used to accents
proud – habit – still slow progress – want to speak more

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about something I did to learn English. I started listening to English podcasts and watching English videos on the bus every day.

It takes me about one hour to get to work, so I used the time on the bus. I put on my headphones and listened to short podcasts for learners. Then I watched videos on YouTube with English subtitles. When I heard a new word, I wrote it down in my phone notes. I did this for six months.

It helped me in several ways. My listening is better, and I can understand more words. I also got used to different accents. And I don't waste time on the bus anymore.

I feel proud of myself, because I kept this habit for a long time. But my speaking is still weak, so I want to practise speaking more.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about something I did to learn English: I started listening to English podcasts and watching English videos on the bus every day.

My commute takes about an hour, so I decided to make use of that time. I'd put on my headphones and listen to short podcasts for learners, then watch YouTube videos with English subtitles. Whenever I heard a new word, I jotted it down in my phone notes. I kept this up for six months.

It helped in a number of ways. My listening improved noticeably, my vocabulary grew, and I got used to different accents. Best of all, I stopped wasting time on the bus.

I'm quite proud of myself for sticking to the habit. That said, my speaking still lags behind, so my next step is to practise speaking aloud much more.
grammar: **would + V (thói quen quá khứ)** → "I'd put on my headphones."
**Whenever + S + V** → "Whenever I heard a new word."
**get used to + N/V-ing** → "got used to different accents."
**Best of all,...** → nhấn mạnh lợi ích.

p3.q: What difficulties do people face when learning a language?
p3.a6: Many people don't have time, and they feel shy about speaking. Pronunciation and grammar are also difficult, and some people lose motivation because they don't see fast progress.
p3.a7: Lack of time, fear of making mistakes when speaking, tricky pronunciation and grammar, and the slow pace of progress, which can sap motivation.

p3.q: Do you think language learning is important? Why?
p3.a6: Yes, very important. A language helps us find better jobs, travel and understand other cultures. English especially is important in IT, where much information is in English.
p3.a7: Very. It opens up career opportunities, makes travel easier and deepens understanding of other cultures. English in particular is essential in IT, where most resources are in English.

p3.q: What is the best way to learn a foreign language?
p3.a6: I think the best way is to practise every day, even for a short time. We should listen, speak and read. Using the language with real people is also very helpful.
p3.a7: Consistency is key: a little every day beats cramming. A good mix of listening, speaking, reading and writing, plus real conversation, works best.

p3.q: Is it better to learn a language in a class or by yourself?
p3.a6: A class is good because a teacher gives feedback and a plan. Learning by yourself is flexible and cheaper. For me, a mix is best.
p3.a7: Classes offer structure and feedback, while self-study is flexible and cheaper. A blend of both suits most working adults, including me.

p3.q: How has technology changed language learning?
p3.a6: Now we have apps, online classes and videos, so we can learn anywhere. It's cheaper and more convenient. But we need self-discipline.
p3.a7: Apps, online classes and AI tools have made learning accessible anytime, anywhere, and cheaper, though they demand self-discipline.

p3vocab.m: làm hao mòn động lực; *tricky* = khó nhằn.
mở ra cơ hội; *resources* = tài liệu.
sự đều đặn; *cramming* = học nhồi.
khung chương trình; *feedback* = phản hồi.
tự kỷ luật; *accessible* = dễ tiếp cận.

cards.title: A place you would like to visit in your free time
points: how long you will stay there
and explain why you would like to visit it
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: nơi bạn muốn đến là Huế (Cố đô), dự định ở 4 ngày, ăn bún bò Huế, tham quan Đại Nội. Bạn thay bằng nơi thật. Đề này có bốn câu Part 3 khá "lạ" (du lịch có kế hoạch, du lịch di tích, tiếng ồn ở thành phố du lịch), mình trả lời đủ cả 4.

notes.v: Hue – central Vietnam – ancient capital
Imperial Citadel – royal tombs – boat on Perfume River – bun bo Hue
4 days – long weekend / holiday – by train
history – culture – food – peaceful, slow – never been

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a place that I would like to visit in my free time, which is Hue. It's a city in central Vietnam, and it was the ancient capital of the country.

If I go there, I will visit the Imperial Citadel and some royal tombs. I will also take a boat trip on the Perfume River. Of course, I want to try the local food, especially bun bo Hue, and also some small cakes.

I plan to stay for four days. I'd like to go during a long holiday, and I think I will travel there by train.

I want to go for several reasons. First, I love history and culture, and I've never been there. Second, the city is quiet and slow, which is very different from Hanoi. I think it will be a good way to relax and learn something new.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a place I'm keen to visit in my free time: Hue, a city in central Vietnam that used to be the country's imperial capital.

If I get the chance, I'll explore the Imperial Citadel and a few of the royal tombs, and I'll take a boat trip along the Perfume River. I'm also looking forward to the food, particularly bun bo Hue and the local sweets.

I'm planning to stay for four days, ideally over a long holiday, and I'd probably go by train.

There are a couple of reasons I'm drawn to it. For one thing, I'm interested in history and culture, and I've never been there. For another, Hue has a calm, unhurried atmosphere, which is a world away from Hanoi's hustle and bustle. I think it would be the perfect way to unwind and learn something new at the same time.
grammar: **Điều kiện loại 1** → "If I get the chance, I'll explore..."
**be planning to + V** → kế hoạch.
**I'd probably + V** → khả năng.
**used to be** → "used to be the imperial capital."

p3.q: Do people prefer planned travel?
p3.a6: Many people prefer planning because it saves time and money. They can book hotels and tickets early at lower prices. But some young people like unplanned travel because it's free and exciting.
p3.a7: Many do, as planning saves time and money, with early bookings often cheaper. Some adventurous young travellers prefer spontaneity, though, enjoying the freedom to go with the flow.

p3.q: Why do places with historical attractions develop tourism more aggressively?
p3.a6: Because history attracts many visitors, both local and foreign, so these places earn a lot of money from tourism. The government and local people want to protect and promote them, so they invest more.
p3.a7: Because historical sites are a ready-made draw for tourists, so they generate substantial income. Authorities and locals therefore invest heavily in promoting and preserving them.

p3.q: Why do you think people usually travel?
p3.a6: To relax and escape from work, to see new places and learn about other cultures, and to spend time with family and friends.
p3.a7: To unwind, to broaden their horizons through new places and cultures, and to spend quality time with loved ones.

p3.q: Why does living in tourist cities experience more noise?
p3.a6: There are many visitors, vehicles, restaurants, bars and street performers. Many places are busy day and night, so local people hear noise all the time.
p3.a7: Tourist hotspots are packed with visitors, traffic, bars and street entertainment, often running late into the night, so residents get little peace.

p3vocab.m: tùy hứng; *spontaneity* = sự ngẫu hứng.
điểm thu hút sẵn có; *preserve* = bảo tồn.
thời gian chất lượng; *broaden one's horizons* = mở rộng tầm nhìn.
điểm nóng; *get little peace* = ít được yên tĩnh.

cards.title: Describe a person who works in a successful company
points: and explain why you think the company is successful
cards.note: Lưu ý quan trọng: trong PDF, đề này mất toàn bộ phần gợi ý cue card và Part 3 trùng nguyên văn đề 45 (family business). Mình:

notes.v: Dung – university friend – developer
big software company – Hanoi – 2,000 staff
software for banks and foreign clients
good products – talented staff – good benefits – training – clients trust

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about my friend Dung, who works in a successful company. He's a friend from university, and now he's a software developer.

He works for a big software company in Hanoi. It has about two thousand employees. The company makes software for banks and also for foreign clients.

I think the company is successful for several reasons. First, it has good products, and clients trust it. Second, it has many talented staff, and the company gives them training and a good working environment. Dung says the salary is good and that there are many chances to learn and be promoted.

I sometimes feel a little jealous of him, but he also works very hard and often works late. I'd like to learn from his company and maybe work in a big company like that in the future.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about my friend Dung, who works for a very successful company. We were at university together, and he's now a software developer.

He works for a large software company in Hanoi with around two thousand employees. It develops software for banks and for foreign clients.

I think it's successful for a few reasons. For one thing, its products are reliable, so clients keep coming back. For another, it attracts talented people and invests in them through training and a supportive working environment. Dung tells me the pay is good and there are plenty of opportunities for promotion.

I'll admit I'm a little envious sometimes, but I also know he works incredibly hard and often stays late. I'd like to learn from that company's approach, and perhaps work for a big firm like that one day.
grammar: **Mệnh đề quan hệ "who"** → "my friend Dung, **who** works for..."
**For one thing... For another...** → liệt kê lý do.
**I'll admit (that)...** → mở đầu nhượng bộ.
**work + adv** → "works incredibly hard."

p3.q: What makes a company successful?
p3.a6: Good products or services, a clear plan and good leaders. It also needs good staff who work together. Customer trust is also important.
p3.a7: Quality products, strong leadership, a clear strategy and motivated staff, along with the ability to earn and keep customer trust.

p3.q: Do people prefer working in big companies or small companies?
p3.a6: Big companies are stable and give better pay and training. Small companies give more freedom and a friendly environment. Young people may prefer small companies to learn fast, like in my first job.
p3.a7: Big firms offer stability, higher pay and structured training, while small ones offer flexibility, a closer team and broader responsibilities. I started in a small company, which taught me a lot quickly.

p3.q: What do employees want from their employers?
p3.a6: A good salary, a safe and friendly workplace, chances to grow and respect. Many also want flexible working time.
p3.a7: A fair salary, job security, opportunities to grow, respect and, increasingly, flexible working hours and a good work-life balance.

p3.q: Are salary and job satisfaction equally important?
p3.a6: Both are important. Money is necessary for life, but if you don't like your job, you will feel unhappy. In the long term, I think satisfaction is more important.
p3.a7: Both matter, but while a decent salary meets basic needs, satisfaction sustains you in the long run, so I'd weigh job satisfaction slightly more.

p3vocab.m: chiến lược; *motivated* = có động lực.
đào tạo bài bản; *broader responsibilities* = trách nhiệm đa dạng.
sự ổn định; *work-life balance* = cân bằng công việc - cuộc sống.
duy trì; *weigh* = cân nhắc.

cards.title: An important river/lake in your country
points: and explain why it is important
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: bạn chọn sông Hồng (Red River) chảy qua Hà Nội, với các cầu Long Biên, Chương Dương, Nhật Tân. Mình nói ở mức chung (không đưa số km chính xác); nếu muốn nói số liệu bạn nên tự kiểm tra. Bạn cũng có thể chọn Hồ Tây (đã dùng ở đề 19).

notes.v: Red River – northern Vietnam – through Hanoi
very long – flows from China to the sea – wide in Hanoi
brown/red water (silt) – bridges – sandbanks – farmland on bank
water for farming – fertile delta – transport – history – bridges, culture

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about the Red River, which is one of the most important rivers in Vietnam. It's in the north of the country, and it flows through Hanoi.

It's a very long river. It starts in China, passes through the northern provinces and goes to the sea. In Hanoi, it's very wide.

The water has a brown-red colour because it carries a lot of mud, and that is why it's called the Red River. There are many big bridges over it, like Long Bien Bridge, and there are farms and green fields along the banks.

I think it's important for several reasons. It provides water for farming, and the land around it is very fertile, so it's a big rice-growing area. Boats also use it to carry goods. Also, Hanoi's history and culture are closely connected with this river.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about the Red River, one of the most important rivers in Vietnam. It's in the north of the country and flows right through Hanoi.

It's a very long river that rises in China, winds through the northern provinces and eventually empties into the sea. By the time it reaches Hanoi, it's remarkably wide.

Its water has a reddish-brown tint because of the silt it carries, hence its name. Several major bridges span it, including the historic Long Bien Bridge, and farmland and greenery line its banks.

It matters for a number of reasons. It supplies water for irrigation, and its fertile floodplain is a major rice-growing region. It's also used to transport goods by boat. Beyond that, the history and culture of Hanoi are closely bound up with the river, which makes it a part of our national identity.
grammar: **Mệnh đề quan hệ** → "the silt **it** carries."
**by the time + mệnh đề** → "By the time it reaches Hanoi."
**hence + N** → "hence its name."
**It matters for a number of reasons** → mẫu giải thích.

p3.q: What are the popular water sports in your country?
p3.a6: Swimming is the most popular, and also boating and kayaking. In the sea, people like surfing and diving. But water sports are not as popular as football.
p3.a7: Swimming is the most common, followed by kayaking, paddleboarding and, along the coast, surfing and diving, although they're still less popular than football.

p3.q: Are rivers and lakes important to a country?
p3.a6: Yes, very important. They give us water for drinking and farming, and fish for food. They also make the air cooler and are good places for relaxing.
p3.a7: Absolutely. They supply drinking water and irrigation, support fisheries, regulate the local climate and provide space for recreation.

p3.q: How can rivers and lakes benefit local people?
p3.a6: They provide jobs in fishing, farming and tourism. They also provide water for daily life and places to relax, like walking around West Lake.
p3.a7: By providing livelihoods in fishing, farming and tourism, as well as fresh water and green spaces where people can unwind, such as West Lake.

p3.q: Do you think rivers and lakes attract tourists?
p3.a6: Yes, they do. Many tourists like taking boat trips, enjoying the view and eating near the water. For example, many visitors go to Hoan Kiem Lake and Ha Long Bay.
p3.a7: Definitely. Scenic water bodies draw visitors for boat trips, waterside dining and views, as Hoan Kiem Lake and Ha Long Bay do.

p3.q: How do rivers and lakes affect local tourism?
p3.a6: They bring many visitors, so hotels, restaurants and shops develop. But too many tourists can cause rubbish and pollution, so local people must protect them.
p3.a7: They bring visitors who support local hotels, restaurants and shops, though overcrowding can lead to litter and pollution, so protection is essential.

p3.q: Are rivers and lakes good for transport? Why?
p3.a6: Yes, especially in the south, where boats carry people and goods. It's cheap and can carry a lot. But it's slow, so it's not good for people in a hurry.
p3.a7: Yes, for bulky goods in particular: waterways are cheap and can carry heavy loads, as in the Mekong Delta, though they're slower than roads or rail.

p3vocab.m: chèo ván đứng; *along the coast* = dọc bờ biển.
nghề cá; *recreation* = giải trí.
sinh kế; *green space* = không gian xanh.
đẹp như tranh; *waterside* = ven nước.
rác thải; *overcrowding* = quá tải.
đường thủy; *bulky goods* = hàng cồng kềnh.

cards.title: A home that you like to visit but do not want to live in
points: why you like to visit it
and explain why you would not like to live there
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: ngôi nhà là nhà của bà ở quê (Thanh Hóa) (nối đề 18, 29): bạn thích về thăm nhưng không muốn sống ở đó vì xa, thiếu tiện nghi. Đề 66 cùng kiểu nhưng là nhà của bạn bè, mình dùng chuyện khác để bạn có hai lựa chọn. Bạn thay bằng chuyện thật.

notes.v: grandmother's village – Thanh Hoa – 4 hours from Hanoi
old brick house – tiled roof – big yard – garden – well – wooden furniture
grandmother's cooking – fresh air – quiet – family gathering at Tet
far from work – poor internet – few shops, hospitals – hot in summer – boring for young

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about my grandmother's house in a village in Thanh Hoa, which I love visiting but wouldn't want to live in.

It's an old brick house with a tiled roof. It has a big yard with a garden, a small well and some fruit trees. Inside, there's a lot of old wooden furniture.

I like to visit it for several reasons. First, I love my grandmother's cooking. Second, the air is fresh and the village is very quiet, so I feel relaxed. Also, my whole family gathers there at Tet, and we have a great time together.

But I wouldn't like to live there. It's too far from my workplace, and the internet is slow. There are few shops and no big hospital nearby. It's also very hot in summer, and I think life there would be boring for a young person like me.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about my grandmother's house in a village in Thanh Hoa, a place I love visiting but couldn't see myself living in.

It's an old brick house with a tiled roof, set in a large yard with a garden, a small well and a few fruit trees. Inside, there's plenty of antique wooden furniture.

I love visiting for several reasons. For one thing, my grandmother's home cooking is unbeatable. For another, the air is fresh and the village is wonderfully peaceful, so I unwind instantly. And at Tet, the whole family gathers there, which makes it extra special.

That said, I wouldn't want to live there. It's too far from my workplace, the internet is patchy, and there are few shops and no major hospital nearby. It's also sweltering in summer, and I think a young person like me would soon find the quiet life rather dull.
grammar: **wouldn't want to + V** → từ chối nhẹ nhàng.
**set in + N** → "set in a large yard."
**That said,...** → nhượng bộ.
**find + O + adj** → "find the quiet life dull."

p3.q: What are the differences between houses or buildings in the city and in the countryside?
p3.a6: In the city, there are many apartments and tall buildings because land is expensive. In the countryside, houses are usually bigger and have a yard or garden. Rural houses are often built in a traditional style.
p3.a7: City dwellings are mostly apartments or narrow tall houses, as space is limited and expensive. Rural homes are typically spacious, with yards and gardens, and often follow traditional styles.

p3.q: Do you prefer to live in the city or in the countryside?
p3.a6: I prefer the city because there are more jobs, services and entertainment. But I like the countryside for holidays. Living in the suburbs, like me, is a good balance.
p3.a7: The city, for jobs, services and entertainment, though I love the countryside for short breaks. Living on the outskirts, as I do, is a good compromise.

p3.q: What safety risks are there in residential buildings in cities?
p3.a6: Fire is the biggest risk, especially in tall apartment buildings and small houses with narrow alleys. There are also risks of crime and broken lifts.
p3.a7: Fire is the main danger, particularly in high-rise blocks and narrow alley houses where escape routes are limited. Break-ins and faulty lifts are other concerns.

p3.q: Is it expensive to decorate a house or an apartment in the place where you live?
p3.a6: It can be, if you want good furniture and a nice design. But if you choose carefully and do some work yourself, you can save money.
p3.a7: It can be, if you go for quality furniture and professional design, but with careful choices and a bit of DIY you can keep costs down.

p3vocab.m: nơi ở; *spacious* = rộng rãi.
ngoại ô; *compromise* = sự dung hòa.
lối thoát hiểm; *break-in* = trộm đột nhập.
tự làm; *keep costs down* = giữ chi phí thấp.

cards.title: An environmental law you would like your country to introduce
points: why people should follow the law
whether the law will be popular
and explain how you feel about this law
cards.note: Lưu ý quan trọng: Part 3 của đề này trong PDF lại là 3 câu y hệt đề 38 và 51 (chụp ảnh khi du lịch...), rõ ràng chép nhầm. Những câu đó đã trả lời ở file đề 38. Ở đây mình viết 5 câu Part 3 về môi trường bám sát đề. Đề 33 (luật môi trường hiện có) và 51 (luật mới) có phần gần giống nên bạn có thể tái sử dụng ý.

notes.v: reduce single-use plastic in food delivery – cutlery only on request – charge for plastic bags
too much plastic waste – pollutes rivers, sea – harms animals – health
many young people support – shops/customers worry about cost – need time
hopeful – small habit – big effect – need clear rules and checking

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about an environmental law that I would like my country to introduce. It's a law to reduce single-use plastic in food delivery. For example, restaurants must give plastic bags, spoons and chopsticks only when customers ask for them, and they have to charge a small fee for plastic bags.

I think people should follow this law because we use too much plastic. Every day I order food, and I see that every meal comes with many plastic items. Plastic pollutes rivers and the sea and harms animals.

I think the law will be quite popular among young people, because many of them care about the environment. But some shops may complain about the cost, so it will take time.

I feel hopeful about this law, because it's a small change in our habits, but it can have a big effect.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about an environmental law I'd love to see introduced: one that cuts down on single-use plastic in food delivery. Under it, restaurants would provide plastic bags, spoons and chopsticks only on request, and would charge a small fee for plastic bags.

People should follow it because we use far too much plastic. I order food regularly, and every meal arrives with a pile of plastic items. All that waste ends up polluting rivers and the sea and harming wildlife.

I think it would be fairly popular among young people, many of whom care about the environment, although some shops might object to the extra cost, so it would take time to win everyone over.

I feel optimistic about it. It asks us to change a small habit, but the cumulative effect could be huge, provided the rules are clear and properly enforced.

vocab.m: gây hại động vật hoang dã

grammar: **Under it, S + would + V** → mô tả luật giả định.
**many of whom** → mệnh đề quan hệ có lượng từ.
**although + mệnh đề** → "although some shops might object."
**provided (that)** → điều kiện.

p3.q: What are the most serious environmental problems in your country?
p3.a6: Air pollution in big cities, plastic waste and flooding are serious. Water pollution in rivers is also a problem.
p3.a7: Air pollution in major cities, plastic waste, polluted rivers and flooding, which is made worse by rapid urbanisation.

p3.q: Who is most responsible for protecting the environment?
p3.a6: I think everyone is, but companies and the government have a bigger role because they make big decisions. Individuals can help by changing small habits.
p3.a7: Everyone shares responsibility, but governments and large corporations bear the most, since their decisions have the biggest impact. Individuals can still make a difference through everyday habits.

p3.q: Do you think people's habits can be changed by laws?
p3.a6: Yes, if the law is clear and the punishment is fair. For example, rules about wearing a helmet have changed people's habits. But people also need education.
p3.a7: Yes, when laws are clear and enforced, as helmet rules showed. But lasting change also needs education, so that people understand why.

p3.q: What can schools do to teach children about the environment?
p3.a6: Schools can teach about recycling, organise tree-planting days and clean-up activities, and have waste-sorting bins. Children learn better by doing than listening.
p3.a7: They can build environmental topics into lessons, run tree-planting and clean-up days and set up waste-sorting bins, because children learn better by doing.

p3.q: Will technology help solve environmental problems?
p3.a6: I think yes. Electric vehicles, solar energy and recycling technology can help. But technology alone isn't enough; people must change behaviour too.
p3.a7: To a large extent. Electric vehicles, solar power and better recycling can all reduce harm, but technology alone won't suffice without a change in behaviour.

p3vocab.m: đô thị hóa; *flooding* = ngập lụt.
tập đoàn; *bear responsibility* = chịu trách nhiệm.
thay đổi bền vững; *helmet* = mũ bảo hiểm.
ngày dọn dẹp; *by doing* = bằng thực hành.
năng lượng mặt trời; *suffice* = đủ.

cards.title: A piece of local news that people are interested in
points: and explain why people were interested in it
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: tin tức là tin về một tuyến metro mới ở Hà Nội đi vào hoạt động/chạy thử, mọi người rất quan tâm vì chờ đợi nhiều năm (mình nói chung, không nêu tên tuyến hay ngày cụ thể; bạn thay bằng tin thật bạn biết). Part 3 PDF có 4 câu.

notes.v: new metro line in Hanoi – opened / trial run
Facebook + TV news at home + colleagues talk
city government, metro company, passengers, journalists
traffic jams – convenient – cheap – first modern transport – curious to try

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a piece of local news that many people in Hanoi were interested in. It was about a new metro line.

I first saw it on Facebook, and then I watched it on the TV news at home. My colleagues also talked about it at lunch.

The people involved were the city government, the company that runs the metro, and many passengers. Journalists also reported from the stations, and many people went to try the new trains.

I think people were interested for several reasons. First, Hanoi has serious traffic jams, so people hope that the metro will help. Second, it's modern, convenient and cheap. It is also one of the first modern kinds of public transport in the city, so people were curious. I also wanted to try it, and I hope that there will be a line near my home in the future.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a piece of local news that generated a lot of interest in Hanoi: the news about a new metro line.

I first saw it on Facebook and then watched it on the evening TV news. My colleagues were also buzzing about it over lunch.

The main parties involved were the city authorities, the company operating the metro and, of course, the passengers. Journalists were reporting live from the stations, and crowds of people turned up to try the new trains.

People were so interested for a few reasons. For one thing, Hanoi suffers from terrible traffic congestion, so there's real hope that the metro will ease it. For another, it's modern, convenient and affordable, and it's one of the city's first modern public transport systems, so people were curious. I'm keen to try it myself, and I'm hoping a line will eventually reach my part of town.
grammar: **Bị động** → "it was reported..."
**Quá khứ tiếp diễn** → "Journalists were reporting live."
**so + adj + for + lý do** → "so interested for a few reasons."
**I'm hoping + mệnh đề** → hy vọng hiện tại.

p3.q: How do people usually get local news nowadays?
p3.a6: Most people use their phones. They read news on Facebook, Zalo and news apps. Some people also watch TV or hear it from friends and family.
p3.a7: Mostly through smartphones: social media, Zalo groups and news apps, though older people still rely on TV and word of mouth.

p3.q: Do you think local news is more important than international news? Why?
p3.a6: For daily life, I think local news is more important because it affects us directly, like traffic, weather and prices. But international news is also useful to understand the world.
p3.a7: For daily life, yes, since it affects us directly: traffic, weather and prices. International news matters too, particularly for business and a broader understanding.

p3.q: Why are some news stories more popular than others?
p3.a6: Stories that affect people's lives, like prices or safety, are popular. Strange or emotional stories and stories about famous people are also popular. Short, easy stories with a good headline are shared more.
p3.a7: Stories that touch people's lives, such as prices and safety, or that are emotional, surprising or about celebrities, spread fastest, particularly with a catchy headline.

p3.q: Do social media affect the way people receive news?
p3.a6: Yes, a lot. News spreads very fast, and people can comment and share. But there is also a lot of fake news, so people must check the information.
p3.a7: Enormously. News spreads in seconds and people can comment and share, but misinformation spreads just as fast, so verifying sources is vital.

p3vocab.m: truyền miệng; *news app* = ứng dụng tin tức.
ảnh hưởng trực tiếp; *broader understanding* = hiểu biết rộng hơn.
tiêu đề; *spread* = lan truyền.
kiểm chứng; *fake news* = tin giả.

cards.title: A time when you got up early
points: and how you felt about it
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: bạn dậy lúc 4 giờ 30 sáng để bắt xe khách về quê Thanh Hóa dự giỗ ông/bà (nối đề 29, 62). Bạn thay bằng chuyện thật (dậy sớm đi thi, ngắm bình minh...).

notes.v: last winter – 4:30 a.m. – Saturday – cold and dark
washed face – packed bag – walked to bus stop – coach to Thanh Hoa
avoid traffic – family death anniversary at 11 – help cook
sleepy, cold – then proud, happy – arrived early, helped grandmother

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about a time when I got up very early. It was last winter, on a Saturday, at half past four in the morning. It was cold and still dark outside.

First, I washed my face, had a quick breakfast and packed my bag. Then I walked to the bus stop and took a coach to my grandmother's village in Thanh Hoa.

I got up early for two reasons. First, I wanted to avoid the traffic, because the road is usually crowded later in the day. Second, my family was having a death anniversary at eleven o'clock, and I wanted to arrive early to help my grandmother cook.

At first, I felt sleepy and cold, and it wasn't easy to get out of bed. But when I arrived early and helped my grandmother in the kitchen, I felt happy and proud. It was a good start to the day.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about a time when I got up really early. It was last winter, on a Saturday, at half past four in the morning, when it was still cold and pitch dark.

I splashed some water on my face, had a quick bite, packed my bag and walked to the bus stop to catch a coach to my grandmother's village in Thanh Hoa.

There were two reasons for the early start. For one thing, I wanted to beat the traffic, as the road gets jammed later in the day. For another, the family was holding a death anniversary at eleven, and I wanted to get there in time to help my grandmother with the cooking.

I felt groggy and chilled at first, and dragging myself out of bed was a struggle. But once I arrived early and lent a hand in the kitchen, I felt happy and proud. It was a great way to start the day.
grammar: **for one thing... for another...** → lý do.
**to + V chỉ mục đích** → "to catch a coach."
**once + mệnh đề** → "once I arrived early..."
**get there in time to + V** → "in time to help."

p3.q: Is it good to arrive early in any situation?
p3.a6: Usually yes, because we don't feel stressed and can prepare better, like for exams or interviews. But for a party, arriving too early can be uncomfortable for the host.
p3.a7: Generally, yes, since it reduces stress and leaves time to prepare, for instance for interviews. For social events, however, arriving too early can inconvenience the host.

p3.q: Do you know anyone who likes to get up early?
p3.a6: Yes, my father. He gets up at five every day, does exercise and drinks tea. He says the morning is the most peaceful time.
p3.a7: Yes, my father. He's up at five every day for some exercise and a cup of tea, and he swears the morning is the most peaceful part of the day.

p3.q: Why do people get up early?
p3.a6: Some have to because of work, school or a long commute. Others want to exercise, study or enjoy a quiet time before the day gets busy.
p3.a7: Some have no choice because of work, school or a long commute; others choose to, in order to exercise, study or enjoy some peace before the day gets hectic.

p3.q: What kinds of occasions need people to arrive early?
p3.a6: Exams, job interviews, flights, important meetings and weddings. In these situations, being late can cause serious problems.
p3.a7: Exams, job interviews, flights, key meetings and weddings: occasions where being late could have serious consequences.

p3.q: Why do some people like to stay up late?
p3.a6: Some people feel more creative or have more free time at night. Others like to watch videos or play games, which I do too, but it's not healthy.
p3.a7: Some feel more creative at night or only get free time then; others stay up scrolling or gaming, which I'm guilty of too, although it's unhealthy.

p3.q: What kind of people like getting up early?
p3.a6: Usually disciplined and organised people, and people with busy jobs. Older people also often wake up early naturally.
p3.a7: Typically disciplined, organised people with busy schedules, along with older people, who naturally tend to wake earlier.

p3vocab.m: gây bất tiện; *host* = chủ nhà.
quả quyết; *peaceful* = yên bình.
không có lựa chọn; *hectic* = bận rộn.
hậu quả; *key meeting* = cuộc họp quan trọng.
có lỗi là; *unhealthy* = không lành mạnh.
có kỷ luật; *schedule* = lịch trình.

cards.title: Describe a friend's home you visited and liked but didn't want to live there
points: when and why you visited it
and explain why you didn't want to live there
cards.note: Thông tin giả định: nhà của bạn là nhà bạn Nam (đề 35) ở vùng ngoại ô: nhà rộng 3 tầng, có sân vườn, yên tĩnh, nhưng bạn không muốn ở vì quá xa trung tâm và rộng quá khó dọn dẹp. Khác với đề 62 (nhà bà ở quê). Part 3 PDF có 10 câu, mình trả lời gọn từng câu. Bạn thay bằng chuyện thật.

notes.v: my friend Nam – university friend
last month – class reunion – housewarming/ gathering
big three-storey house – outskirts – garden – big kitchen – balcony
spacious – quiet – green – big kitchen – cosy
too far – too big to clean – need a car – lonely

cards.a6:
I'd like to talk about my friend Nam's house, which I visited and liked, but I don't want to live there.

I visited it last month. Nam held a small class reunion at his house, so I went there with some other friends.

It's a large three-storey house on the outskirts of Hanoi. There's a garden in front, a big kitchen and a nice balcony on the second floor. It has a lot of space and plenty of light.

I liked it because it's spacious, green and very quiet. The air is fresh, and I felt relaxed there. The big kitchen was perfect for cooking together.

But I wouldn't like to live there. First, it's too far from the city centre and from my workplace. Second, the house is too big, so it would take a long time to clean. And I think I would feel lonely in such a quiet area.
cards.a7:
I'd like to talk about my friend Nam's house, which I visited and really liked but wouldn't want to live in.

I went there last month when Nam hosted a small class reunion, so I came along with a few other friends.

It's a spacious three-storey house on the outskirts of Hanoi, with a garden at the front, a huge kitchen and a lovely balcony on the second floor. It's bright and airy throughout.

What I liked was how roomy, green and peaceful it was. The air was fresh, I felt completely relaxed and the big kitchen was perfect for cooking together.

That said, I couldn't see myself living there. For one thing, it's too far from the city centre and my workplace. For another, it's so big that cleaning it would be a chore. And I suspect the quiet would start to feel lonely after a while.
grammar: **which + I visited** → mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định.
**wouldn't want to + V** → không muốn.
**so + adj + that** → "so big that cleaning it would be a chore."
**Điều kiện loại 2** → "it would take a long time."

p3.q: What kind of homes do people usually prefer to live in?
p3.a6: Most people prefer a house of their own with enough space, a quiet area and good services nearby. In cities, many people live in apartments because they're cheaper and safer.
p3.a7: A comfortable home with enough space, a quiet neighbourhood and good amenities nearby. In cities, many settle for apartments for affordability and security.

p3.q: Why do some people prefer living in houses rather than apartments?
p3.a6: Houses have more space and privacy, and you can have a garden or a pet. You don't share walls with neighbours, and you can change the house as you like.
p3.a7: Houses offer more space, privacy and freedom to renovate, plus room for a garden or pets and fewer neighbour-related noise problems.

p3.q: What are the advantages of living in a large house?
p3.a6: There's space for the whole family and for guests. Everyone has their own room, and there's space for hobbies. It's also good for family gatherings.
p3.a7: There's room for the whole family and guests, each person can have private space and it's ideal for gatherings and hobbies.

p3.q: Do you think people need a lot of space in their homes?
p3.a6: Not always. A small but well-designed home can be enough. A big house costs more money and takes a lot of time to clean. Some people just need comfort.
p3.a7: Not necessarily. A small, well-designed home can be perfectly adequate, whereas a large one means higher costs and more upkeep.

p3.q: What makes a home comfortable and pleasant to live in?
p3.a6: Good light and fresh air, a clean and tidy space, comfortable furniture and a quiet neighbourhood. Also, living with people you love is important.
p3.a7: Natural light, good ventilation, a tidy space, comfortable furniture and a peaceful neighbourhood, but above all, the people you share it with.

p3.q: Why do some people like visiting other people's homes?
p3.a6: They can get new ideas for decoration and see how others live. It's also a good way to get closer to friends and family, and they often enjoy home-made food.
p3.a7: To pick up decorating ideas, get a glimpse of how others live and strengthen friendships, not to mention enjoying home cooking.

p3.q: Do you think people's homes reflect their personalities?
p3.a6: Yes, I think so. A tidy home may show an organised person, and a home with many books may show a person who loves reading. Colours and decoration also show a person's style.
p3.a7: To a large extent. A tidy home suggests an organised person and shelves of books a keen reader, and colours and décor reveal personal taste.

p3.q: What factors should people consider when choosing a place to live?
p3.a6: Price, location, distance to work, safety and nearby services like schools, hospitals and shops. Noise and air quality are also important.
p3.a7: Budget, location and commuting distance, safety, nearby schools, hospitals and shops, and environmental factors such as noise and air quality.

p3.q: Is it better to live in the city or in the countryside?
p3.a6: It depends on the person. The city has more jobs and services, but it's noisy and polluted. The countryside is peaceful but has fewer chances. For me, the suburbs are a balance.
p3.a7: It depends on priorities. Cities offer jobs and services but also noise and pollution; the countryside is peaceful but has fewer opportunities. The suburbs, for me, strike a balance.

p3.q: Do you think people's preferences for homes change as they get older?
p3.a6: Yes. Young people like city centres and apartments for convenience and fun. As they get older and have families, they want bigger homes in quiet areas. Elderly people prefer homes near hospitals.
p3.a7: Definitely. Young people favour central apartments for convenience; families want more space and quieter areas; the elderly prioritise accessibility and proximity to healthcare.

p3vocab.m: tiện ích; *settle for* = chấp nhận.
sự riêng tư; *renovate* = cải tạo.
buổi tụ họp; *private space* = không gian riêng.
đủ dùng; *upkeep* = chi phí bảo trì.
thông gió; *neighbourhood* = khu phố.
nhìn thoáng qua; *not to mention* = chưa kể.
phản ánh tính cách; *décor* = đồ trang trí.
khoảng cách đi làm; *environmental factors* = yếu tố môi trường.
cân bằng; *priority* = ưu tiên.
gần với; *accessibility* = dễ đi lại.
